records.arabic: أبو عامر الهوذني مشهور بكنيته يقال رأى ويقال ذكره بن سميع في رجال حمص ممن أدرك الجاهلية وذكره أبو زرعة الدمشقي في الطبقة العليا التي تلي الصحابة فقال انه من أصحاب أبي عبيدة وقال البخاري في تاريخه سمع بلالا قلت وروى أيضا عن معاذ بن جبل والمقدام بن معد يكرب وعبد الله بن قرط ومعاوية وشهد خطبة عمر بالجابية روى عنه ابنه أبو اليمان عامر وأزهر بن عبد الله الحرازي وأبو سلام الأسود وغيرهم وقال أبو زرعة الرازي والدارقطني أبو عامر الهوزني لا باس بن ذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين قال العجلي شامي تابعي ثقة من كبار التابعين
records.english: Abu Amir al-Hawdhani, known by his kunya. It is said that he saw the Prophet. Ibn Sumayʿ mentioned him among the men of Homs who lived through the pre-Islamic period. Abu Zurʿa al-Dimashqi included him in the senior generation following the Companions and said that he was among the companions of Abu ʿUbayda. Al-Bukhari said in his History that he heard Bilal. I say: He also transmitted from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, al-Miqdam ibn Maʿdi Karib, ʿAbd Allah ibn Qurt, and Muʿawiya, and he was present at ʿUmar’s sermon at al-Jabiya. His son Abu al-Yaman ʿAmir, Azhar ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Harazi, Abu Salam al-Aswad, and others transmitted from him. Abu Zurʿa al-Razi and al-Daraqutni said: Abu ʿAmir al-Hawzani is acceptable. Ibn Hibban included him among the trustworthy Successors. Al-ʿIjli said: He was a trustworthy Syrian Successor and one of the senior Successors.

records.arabic:
من بني أبي بكر بن كلاب أبو المسيب الشاعر ويعرف بالقتال الكلابي قال أبو زيد الأنصاري هو من شعراء الجاهلية وذكر أبو عبيدة ان مروان بن الحكم سجنه قال أبو عبيد البكري في شرح أمالي القالي فهو على هذا من المخضرمين ومن شعره في قومه
هل من معاشر غيركم ادعوهم
فلقد سئمت دعاء يال كلاب
records.english:
of Banu Abi Bakr ibn Kilab, Abu al-Musayyib the poet, known as al-Qattal al-Kilabi. Abu Zayd al-Ansari said: He was one of the poets of the pre-Islamic period. Abu ʿUbayda mentioned that Marwan ibn al-Hakam imprisoned him. Abu ʿUbayd al-Bakri said in Sharh Amali al-Qali: On this basis he lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods. Among his poetry concerning his people is:

Are there clans other than you whom I may call?
I have grown weary of crying, “O people of Kilab!”

records.arabic:
التميمي ذكر المرزباني في معجم الشعراء انه استشهد باليمامة مع خالد بن الوليد فقال نافع بن الأسود يرثيه
اذهب فلا يبعدنك لله من رجل
موري حروب وللعافين والنادي
ما كان يعدله في الناس من أحد
ولا يوازيه في نعمى وارصاد
لقد تركت بني عمرو وأخوتها
يدعون باسمك للمنتاب والرادي
records.english:
al-Tamimi. Al-Marzubani mentioned in Muʿjam al-Shuʿaraʾ that he was martyred at al-Yamama with Khalid ibn al-Walid. Nafiʿ ibn al-Aswad elegized him, saying:

Go, and may God not make you distant—what a man,
a kindler of wars and a benefactor to petitioners and the assembly.
No one among the people was counted his equal,
nor matched him in beneficence and readiness.
You have left Banu ʿAmr and their brethren
calling your name for every visitor and comer.

records.arabic: قال بن عساكر له إدراك وكان رسول أبي بكر الصديق إلى أبي عبيدة لمادنا من الجابية ذكره أبو حذيفة إسحاق بن بشر في الفتوح عن بن إسحاق عمن أخبره عن عطاء عن بن عباس قال وسار أبو عبيدة حتى دنا من الجابية فقيل له ان هرقل بأنطاكية فكتب إلى أبي بكر فكتب اليه يعلمه انه يمده بالرجال بعد الرجال وبعث بكتابه مع عبد الله بن نزار العبسي
records.english: Ibn Asakir said that he lived into the Islamic period and was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq’s messenger to Abu ʿUbayda when he drew near al-Jabiya. Abu Hudhayfa Ishaq ibn Bishr mentioned him in al-Futuh, from Ibn Ishaq, from someone who informed him, from ʿAtaʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Abu ʿUbayda traveled until he drew near al-Jabiya. He was told that Heraclius was in Antioch, so he wrote to Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr wrote back informing him that he would reinforce him with men, one contingent after another, and sent his letter with ʿAbd Allah ibn Nizar al-ʿAbsi.

records.arabic: يأتي في هداج قال إبراهيم بن المندر حدثنا هاشم بن غطفان حدثني عبد الله بن هداج وكان قد أدرك الجاهلية قال جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر خبرا أخرجه أبو نعيم وقد أخرجه أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة عن هاشم بن غطفان فزاد عن بن عبد الله بن هداج عن أبيه قال جاء رجل فذكره قال البخاري في التاريخ عبد الله بن هداج من بني عدي بن حنيف روى عنه أبو عمار هاشم بن غطفان المزني
records.english: He appears under Hadaj. Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir said: Hashim ibn Ghatafan related to us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Hadaj, who had lived through the pre-Islamic period, related to me, saying: “A man came to the Prophet ﷺ,” and he related a report that Abu Nuʿaym cited. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba also cited it from Hashim ibn Ghatafan, adding: “from the son of ʿAbd Allah ibn Hadaj, from his father, who said: A man came,” and then he mentioned it. Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: ʿAbd Allah ibn Hadaj was of Banu ʿAdi ibn Hanif. Abu ʿAmmar Hashim ibn Ghatafan al-Muzani transmitted from him.

records.arabic: من بني راسب بن مالك بن ميدعان بن مالك بن نصر بن الأزد له إدراك وشهد فتوح العراق مع سعد بن أبي وقاص وذكر الطبري في التاريخ ان سعدا أرسله مع المضارب العجلي وجماعة وامر عليهم ضرار بن الخطاب بأمر عمر إلى أناس اجتمعوا من الذين يقاتلونهم ثم كان مع على في حروبه ولما وقع التحكيم فأنكره الخوارج واجتمعوا بالنهروان أمر عليهم عبد الله بن وهب الراسبي وكان عجبا في كثرة العبادة حتى لقب ذا الثفنات كان لكثرة سجوده صار في يديه وركبتيه كثفنات البعير وقتل الراسبي المذكور مع من قتل بالنهروان وقصته في ذلك مشهورة ذكره بن الكلبي وعيره
records.english: of Banu Rasib ibn Malik ibn Mayda'an ibn Malik ibn Nasr ibn al-Azd. He lived into the Islamic period and took part in the conquests of Iraq with Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Al-Tabari related in the History that, at Umar's command, Sa'd sent him with al-Mudarib al-Ijli and a group, appointing Dirar ibn al-Khattab over them, against some of those who were fighting them and had assembled. He was later with Ali in his wars. When arbitration took place, the Kharijites rejected it and gathered at al-Nahrawan; they appointed Abd Allah ibn Wahb al-Rasibi as their commander. He was extraordinary in the abundance of his worship, such that he was nicknamed Dhu al-Thafinat, because his frequent prostration had caused calluses like those of a camel to form on his hands and knees. The aforementioned al-Rasibi was killed with those slain at al-Nahrawan, and his story in that affair is well known. Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned him. The following source word remains uncertain; it may mean “and others.”

names.arabic: بني راسب بن مالك بن ميدعان بن مالك بن نصر بن الأزد
names.english: Banu Rasib ibn Malik ibn Mayda'an ibn Malik ibn Nasr ibn al-Azd

records.arabic:
الغاضري السكوني ذكره وثيمة في الردة وقال لما ازمع قومه على الردة وانتزعوا من زياد بن لبيد ناقة كان وسمها بميسم الصدقة قام فيهم عبد الله بن يزيد فقال يا معشر الملوك اني لا أصغر عن القول ولا يعظم أحد منكم عن الاستماع واني اناشدكم الله والرحم ان تصيروا أحاديث في ناقة أخذت بحق وارتجاعها باطل وانشدهم
ما كان في ناقة ضلت حلومكم
ما تغدرون بعهد الله والذمم
ألقى زياد عليها حق ميسمه
بعد اللسان وبعد الكف والقدم
ليس التشوش على بكر واخوتهم
أسام فيها ورب الحل والحرم قال فبعت اليه الأشعث بن قيس أرى كلامك يدفعنا وإياك إلى ما نكره وانا لا نحمل ذلك وخرج بينهم إلى المدينة ثم رجع مع المسلمين لقتالهم واستشهد مع زياد بن لبيد فرثاه مرباع الكندي بقوله
اعبد الله قد اعذرت فينا
ولكنا هزئنا بالنصيح
وقد اسمعتنا بدعاء داع
إلى العلياء والأمر الصحيح
records.english:
al-Ghadiri al-Sakuni. Wathima mentioned him in The Ridda and said: When his people resolved to apostatize and seized from Ziyad ibn Labid a she-camel that he had branded with the alms-tax brand, Abd Allah ibn Yazid stood among them and said, 'O company of kings, I am not too insignificant to speak, nor is any of you too great to listen. I adjure you by God and kinship: do not become the subject of tales over a she-camel that was taken rightfully and whose repossession is wrongful.' He recited to them:
Was it over a she-camel that your reason went astray?
Do not betray God's covenant and sworn pledges.
Ziyad placed upon her the due mark of his brand,
after the tongue, and after the hand and the foot.
Confusion against Bakr and their brothers has an uncertain construction;
The source’s next phrase remains unresolved in sense and connection—by the Lord of the profane and the sacred.
Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays then sent word to him: 'I see that your speech will drive us and you toward what we dislike, and we will not bear that.' He departed from among them for Medina, then returned with the Muslims to fight them, and he was martyred with Ziyad ibn Labid. Mirba' al-Kindi elegized him, saying:
O Abd Allah, you fully discharged your duty toward us,
but we mocked the sincere adviser.
You made us hear, through the call of one who called,
a summons to loftiness and the sound course.

names.arabic: عبد الله بن يزيد بن قيس الغاضري السكوني

records.arabic:
أخو الأحوص بن جعفر بن كلاب العامري الكلابي ذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء وكان شهد القادسية فعقر ناقته وقال
وما عقرت بالسيلحيين مطيتي
وبالجسر الا خشية ان اعيرا قلت وما أظنه ترك اسمه على حاله في الإسلام
records.english:
the brother of al-Ahwas ibn Jafar ibn Kilab al-Amiri al-Kilabi. Al-Marzubani mentioned him in the Dictionary of Poets. He witnessed al-Qadisiyya, where he hamstrung his she-camel and said:
I did not hamstring my mount at al-Silhayn,
nor at the bridge, except from fear that I would be reproached.
I say: I do not think he retained his name unchanged in Islam.

names.arabic: الأحوص بن جعفر بن كلاب العامري الكلابي
names.english: al-Ahwas ibn Ja'far ibn Kilab al-Amiri al-Kilabi

records.arabic: ويقال بن محمد بن خولى بن عبد عمرو بن عبد يغوت بن الصائد الهمداني أبو عمارة الكوفي أدرك الجاهلية قال الخطيب يقال اسمه عبد الرحمن قلت ولعله غير في الإسلام وقال أبو عمر أدرك زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسمع منه قلت وتأتي فصة إسلامه في زمن النبي صلى الله عيه وآله وسلم في ترجمة والده يزيد رواها أبو يعلى وغيره روى عبد خير عن أبي بكر الصديق وعن بن مسعود وعلى وكان من كبار اصحابه وعن عائشة وغيرهم روى عنه ابنه المسيب والشعبي وأبو إسحاق السبيعي وعبد الملك بن سلع وعلقمة بن مرثد والحكم وعطاء بن السائب وآخرون نزل الكوفة قال عبد الملك بن سلع قلت له كم اتى عليك قال عشرون ومائة سنة أخرجه الدولابي في الكنى فيمن يكنى أبا عمارة وذكره أحمد بن حنبل في الاثبات عن على ووثقه بن معين والنسائي والعجلي وذكره مسلم في الطبقة الأولى من التابعين
records.english: or, it is said, son of Muhammad ibn Khawla ibn Abd Amr ibn Abd Yaghuth ibn al-Sa'id—al-Hamdani, Abu Umara al-Kufi. He lived in the pre-Islamic period. Al-Khatib said that his name was reportedly Abd al-Rahman. I say: perhaps it was changed in Islam. Abu Umar said that he lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not hear from him. I say: the account of his accepting Islam during the time of the Prophet ﵌ will appear in the biography of his father Yazid; Abu Ya'la and others transmitted it. Abd Khayr related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Ibn Mas'ud, Ali—he was one of Ali's leading companions—and A'isha, among others. Those who related from him include his son al-Musayyib, al-Sha'bi, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Abd al-Malik ibn Sala', Alqama ibn Marthad, al-Hakam, Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, and others. He settled in Kufa. Abd al-Malik ibn Sala' said: 'I asked him, “How old have you become?” He replied, “One hundred and twenty years.”' Al-Dulabi included this in al-Kuna among those bearing the kunyah Abu Umara. Ahmad ibn Hanbal listed him among the reliable authorities transmitting from Ali. Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i, and al-Ijli declared him trustworthy, and Muslim placed him in the first rank of the Successors.

records.arabic: ذكره وثيمة في كتاب الردة عن بن إسحاق فيمن انحاز من بني أسد عن طليحة بن خويلد الأسدي لما ادعى النبوة واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: Wathima mentioned him in the Book of Apostasy, from Ibn Ishaq, among those of Banu Asad who withdrew from Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi when he claimed prophethood. Ibn Fathun added him as an omission.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
أخو ضرار بن الأزور الصحابي كان ببلاد قومه لما ادعى طليحة بن خويلد النبوة ففارقه وقال يخاطب اخاه ضرارا ليحرض الأنصار على جهاد من بالبطاح من أهل الردة بقصيدة أولها
قد قلت للمرء الشقيق ضرار
طال البكاء لفرقة الأنصار ( ذكره وثيمة عن بن إسحاق )
records.english:
the brother of Dirar ibn al-Azwar, the Companion. He was in his people's territory when Tulayha ibn Khuwaylid claimed prophethood, so he parted from him. Addressing his brother Dirar in order to urge the Ansar to fight the apostates at al-Bitah, he said a poem beginning:
I said to the man who is my full brother, Dirar:
long has the weeping been over separation from the Ansar.
(Wathima mentioned him from Ibn Ishaq.)

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن مالك بن الصحبان الأزدي بن عم سنان بن كعب بن مالك بن الصحبان المقدم ذكره له إدراك وكان ولده مجاعة شريفا في الأزد في زمان المهلب ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english: son of Malik ibn al-Sahban al-Azdi, the paternal cousin of Sinan ibn Ka'b ibn Malik ibn al-Sahban, mentioned previously. He lived into the Islamic period. His son Muja'a was a noble among al-Azd in the time of al-Muhallab. Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned him.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن تيم بن مالك بن الصحبان الأزدي
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Taym ibn Malik ibn al-Sahban al-Azdi

names.arabic: سنان بن كعب بن مالك بن الصحبان
names.english: Sinan ibn Ka'b ibn Malik ibn al-Sahban

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكره وثيمة في كتاب الردة عن بن إسحاق وانه ممن ثبت على إسلامه وفارق طليحة وقد تقدم ذكر أبيه حبيش في الحاء المهملة ويأتي ذكر أخيه غسان في الغين المعجمة
records.english: Wathima mentioned him in the Book of Apostasy, from Ibn Ishaq, and said that he was among those who remained steadfast in Islam and parted from Tulayha. His father Hubaysh was discussed above under the unpointed letter ha, and his brother Ghassan will be discussed under the dotted letter ghayn.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكر المدائني انه وفد على أبي بكر الصديق فسماه عبد الرحمن وقد تقدم في حرف الباء الموحدة في باب وهو اسمه الأول وذكرت له قصة في فتح تستر مع أبي موسى الأشعري نقلته من خط الخطيب في المؤتلف
records.english: al-Madaini mentioned related that he came as a delegation to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who named him Abd al-Rahman. He was discussed above under the single-dotted letter ba, in 'Bab,' which was his first name. I also related there an account concerning him in the conquest of Tustar with Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, copied from al-Khatib's handwriting in al-Mu'talif.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن ذي الجرة الحميري
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Dhi al-Jarra al-Himyari

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

title.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن ذي الجرة الحميري
title.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Dhi al-Jarra al-Himyari

records.arabic: أخو أبي وائل شقيق روى عنه شقيق وكان عبد الرحمن اسن منه وقد تقدم ذكر شقيق في هذا القسم وعبد الرحمن أولى بذلك وذكره بن حبان في ثقات التابعين وقال روى عنه اخوه
records.english: the brother of Abu Wail, Shaqiq. Shaqiq related from him, and Abd al-Rahman was older than he. Shaqiq was discussed previously in this section, though Abd al-Rahman has a stronger claim to inclusion here. Ibn Hibban listed him among the trustworthy Successors and said that his brother related from him.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال البغوي يقال انه أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ونفي ذلك أبو حاتم وغيره وسأذكر ترجمته في القسم الرابع
records.english: Al-Baghawi said that he was reportedly alive in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. Abu Hatim and others denied this. I will give his biography in the fourth section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن عساكر له أدرك واخرج من طريق الخرائطي بسند له إلى جعفر بن برقان عن أبي سكينة الحمصي عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله قال قدم عمر بن الخطاب الجابية فقام فينا خطيبا فذكر الخطبة
records.english: Ibn Asakir said he lived into the Islamic period, and transmitted, by way of al-Khara'iti with his chain to Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Abu Sakina al-Himsi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab came to al-Jabiya, stood among us as a preacher, and delivered the sermon.'

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بمهملتين مصغرا بن عسل مكبرا ثم سكون بن عسال المرادي أبو عبيد الله الصنابحي اليماني نزيل الشام وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فوجده قد مات فصلى خلف أبي بكر وروى عنه وعن عمر وعي وبلال وسعد بن عبادة ومعاذ بن جبل وجماعة روى عنه اسلم مولى عمر وعطاء بن يسار وعبد الله بن محيريز وأبو الخير اليزني ويونس بن ميسرة وآخرون قال بن سعد ثقة قليل الحديث وقال بن يونس شهد فتح مصر وقال العجلي تابعي ثقة ونحوه بن حبان وقال بن معين تأخر إلى زمان عبد الملك وذكره البخاري فيمن مات ما بين السبعين إلى الثمانين وقال يعقوب بن شيبة هؤلاء الصنابحيون الذين يروى عنهم في العدد ستة وانما هما اثنان فقط الصنابح الأحمسي ويقال له الصنابحي الأحمسي وهو واحد ومن ذكره بلفظ النسب أخطأ وهو الذي يروي عنه الكوفيون والثاني عبد الرحمن بن عسيلة كنيته أبو عبد الله روايته عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مرسلة وروى عن أبي بكر وغيره فمن قال فيه عبد الرحمن الصنابحي أصاب اسمه ومن قال عن أبي عبد الله الصنابحي أصاب كنيته ومن قال عن أبي عبد الرحمن الصنابحي فقد أخطأ قلب كنيته فجعلها اسمه هذا قول على بن المديني ومن تابعه قال يعقوب وهو الصواب عندي قلت وقد تقدم في العبادلة في القسم الأول بيان الاختلاف في عبد الله الصنابحي ومن اثبت انه غير عبد الرحمن بن عسيلة ومن نسب من قال ذلك للوهم ولله الحمد
records.english: written with two unpointed consonants, in diminutive form—ibn Asal, in the augmentative, then Sukun ibn Assal al-Muradi, Abu Ubayd Allah al-Sunabihi al-Yamani, a resident of Syria. He came in delegation to the Prophet ﷺ but found that he had died, so he prayed behind Abu Bakr. He related from Abu Bakr, Umar, [an unidentified narrator in the damaged reading], Bilal, Sa'd ibn Ubada, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, and a group. Those who related from him include Aslam, Umar's client, Ata ibn Yasar, Abd Allah ibn Muhayriz, Abu al-Khayr al-Yazani, Yunus ibn Maysara, and others. Ibn Sa'd said: 'Trustworthy, with few hadiths.' Ibn Yunus said that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt. Al-Ijli said: 'A trustworthy Successor,' and Ibn Hibban said something similar. Ibn Ma'in said that he lived until the time of Abd al-Malik. Al-Bukhari listed him among those who died between the years seventy and eighty. Ya'qub ibn Shayba said: 'The persons called al-Sunabihi from whom reports are related are numbered as six, but in fact they are only two. One is al-Sunabih al-Ahmasi, who is also called al-Sunabihi al-Ahmasi; he is one person, and anyone who mentioned him with the nisbah form was mistaken. He is the one from whom the Kufans relate. The second is Abd al-Rahman ibn Usayla, whose kunyah is Abu Abd Allah. His transmission from the Prophet ﷺ is disconnected, and he related from Abu Bakr and others. Whoever called him Abd al-Rahman al-Sunabihi got his name right; whoever said Abu Abd Allah al-Sunabihi got his kunyah right; and whoever said Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sunabihi erred, reversing his kunyah and making it his name.' This is the view of Ali ibn al-Madini and those who followed him. Ya'qub said: 'In my view, it is correct.' I say: the disagreement concerning Abd Allah al-Sunabihi was explained above among the Abd Allahs in the first section, including who affirmed that he was distinct from Abd al-Rahman ibn Usayla and who attributed error to the one who said so. ولله الحمد.

records.arabic: الجرشي الحمصي قاضيها ذكره بن منده في الصحابة وتعقبه أبو نعيم بأنه مشهور من تابعي أهل الشام وقد روى آدم بن أبي إياس في كتاب الثواب عن حريز بن عثمان عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي عوف وكان قد أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكر حديثا وذكره جمهور من صنف في الرجال في التابعين قال العجلي شامي تابعي ثقة وذكره بن حبان في الثقات
records.english: al-Jurashi of Hims, its judge. Ibn Manda listed him among the Companions. Abu Nu'aym objected that he was well known as one of the Successors of Syria. Adam ibn Abi Iyas related in The Book of Reward, from Hariz ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Awf—who had lived in the time of the Prophet ﷺ—and then gave a hadith. Most authors who wrote on transmitters listed him among the Successors. Al-Ijli said: 'A Syrian, a trustworthy Successor.' Ibn Hibban included him among the trustworthy.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن أبي عوف الجرشي الحمصي
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Awf al-Jurashi al-Himsi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بن كريز ويقال هانئ بن ربيعة بن عامر بن عدي بن وائل الأشعري تقدم نسبه وسمي ابنه في القسم الأول واما هذا فتابعي شهير له إدراك وهاجر في زمن عمر قال البغوي هو قديم لا أدري أدرك أم لا وقيل انه ولد في حياة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال حرب عن أحمد أدرك ولم يسمع وقال الترمذي يقال انه أدرك وقال أبو نعيم مختلف في صحبته وقال أبو حاتم جاهلي ليست له صحبة وروايته مرسلة وقال أبو عمر كان مسلما في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يره سمع معاذ بن جبل وقال يعقوب بن شيبة أدرك عمر وسمع منه وقال بن أبي خيثمة قال أبو مسهر كان رأس التابعين وقد روى عبد الرحمن بن غنم عن عمر وعثمان ومعاذ وأبي عبيدة وأبي ذر وأبي الدرداء وأبي مالك الأشعري وشداد بن أوس وثوبان وعبادة وغيرهم روى عنه ابنه محمد وعطية بن قيس وأبو سلام الأسود وشهر بن حوشب ومكحول ورجاء بن حيوة وآخرون وقال أبو زرعة الدمشقي عن دحيم عبد الرحمن بن غنم مقدم عندي على الصنابحي وهو رجل أهل الشام قال خليفة وغيره مات سنة ثمان وسبعين من الهجرة
records.english: son of Kurayz, also said to be Hani, son of Rabia ibn Amir ibn Adi ibn Wa'il—al-Ash'ari. His lineage was given above, and his son was named in the first section. This man, however, was a famous Successor who lived into the Islamic period and emigrated in Umar's time. Al-Baghawi said: 'He was early; I do not know whether he lived to see [the Prophet] or not.' It was also said that he was born during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. Harb related from Ahmad: 'He lived to see him but did not hear from him.' Al-Tirmidhi said that he was reportedly alive then. Abu Nu'aym said that his status as a Companion was disputed. Abu Hatim said: 'He was a man of the pre-Islamic period, but he had no Companionship, and his transmission is disconnected.' Abu Umar said: 'He was a Muslim during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not see him. He heard Mu'adh ibn Jabal.' Ya'qub ibn Shayba said that he lived to see Umar and heard from him. Ibn Abi Khaythama said that Abu Mushir stated: 'He was the foremost of the Successors.' Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm related from Umar, Uthman, Mu'adh, Abu Ubayda, Abu Dharr, Abu al-Darda, Abu Malik al-Ash'ari, Shaddad ibn Aws, Thawban, Ubada, and others. Those who related from him include his son Muhammad, Atiyya ibn Qays, Abu Sallam al-Aswad, Shahr ibn Hawshab, Makhul, Raja ibn Haywa, and others. Abu Zur'a al-Dimashqi related from Duhaym: 'In my view, Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm takes precedence over al-Sunabihi; he is the learned man of the people of Syria.' Khalifa and others said that he died in the year 78 AH.

aliases: Hani ibn Rabi'a ibn Amir ibn Adi ibn Wa'il
names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن غنم بن كريز
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm ibn Kurayz

records.arabic: أبو عطية المذبوح مشهور بكنيته له إدراك وشهد اليرموك قال بن المبارك في الزهد حدثنا أبو بكر بن أبي مريم عن حماد بن سعيد بن أبي عطية قال لما حضر أبا عطية الموت جزع فقيل له اتجزع قال ومالي لا اجزع وانما هي ساعة ثم لا أدري أين يسلك بي وذكر بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه انه سأل عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد العزيز بن محمد بن أبي عطية المذبوح عن اسم جده فقال عبد الرحمن بن قيس وانما قيل له المذبوح لأنه أصابه سهم وهو مع أبي عبيدة باليرموك فقطع جلده ولم يفر الاوداج فكان إذا شرب الماء يرى مجراه عاش بعد ذلك زمانا فسمى المذبوح
records.english: Abu Atiyya al-Madhbuh, known by his kunya. He lived into the Islamic period and witnessed al-Yarmuk. Ibn al-Mubarak said in al-Zuhd: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam related to us, from Hammad ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Atiyya, who said: When death approached Abu Atiyya, he became alarmed. He was asked, 'Are you alarmed?' He replied, 'Why should I not be alarmed? It is but an hour, after which I do not know where I will be taken.' Ibn Abi Hatim related from his father that he asked Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Atiyya al-Madhbuh about his ancestor's name, and he replied, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays.' He was called al-Madhbuh, 'the Slaughtered,' because an arrow struck him while he was with Abu Ubayda at al-Yarmuk and cut his skin without severing the jugular veins. When he drank water, its course could be seen. He lived for a long time afterward and so was named al-Madhbuh.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن قيس بن سواء
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays ibn Sawa

names.arabic: حماد بن سعيد بن أبي عطية
names.english: Hammad ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Atiyya

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن عبد الرحمن بن عبد العزيز بن محمد بن أبي عطية المذبوح
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Aziz ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Atiyya al-Madhbuh

title.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن قيس بن سواء
title.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Qays ibn Sawa

records.arabic: شامي سمع أبا عبيدة بن الجراح روى عنه الوليد بن أبي مالك ذكره البخاري وقال لا يصح حديثه وقال أبو حاتم بل هو صالح الحديث
records.english: a Syrian who heard Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, and al-Walid ibn Abi Malik related from him. Al-Bukhari mentioned him and said that his hadith is unsound. Abu Hatim, however, said that he is acceptable in hadith.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الحنفي أدرك الجاهلية ولما ارتد أهل اليمامة انكر على مسيلمة وقومه وكتب إلى أبي بكر يخبره بعورتهم ذكره وثيمة وأنشد له شعرا يمدح فيه خالد بن الوليد وفيه لسنا نغرك من حنيفة انهم والراقصات إلى بني كفار
records.english: al-Hanafi; he lived in the pre-Islamic period. When the people of al-Yamama apostatized, he denounced Musaylima and his people and wrote to Abu Bakr informing him of their vulnerable points. Wathima mentioned him and cited poetry by him praising Khalid ibn al-Walid, including: 'We do not mislead you concerning Hanifa: by those swaying on the journey to Mina, they are unbelievers.'

records.arabic: بفتح الميم ويجوز ضمها وكسرها بعدها لام ثقيلة بن عمرو بن عدي بن وهب بن ربيعة بن سعد بن خزيمة بن كعب بن رفاعة بن مالك بن نهد أبو عثمان النهدي مشهور بكنيته نسبه بن الكلبي وتبعه جماعة وسقط من كلام أبي عمر ذكره سعد ولا بد منه ذكره بن أبي شيبة من طريق عاصم سئل أبو عثمان وأبا اسمع هل أدركت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال نعم واسلمت على عهده واديت له ثلاث صدقات وغزوت على عهد عمر غزوات وروى بن أبي خيثمة من طريق حميد بن أبي عثمان قال كنا في الجاهلية إذا تحملنا حملنا حجرا على بعير فإذا رأينا أحسن منه القيناه واخذنا الآخر فإذا سقط عن البعير قلنا سقط إلهكم فالتمسوا غيره قال بن المديني هاجر إلى المدينة بعد موت أبي بكر فوافق استخلاف عمر فسمع منه ونزل الكوفة فلما قتل الحسين تحول إلى البصرة وسمع أبو عثمان من كبار الصحابة فروى عن عمر وعلى وسعد وسعيد وطلحة وابن مسعود وحذيفة وبلال وأبي هريرة وأبي موسى وعائشة وغيرهم روى عنه قتادة وسليمان التيمي وثابت وعاصم الأحول وعوف وخالد الحذاء وأيوب وحميد وآخرون قال عبد القاهر بن السري عن أبيه عن جده حج أبو عثمان ستين حجة وعمرة وكان يقول اتت على مائة وثلاثون سنة قال عمرو بن علي مات سنة خمس وتسعين وقال بن معين سنة مائة وقال خليفة بعد سنة مائة
records.english: the mim has a fathah but may also have a dammah or kasrah, followed by a doubled lam—ibn Amr ibn Adi ibn Wahb ibn Rabi'a ibn Sa'd ibn Khuzayma ibn Ka'b ibn Rifa'a ibn Malik ibn Nahd, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, famous by his kunyah. Ibn al-Kalbi gave this lineage and a group followed him. Sa'd has fallen out of Abu Umar's wording, though it is indispensable. Ibn Abi Shayba mentioned, by way of Asim, a damaged attribution, followed by the question: 'Did you live to see the Prophet ﷺ?' He replied: 'Yes. I accepted Islam during his lifetime, paid three alms levies to him, and went on military expeditions during Umar's rule.' Ibn Abi Khaythama related by way of Humayd that Abu Uthman said: 'In the pre-Islamic period, whenever we traveled we would load a stone onto a camel. If we saw a better one, we threw it away and took the other. If it fell from the camel, we would say, “Your god has fallen; look for another one.”' Ibn al-Madini said: 'He emigrated to Medina after Abu Bakr's death and arrived at the time Umar assumed the caliphate, so he heard from him. He settled in Kufa, but when al-Husayn was killed he moved to Basra.' Abu Uthman heard from leading Companions, relating from Umar, Ali, Sa'd, Sa'id, Talha, Ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfa, Bilal, Abu Hurayra, Abu Musa, A'isha, and others. Those who related from him include Qatada, Sulayman al-Taymi, Thabit, Asim al-Ahwal, Awf, Khalid al-Hadhdha, Ayyub, Humayd, and others. Abd al-Qahir ibn al-Sari related from his father, from his grandfather: 'Abu Uthman performed sixty pilgrimages and umras, and used to say, “I have reached one hundred and thirty years.”' Amr ibn Ali said that he died in 95 AH; Ibn Ma'in said in 100; and Khalifa said after 100.

records.arabic: أدرك الجاهلية وهاجر في خلافة عمر وقرأ على معاذ بن جبل ذكر ذلك أبو سعيد بن يونس ثم صار من كبار الخوارج وهو اشقى هذه الأمة بالنص الثابت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقتل علي بن أبي طالب فقتله أولاد علي وذلك في شهر رمضان سنة أربع وأربعين ذكره الذهبي في التجريد لكونه على الشرط وليس بأهل ان يذكر مع هؤلاء وبسطت ترجمته في لسان الميزان
records.english: He lived in the pre-Islamic period and emigrated during Umar's caliphate, and studied recitation under Mu'adh ibn Jabal; Abu Sa'id ibn Yunus mentioned this. He later became one of the leading Kharijites. By the sound text from the Prophet ﷺ, he is the most wretched person of this community, on account of his killing Ali ibn Abi Talib. Ali's sons killed him, in Ramadan of the year 44 AH. Al-Dhahabi included him in al-Tajrid because he met its criteria, though he is unworthy of being mentioned with these men. I treated his biography at length in Lisan al-Mizan.

records.arabic: ذكره الواقدي فيمن اسلم من أهل سبأ في العهد النبوي وكذا ذكره سيف في الفتوح وقد تقدم ذكر أخيه عبد الله وسيأتي في ترجمة أبيه النعمان كيفية إسلامه
records.english: Al-Waqidi mentioned him among the people of Saba who accepted Islam during the Prophetic era, and Sayf likewise mentioned him in The Conquests. His brother Abd Allah was discussed above, and the manner of his conversion will appear in the biography of his father al-Nu'man.

records.english: their client and the grandfather of Musa ibn Nusayr, who conquered the Far Maghreb. Before that he witnessed al-Yarmuk with his father and was martyred that day, in the year 15 AH.'

records.arabic: بن عبد الله بن أبي يعمر بن حبيب بن عائذ بن مالك بن وائلة بن عمرو بن ناج بن يشكر بن عدوان بن عمر بن قيس بن غيلان الجدلي أبو عبد الله مشهور بكنيته وقيل اسمه عبد الرحمن قال بن منده هو قديم ثم ذكر في الصحابة ولا يصح قلت أرسل شيئا وهو معدود في التابعين ذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى من تابعي أهل الكوفة وروى عن سلمان الفارسي وعن علي وعائشة وغيرهم روى عنه الشعبي وأبو إسحاق السبيعي وسعيد بن خالد الجدلي وآخرون ووثقه أحمد وابن معين والعجلي
records.english: son of Abd Allah ibn Abi Yamar ibn Habib ibn A'idh ibn Malik ibn Wa'ila ibn Amr ibn Naj ibn Yashkur ibn Adwan ibn Amr ibn Qays ibn Ghaylan al-Jadali, Abu Abd Allah, famous by his kunyah. It is also said that his name was Abd al-Rahman. Ibn Manda said, 'He was early,' and then listed him among the Companions, but that is unsound. I say: he transmitted something in disconnected form and is counted among the Successors. Ibn Sa'd listed him in the first generation of the Kufan Successors. He related from Salman al-Farisi, Ali, A'isha, and others. Al-Sha'bi, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Sa'id ibn Khalid al-Jadali, and others related from him. Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, and al-Ijli declared him trustworthy.

records.arabic:
واسم الطبيب يزيد بن عمرو بن وعلة بن أنس ان عبد الله بن عبد نهم بن جشم بن عبد شمس بن سعد بن زيد مناة بن تميم الشاعر المشهور ذكر سيف في الفتوح انه شهد مع المثنى بن حارثة قتال هرمز وله في ذلك آثار مشهورة وكان في جيش النعمان بن مقرن الذين حاربوا الفرس بالمدائن قال أبو الفرج هو مخضرم وهو شاعر مجيد ليس بالمنكر وهو القائل في قتال الفرس
هل حبل خولة بعد الهجر موصول
أم أنت عنها بعيد الدار مشغول يقول فيها
يقارعون رءوس الفرس ضاحية
منهم فوارس لا عزل ولا ميل وذكر بن دريد في الاخبار المنثورة وأبو الفرج الأصبهاني في الاغاني عنه عن بن أخي الأصمعي عن عمه قال اجتمع الزبرقان بن بدر والمخبل السعدي وعبدة بن الطبيب وعمرو بن الاهتم وعلقمة بن عبدة قبل ان يسلموا والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمكة قبل ان يبعث فنحروا جزورا واشتروا خمرا ببعير وجعلوا يشوون ويأكلون ويشربون فقال بعضهم لو ان قوما طاروا من جودة اشعارهم لطرتم فتحاكموا إلى أول من يطلع عليهم فطلع ربيعة بن حدار اليربوعي فسروا به وحكموه فقال أخاف ان تغضبوا فأمنوه من ذلك فقال لهم اما عمرو فشعره برود يمنية تنشر وتطوي واما الزبرقان فكرجل اتى جزورا فأخذ من مطايها ثم خلطه بعد ذلك واما المخبل فشهب نار يلقيها الله على من يشاء من عباده واما علقمة فكمزادة احكم خرزها فليس يسقط منها شيء وقال المرزباني كان عبدة اسود من لصوص الرباب وهو مخضرم وهو الذي رثى قيس بن عاصم المنقري التميمي لما مات بقوله
عليك سلام الله قيس بن عاصم
ورحمته ما شاء ان يترحما
تحية من اوليته منك نعمة
إذا زار عن شحط بلادك سلما ويقول فيها
وما كان قيس هلكه هلك واحد
ولكنه بنيان قوم تهدما كان أبو عمرو بن العلاء يقول هذا البيت ارثى بيت قيل وقال بن الأعرابي هو قائم بنفسه ماله نظير في الجاهلية ولا الإسلام قال ولما اسن عبدة جمع بنيه وانشأ قصيدته التي يوصيهم فيها وهي من القصائد التي يقول فيها
ولقد علمت بأن قصري حفرة
غبراء يحملني إليها شرجع
فبكت بناتي شجوهن وزوجتي
والاقربون إلى ثم تصدعوا
وتركت في غبراء يكره وردها
تسفى على الريح حين أودع قوله قصري بفتح القاف وسكون المهملة أي آخر امرى قوله شرجع بفتح المعجمة وسكون الراء ثم جيم هو سرير الميت وقوله تصدعوا أي تفرقوا قوله تسفى بمهملة ثم فاء مع فتح أوله أي تهب بالتراب وقال المرزباني مخضرم ويروي ان عمر كان يعجب من شعر عبدة وقيل لخالد بن صفوان ان عبدة لا يحسن ان يهجو فقال لا بل كان يترفع عن الهجاء
records.english:
And al-Tabib's name was Yazid ibn Amr ibn Wala ibn Anas [the source’s intervening word has an unclear connection to the following name] Abd Allah ibn Abd Nuhm ibn Jusham ibn Abd Shams ibn Sa'd ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim—the famous poet. Sayf mentioned in The Conquests that he joined al-Muthanna ibn Haritha in fighting Hurmuz, and had well-known exploits in that affair. He was among al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin's army that fought the Persians at al-Mada'in. Abu al-Faraj said: 'He was a mukhadram and an excellent poet, by no means objectionable.' Among what he said concerning the fighting against the Persians was:
Is Khawla's bond joined again after abandonment,
or are you, far from home, preoccupied away from her?
In it he says:
They batter the Persians' heads in open daylight;
among them are horsemen neither unarmed nor inclined away.
Ibn Durayd, in al-Akhbar al-Manthura, and Abu al-Faraj al-Isbahani, in al-Aghani, related from him, from the son of al-Asma'i's brother, from his uncle, who said: Al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, al-Mukhabbal al-Sa'di, Abada ibn al-Tabib, Amr ibn al-Ahtam, and Alqama ibn Abada gathered before they accepted Islam, while the Prophet ﷺ was in Mecca before he was commissioned. They slaughtered a camel, bought wine for a camel, and began roasting, eating, and drinking. One of them said, 'If people could fly by virtue of the quality of their poetry, you would fly.' They agreed to seek the judgment of the first person who came upon them. Rabi'a ibn Hadhar al-Yarbu'i appeared, and they were pleased with him and made him judge. He said, 'I fear you will become angry.' They guaranteed him safety from that. He said: 'As for Amr, his poetry is like Yemeni striped robes, unfolded and folded. As for al-Zibriqan, it is like a man who came to a slaughtered camel, took from its choice portions, and then mixed them afterward. As for al-Mukhabbal, it is like meteors of fire that God casts upon whomever He wills among His servants. As for Alqama, it is like a waterskin whose stitching has been made firm, so nothing falls from it.' Al-Marzubani said that Abada was a Black man, one of the brigands of al-Rabab, and a mukhadram. He was the one who elegized Qays ibn Asim al-Minqari al-Tamimi upon his death, saying:
Upon you be God's peace, Qays ibn Asim,
and His mercy, so long as one prays for mercy.
A greeting from one upon whom you bestowed a favor;
when he visits your distant land, he greets it.
He also says in it:
The death of Qays was not the death of one man;
rather, the edifice of a people collapsed.
Abu Amr ibn al-Ala used to say that this was the most elegiac line ever uttered. Ibn al-A'rabi said: 'It stands alone; it has no peer in either the pre-Islamic or Islamic period.' He said: When Abada grew old, he gathered his sons and composed the poem in which he counselled them. It is one of the poems in which he says:
I knew full well that my final end is a dusty pit
to which a bier will carry me.
My daughters wept out their sorrow, as did my wife,
and my nearest kin; then they dispersed.
I was left in the dusty place whose approach is loathed;
the wind blows dust over me when I am laid down.
His word qasri, with fatha on the qaf and an unpointed letter with sukun, means 'the end of my affair.' His word sharja', with fatha on the dotted letter, then ra with sukun, then jim, means 'the dead man's bier.' His word tasadda'u means 'they dispersed.' His word tasfi, with an unpointed letter followed by fa and with its first letter bearing fatha, means 'it blows dust.' Al-Marzubani said: 'A mukhadram.' It is related that Umar admired Abada's poetry. Khalid ibn Safwan was told that Abada did not know how to satirize; he replied, 'No—rather, he held himself above satire.'

records.english: son of Amr ibn Khalid ibn al-Mujamma ibn Malik ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd ibn Awf ibn Uwaym ibn Ju'fi ibn Sa'd al-Ashira al-Ju'fi. He lived into the Islamic period. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he was a poet and [the source may describe him as daring or violent, but the reading is damaged]. It will be stated in the biography of Marthad ibn Qays that Abd Allah ibn al-Hurr witnessed al-Qadisiyya.

records.english: also called Damra ibn Hawdha, or Hawdh, al-Hanafi al-Yamami. He lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not meet him. He was discussed previously in the biography of Lafi's, or al-Ufaysir al-Yamami, in the first section.

records.arabic:
بغير إضافة مصغرا بن سراقة حجازي يقول لعمر
فإنك مسترعي وانا رعية
وانك مدعو بسيماك يا عمر وذكره المرزباني ويأتي في عمرو
records.english:
without a genitive compound, in diminutive form, son of Suraqa, a Hijazi. He said to Umar:
You have been appointed shepherd, and we are a flock,
and you will be summoned by your distinguishing mark, O Umar.
Al-Marzubani mentioned him. He will appear under Amr.

records.english: He fought at al-Qadisiyya and settled in Kufa. Ibn Hibban listed him among the trustworthy Successors.

records.arabic: بمعجمة وزن عطية أحد المعمرين روى أبو موسى من طريق معاوية بن سليم عن هشام بن محمد عن أبيه محمد بن السائب الكلبي قال عاش عبيد بن شرية الجرهمي مائتين وأربعين سنة وقيل ثلاثمائة سنة واسلم ووفد على معاوية فقال أخبرني باعجب ما رأيت قال انتهيت إلى قوم يدفنون ميتا فذكر قصة وفيها الشعر المشهور يبكي الغريب عليه ليس يعرفه وذو قرابته في الحي مسرور وأخرجها أبو موسى من طريق عمران بن سعيد القرشي عن أبيه ان معاوية اتى بعمير بن شرية وقد اتت عليه عشرون ومائتا سنة فذكر نحوه وفيه الشعر فلعل قوله في هذه الرواية عمير تصحيف سمعي فان المشهور عبيد وقد ذكر الرشاطي عن الهمداني ان معاوية كان مستشرفا لاخبار حمير فقال له عمرو بن العاص أين أنت عن عبيد بن شرية فإنه اعلم من بقي بأخبارهم وانسابهم فكتب اليه يأخذ منه الاخبار فالفها كتابا وقد زيد فيه ونقص فلا يؤخذ منه نسختان مستويتان وذكر محمد بن إسحاق النديم في الفهرست انه روى عن زيد بن الكيس وعن أبيه الكيس وعاش عبيد إلى خلافة عبد الملك بن مروان
records.english:
with a dotted letter, on the pattern of Atiyya—one of the exceptionally long-lived. Abu Musa related by way of Mu'awiya ibn Sulaym, from Hisham ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, who said: 'Ubayd ibn Shariya al-Jurhumi lived for 240 years'; it was also said, 300 years. He accepted Islam and came in delegation to Mu'awiya, who said: 'Tell me the most remarkable thing you saw.' He replied: 'I came upon some people burying a dead man,' and related an account containing the famous verse:
The stranger weeps over him, though he does not know him,
while his kinsman in the tribe is rejoicing.
Abu Musa also transmitted it by way of Imran ibn Sa'id al-Qurashi, from his father, stating that Umayr ibn Shariya was brought to Mu'awiya when 220 years had passed over him. He related something similar, including the verse. Perhaps 'Umayr' in this version is an aural corruption, for the well-known name is Ubayd. Al-Rushati related from al-Hamdani that Mu'awiya was eager to learn the reports of Himyar. Amr ibn al-As said to him: 'Why not consult Ubayd ibn Shariya? He is the most learned surviving authority on their reports and genealogies.' He wrote to him and took reports from him, and Ubayd compiled them into a book. Additions and omissions have entered it, so no two copies of it are identical. Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Nadim mentioned in al-Fihrist that he related from Zayd ibn al-Kays and from Zayd's father al-Kays. Ubayd lived until the caliphate of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.

records.arabic: بن سمرة بن عمرو بن قرط التميمي ثم العنبري لأبيه صحبة وبعثه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على الصدقات ولولده عبيد إدراك ولا يعرف له صحبة وله قصة مع إبراهيم بن عربي والى اليمامة في خلافة عبد الملك بن مروان ومع جرير بن الخطفي الشاعر
records.english: son of Samura ibn Amr ibn Qurt al-Tamimi, then al-Anbari. His father had Companionship, and the Prophet ﷺ sent him to collect the alms taxes. His son Ubayd lived into the Islamic period, but no Companionship is known for him. He has an account involving Ibrahim ibn Arabi, governor of al-Yamama during the caliphate of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, and Jarir ibn al-Khatafi, the poet.

names.arabic: عبيد بن غاضرة بن سمرة بن عمرو بن قرط التميمي
names.english: Ubayd ibn Ghadira ibn Samura ibn Amr ibn Qurt al-Tamimi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك ورواية عن عمر واخرج أحمد في الزهد من طريق سعيد بن أبي هلال عن عبد العزيز بن عمر انه سمع عمر يقول لا يعجبنكم طنطنة الرجل ولكن من أدى الأمانة وكف عن اعراض الناس فهو الرجل
records.english: He lived into the Islamic period and transmitted from Umar. Ahmad related in al-Zuhd, by way of Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Umar, that he heard Umar say: 'Do not be impressed by a man's bombast. The true man is the one who discharges the trust and refrains from violating people's honor.'

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: شهد حرب الفرس بالحيرة فلما نزل روزبة قنطرة النهرين خرج إليهم عبيد بن منقذ فذكر القصة
records.english: He took part in the war against the Persians at al-Hira. When Ruzbih halted at the bridge of the two rivers, Ubayd ibn Munqidh went out against them; then he related the account.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: تابعي شهير يكنى أبا معاوية روى عن بن مسعود والمغيرة بن شعبة وسليمان بن صرد ومن التابعين عن علقمة ومسروق والسلماني وروى عنه إبراهيم النخعي وأشعث بن سليم وحمران بن اعين قال العجلي كوفي تابعي ثقة كان يقرىء أهل الكوفة وذكر بن حزم انه أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يلقه واخرج بن أبي شيبة في مسنده من طريق القاسم بن مخيمرة عن عبيد بن نضلة ان الناس قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في عام مجاعة سعر لنا الحديث قال العسكري ليس يصح سماعه وأكثر ظني انه مرسل وقد ذكره كذلك بن أبي حاتم وقال مختلف في صحبته سوى الحديث المرسل واما ادراكه فصحيح وعده على بن المديني في الفقهاء من أصحاب بن مسعود
records.english: a well-known Successor with the kunya Abu Muawiya. He related from Ibn Mas'ud, al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, and Sulayman ibn Surad, and, among the Successors, from Alqama, Masruq, and al-Salmani. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Ash'ath ibn Sulaym, and Humran ibn A'yan related from him. Al-Ijli said: 'A Kufan, a trustworthy Successor; he used to teach the people of Kufa to recite.' Ibn Hazm mentioned that he lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ but did not meet him. Ibn Abi Shayba related in his Musnad, by way of al-Qasim ibn Mukhaymira, from Ubayd ibn Nadla, that in a year of famine the people said to the Prophet ﷺ, 'Fix prices for us'—and then gave the hadith. Al-Askari said: 'His hearing [from the Prophet] is unsound, and I think it most likely disconnected.' Ibn Abi Hatim likewise mentioned him and said: 'His Companionship is disputed, apart from the disconnected hadith; as for his having lived in that time, it is sound.' Ali ibn al-Madini counted him among the jurists who were companions of Ibn Mas'ud.

records.arabic: له إدراك وهو من سبى خالد بن الوليد يأتي خبره في ترجمة يسار جد محمد بن إسحاق صاحب المغازي
records.english: He lived into the Islamic period and was among the captives taken by Khalid ibn al-Walid. His account will appear in the biography of Yasar, grandfather of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, the author of al-Maghazi.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: ذكر في ترجمة سميه في القسم الأول وذكره البخاري وابن حبان في التابعين
records.english: He was mentioned in the biography of his namesake in the first section. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban listed him among the Successors.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الذي كان ينسب اليه زياد بن سمية قبل ان يستخلفه معاوية ذكر بن الأعرابي ان أباه يونس بن عبيد خاصم معاوية في ذلك فذكر قصة طويلة وعبيد المذكور كان مولى الحارث بن كلدة فزوجه مولاه سمية فولدت له زيادا وغيره وذكر الغلابي في كتاب أخبار زياد بأسانيد له ان عمر كان وجه زيادا في وجه فقدم عليه وقد كفاه ما بعثه اليه فخطب خطبة بليغة وناظر عن أبي موسى وكان أبو موسى استكتبه لما ولي إمرة البصرة لعمر فرفعوا فيه إلى أبي موسى فكان زياد يحاجج عن أبي موشى فقال له عمر ما فعلت في أول شيء حصل لك من الكبر قال وجدت عبيدا أبي في الرق فاشتريته بألف فقال له عمر نعم الألف
records.english: to whom Ziyad ibn Sumayya had been ascribed before Mu'awiya acknowledged him as kin. Ibn al-A'rabi related that Ubayd's father, Yunus ibn Ubayd, disputed with Mu'awiya about this, and he gave a long account. The aforementioned Ubayd was a client of al-Harith ibn Kalada. His master married him to Sumayya, who bore him Ziyad and others. In The Reports of Ziyad, al-Ghallabi related with chains of his that Umar once sent Ziyad on a mission. He returned to Umar having accomplished what he had been sent to do, delivered an eloquent speech, and argued on behalf of Abu Musa. Abu Musa had taken him as secretary when Umar appointed him commander of Basra, and complaints about him had been raised to Abu Musa; Ziyad would argue on Abu Musa's behalf. Umar asked him, 'What did you do with the first thing that came to you from high office?' He replied, 'I found Ubayd, my father, in slavery, so I bought him for one thousand.' Umar said, 'An excellent thousand.'

records.arabic:
أحد بني طريف ذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء وأنشد له يخاطب مزرد بن ضرار الأسدي وهو أخو الشماخ وسيأتي ذكره في حرف الميم من أبيات فقال
فقلت تزردها عبيد فانني
لزرد الموالي في السنين مزرد فسمي لذلك مزردا وقال عبيد يجيبه
تركت ضرارا في الظهيرة رازما
فهلا ضرار أبا يزيد مزود
records.english:
one of Banu Tarif. Al-Marzubani mentioned him in the Dictionary of Poets and quoted verses in which Muzarrad ibn Dirar al-Asadi, brother of al-Shammakh—who will be discussed under the letter mim—addressed him, saying:
I said, 'Devour it, Ubayd, for indeed
for devouring clients in lean years I am Muzarrad.'
For that reason he was named Muzarrad. Ubayd replied to him:
You left Dirar at midday [the source word at this point remains unresolved];
why then, Dirar, is Abu Yazid not provisioned?

records.arabic: والد أبي حرة يأتي خبره في ترجمة وهب بن خالد
records.english: the father of Abu Hurra. His account will appear in the biography of Wahb ibn Khalid.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بفتح أوله وزيادة هاء بن عمرو ويقال بن قيس بن عمرو السلماني بفتح المهملة وسكون اللام وفتحها بعضهم قال بن الكلبي اسلم قبل وفاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بسنتين ولم يلقه وكذا قال العجلي وقال تابعي ثقة وقال الواقدي هاجر من اليمن زمن عمر ونزل الكوفة وروى عن بن مسعود وعلي روى عنه محمد بن سيرين وأبو إسحاق السبيعي وإبراهيم النخعي والشعبي وأبو حسان الأعرج وغيرهم وكان بن سيرين أروى الناس عنه وقد ذكر على بن المديني والعلاس ان أصح الأسانيد بن سيرين عن عبيدة عن علي وقال بن نمير كان شريح إذا اشكل عليه شيء كتب إلى عبيدة مات سنة اثنتين وسبعين وأرخ الترمذي سنة ثلاث وابن أبي شيبة سنة أربع وفي كل ذلك نظر بينت وجهه في مختصر التهذيب
records.english: with a fathah on its first letter and an added ha—ibn Amr, also said to be ibn Qays ibn Amr, al-Salmani, with fatha on the unpointed letter and sukun on the lam, though some read the lam with fatha. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he accepted Islam two years before the death of the Prophet ﷺ but did not meet him. Al-Ijli said the same, adding: 'A trustworthy Successor.' Al-Waqidi said that he emigrated from Yemen in Umar's time and settled in Kufa. He related from Ibn Mas'ud and Ali. Muhammad ibn Sirin, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Abu Hassan al-A'raj, and others related from him. Ibn Sirin was the person who related most from him. Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Allas stated that the soundest chain is Ibn Sirin, from Abida, from Ali. Ibn Numayr said: 'Whenever a matter was difficult for Shurayh, he wrote to Abida.' He died in 72 AH; al-Tirmidhi dated his death to 73, and Ibn Abi Shayba to 74. There is evident difficulty in all of that, whose basis I explained in Mukhtasar al-Tahdhib.

aliases: Abida ibn Qays ibn Amr al-Salmani

records.arabic: مولى أبي بكر الصديق يأتي في القسم الأخير
records.english: the client of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. He will appear in the final section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: له إدراك لان عمر قبل شهادته على قدامة بن مظعون حين شرب الخمر أخرجه بن أبي شيبة من وجهين وسيأتي ذكر القصة واضحا في ترجمة أمه ان شاء الله تعالى
records.english: He lived into the Islamic period, because Umar accepted his testimony against Qudama ibn Maz'un when Qudama drank wine. Ibn Abi Shayba transmitted it by two routes. The account will be stated clearly in the biography of his mother, ان شاء الله تعالى.

heading.english: The letter ʿayn followed by tāʾ

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: حليف بني عصمة شهد اليرموك أميرا قاله سيف في الفتوح قال وأمره خالد بن الوليد على بعض الكراديس قال بن عساكر أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا اعرف له رواية استدركه بن فتحون
records.english: an ally of Banu Isma. He witnessed al-Yarmuk as a commander, according to Sayf in The Conquests, who said that Khalid ibn al-Walid appointed him over one of the battalions. Ibn Asakir said: 'He lived during the time of the Prophet ﷺ, but I know of no transmission from him.' Ibn Fathun added him as an omission.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
له إدراك وله مع عثمان خبر في عزل سعيد بن العاص وولاية الأشعري وله قصص مع على ويقال انه القائل في يوم صفين
لمن راية سوداء يخفق ظلها
إذا ما قيل قدمها حصين تقدما
records.english:
He lived into the Islamic period. He has an account with Uthman concerning the dismissal of Sa'id ibn al-As and the appointment of al-Ash'ari, and accounts with Ali. It is said that he was the one who said on the day of Siffin:
Whose black banner is it, its shadow fluttering?
Whenever it was said, 'Advance it,' Husayn advanced.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: قال بن منده ذكر فيمن أدرك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وآوله وسلم روى عنه طارق بن شهاب ولا يصح له صحبة
records.english: Ibn Manda said: 'He was mentioned among those who lived during the time of the Prophet ﵌. Tariq ibn Shihab related from him, but Companionship is not soundly established for him.'

formulas.observedArabic: صلى الله عليه وسلم وآوله وسلم

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بمثناة وموحدة مصغر بن عتيبة بن مرداس التميمي بن الحارث بن مدرك الدهماني ذكره أبو القاسم الحسن بن بشر الآمدي وانه شهد حنينا مع المشركين وأنشد له شعرا يمدح مالك بن عوف رأس القوم في تلك الوقعة وفي أثناء ذلك الشعر ما يدل على انه اسلم بعد ذلك ولم أقف على خبر صحيح بأنه صحابي فذكرته في هذا القسم ونبهت عليه في الأول من قصيدته المذكورة ما نقلته من خط الحافظ أبي بكر الخطيب
واذكر مسيرهم للناس إذ جمعوا
وملك حوله الرايات تختفق
ومالك مالك ما فوقه أحد
وافى حنينا عليه التاج يأتلق
في كل جأواء جمهور مسومة
يعني إذا هي سارت دونها الحدق
وقيس عيلان طرا تحت رايته
ان سار ساروا وان لاقى بهم صدقوا
فضاربوا الناس حتى لم يروا أحدا
حول النبي إلى ان جنه الغسق
ثمة نزل جبريل بنصرهم
من السماء فمهزوم ومعتنق
منا ولو غير جبريل يقاتلنا
لمنعتنا اذن اسيافنا العتق
وفاتنا عمر الفاروق إذ هزموا
بطعنة بل منها سرجه العلق قال أبو الفرج الأصبهاني شاعر مقل مخضرم أدرك الجاهلية والإسلام وكان هجاء وأنشد له شعرا رثى به قومه
records.english:
with a ta and a ba, in diminutive form—ibn Utayba ibn Mirdas al-Tamimi ibn al-Harith ibn Mudrik al-Dahmani. Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Amidi mentioned him and said that he witnessed Hunayn with the polytheists. He quoted poetry in which Utayba praised Malik ibn Awf, the leader of the people in that battle. Within the poem is material indicating that he subsequently accepted Islam. I have not found a sound report that he was a Companion, so I have placed him in this section and called attention to him in the first. From his aforementioned poem, copied from the handwriting of the hadith master Abu Bakr al-Khatib:
Remember their march against the people when they gathered,
with a king around whom the banners fluttered;
Malik—what a Malik! No one stood above him—
came to Hunayn, a crown gleaming upon him,
amid every dark, teeming, marked host,
so vast that, when it marched, eyes could not see beyond it;
and all of Qays Aylan beneath his banner:
if he marched, they marched; if he met the foe with them, they held true.
They fought the people until they saw no one
around the Prophet, until dusk covered him.
Then Gabriel descended from heaven to aid them,
so among us one was routed and another seized.
Had anyone other than Gabriel fought us,
our ancient swords would then have protected us.
Umar al-Faruq escaped us when they were routed,
by a thrust—indeed, his saddlecloth was bloodied by it.
Abu al-Faraj al-Isbahani said: 'A mukhadram poet of small output. He lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods and composed invective.' He also quoted poetry in which Utayba elegized his people.

aliases: Utayba ibn Utayba ibn Mirdas al-Tamimi ibn al-Harith ibn Mudrik al-Dahmani

names.arabic: أبو القاسم الحسن بن بشر الآمدي
names.english: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Amidi

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: بنون ومهملة العجلي واسم النهاس عبدل بن حنظلة بن يام بتحتانية بن الحارث كان من كبار العجليين له إدراك ومشاهد في خلافة أبي بكر قال بن ماكولا كان شريفا وكان مع خالد بن الوليد باليمامة واستعمله على اللهازم حين سار إلى فاطمة وكذا ذكره سيف في الفتوح وقال من الكماة الشجعان وذكره الطبري أيضا وان العلاء بن الحضرمي أرسل اليه في أمر الردة وأخوه عتاب كان شريفا وابنه المغيرة بن عتبة كان قاضي الكوفة استدركه بن فتحون تردد هل هو كذا أو بالتحتانية والنون والأول اصوب
records.english: with a nun and an unpointed consonant, al-Ijli. Al-Nahhas's name was Abdal ibn Hanzala ibn Yam—with a letter dotted below—ibn al-Harith. He was one of the leading men of Ijl, lived into the Islamic period, and took part in campaigns during Abu Bakr's caliphate. Ibn Makula said that he was a nobleman. He was with Khalid ibn al-Walid at al-Yamama, and Khalid appointed him over al-Lahazim when he marched to Fatima. Sayf likewise mentioned him in The Conquests and said that he was one of the brave champions. Al-Tabari also mentioned him and said that al-Ala ibn al-Hadrami sent to him concerning the Ridda. His brother Attab was a nobleman, and his son al-Mughira ibn Utba was judge of Kufa. Ibn Fathun added him as an omission and hesitated whether the name had this spelling or one with the letter dotted below and nun; the former is more correct.

aliases: Abdal ibn Hanzala ibn Yam ibn al-Harith

records.arabic:
ممن ثبت على إسلامه في زمن الردة ذكره وثيمة عن بن إسحاق وأنشد له في ذلك يخاطب الأشعث
ان تمس كندة ناكثين عهودهم
فالله يعلم انني لم انكث
لا تبغ الا الدين دينا واحدا
خذها ولا تردد نصيحة عثعث واستدركه بن فتون
records.english:
among those who remained firm in Islam during the apostasy. Wathima mentioned him from Ibn Ishaq and quoted him addressing al-Ash'ath in that connection:
Though Kinda pass the night breaking their covenants,
God knows that I did not break mine.
Seek no religion but the one true religion;
take this, and do not reject Uth'uth's sincere counsel.
Ibn Fathun added him as an omission.

records.english: the rajaz poet; he is said to have lived into the Islamic period. He was discussed above among those named Abd Allah.

records.arabic:
بن زبان بن عمرو بن سلسلة بن غنم بن ثوب بن معن الطائي المعنى الشاعر يعرف بالاعرج قال بن الكلبي جاهلي إسلامي وهو القائل
تركت الشعر واستبدلت منه
إذا داعي صلاة الصبح قاما
كتاب الله ليس له شريك
وودعت المدامة والندامى قد تقدم في سويد بن عدي بن عمرو وحكى المرزباني القولين وأنشد البيتين المذكورين في الترجمتين واقتصر بن الكلبي على الذي هنا والله اعلم
records.english:
son of Zabban ibn Amr ibn Silsila ibn Ghanm ibn Thawb ibn Ma'n al-Ta'i al-Ma'ni, the poet known as al-A'raj. Ibn al-Kalbi said: 'He belonged to both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods.' He is the one who said:
I abandoned poetry and took in its place,
whenever the caller to the dawn prayer arose,
the Book of God, which has no partner;
and I bade farewell to wine and drinking companions.
He was discussed above under Suwayd ibn Adi ibn Amr. Al-Marzubani reported both views and quoted these two verses in both biographies, while Ibn al-Kalbi gave only the person listed here. والله أعلم.

names.arabic: عدي بن عمرو بن سويد بن زبان بن عمرو بن سلسلة بن غنم بن ثوب بن معن الطائي المعنى
names.english: Adi ibn Amr ibn Suwayd ibn Zaban ibn Amr ibn Silsila ibn Ghanm ibn Thawb ibn Ma'n al-Ta'i al-Ma'ni

records.arabic: أرسله أبو بكر الصديق إلى ملك الروم تقدم في القسم الأول
records.english: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq sent him to the ruler of the Byzantines. He was discussed above in the first section.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic:
بن حارثة بن لام الطائي أحد الشعراء المعمرين وهو القائل
ووالله ما أدري أأدركت امة
على عهد ذي القرنين أم كنت اقدما
متى تنزعا عنى القميص تبينا
جآجيء لم يكسين لحما ولا دما ذكره العسكري في التصحيف وضبطه بالعين والراء المهملتين وقال أبو حاتم السجستاني في المعمرين عوام أو عرام عاش إلى ان دخل على عمر بن عبد العزيز ليزمن ان يكتب في الزمنى فقال له عمر ما زمانتك هذه فذكر البيتين حكاه عن بن الكلبي عن رجل من بني قيس بن حارثة عنه وهو في الجمهرة بنحوه بلا سند وقال في روايته فقال له عمر أيها الشيخ من أدركت فانشدهما وذكره المرزباني فسماه عراما كما قال العسكري وقال انه مخضرم نزل الكوفة وجزم أبو محنف انه عوام بواو وذكر له نحو ما تقدم
records.english:
son of Haritha ibn Lam al-Tai, one of the exceptionally long-lived poets. He is the one who said:
By God, I do not know whether I lived to see a nation
in the age of Dhu al-Qarnayn, or whether I was earlier still.
When this shirt is pulled away from me, there appear
ribs that have not been clothed in flesh or blood.
Al-Askari mentioned him in al-Tashif, vocalized the name with the unpointed ayn and ra, and said: Abu Hatim al-Sijistani stated in al-Mu'ammarin that 'Awwam—or Arram—lived until he came before Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz to have him register him among the chronically disabled. Umar asked him, 'What is this chronic disability of yours?' and he recited the two verses. He reported this from Ibn al-Kalbi, from a man of Banu Qays ibn Haritha, from Arram. It appears similarly in al-Jamhara without a chain. In its version Umar asked him, 'Old man, whom did you live to see?' and he recited them. Al-Marzubani also mentioned him, naming him Arram as al-Askari did, and said that he was a mukhadram who settled in Kufa. Abu Mikhnaf firmly stated that he was Awwam, with a waw, and gave an account similar to the foregoing.

names.arabic: عرام بن المنذر بن حارثة بن لام الطائي
names.english: Arram ibn al-Mundhir ibn Haritha ibn Lam al-Ta'i

records.arabic: روى أبو عون الثقفي عن عرفجة السلمي عن أبي بكر الصديق حديثا ولعله عرفجة بن شريح الكندي والظاهر انه غيره
records.english: Abu Awn al-Thaqafi narrated from Arfaja al-Sulami, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Perhaps he is Arfaja ibn Shurayh al-Kindi, though it appears that he is someone else.

records.arabic: تقدم في الأول

records.arabic: بن شريح بن سعد بن حارثة بن لام الطائي له إدراك وشهد قتال الخوارج مع علي فقال علي لا يفلت منهم واحد ولا يقتلون منا عشرة فكان كذلك وكان عروة فيمن قتل من العشرة
records.english: son of Shurayh ibn Sad ibn Haritha ibn Lam al-Tai. He lived into the Islamic period and joined Ali in fighting the Kharijites. Ali said: 'Not one of them will escape, and they will not kill ten of us.' So it happened, and Urwa was among the ten who were killed.

names.arabic: عروة بن افاف بن شريح بن سعد بن حارثة بن لام الطائي
names.english: Urwa ibn Afaf ibn Shurayh ibn Sa'd ibn Haritha ibn Lam al-Ta'i

records.english: al-Ṭāʾī. He was discussed above in the first section.

records.arabic: بن أبي الجعد البارقي ذكره بن عبد البر وكان استعمله عمر على قضاء الكوفة وضم اليه سلمان بن ربيعة قبل ان يستقضي شريحا قلت ان كان محفوظا فهو بن أخي عروة بن أبي الجعد الماضي في القسم الأول ومنهم من حزم بأنه هو ثم اختلفوا فقيل ان الصواب في عروة بن أبي الجعد انه عروة بن عياض وانه نسب إلى جده وهذا قول الرشاطي ومنهم من قال بل عياض اسم أبي الجعد فعلى هذا يقرأ عياض باعراب عروة
records.english: ibn Abī al-Jaʿd al-Bāriqī. Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned him and said that Umar appointed him to the judgeship of Kufa and attached Salman ibn Rabi'a to him before appointing Shurayh as judge. I say: if this is accurately preserved, he is the nephew of Urwa ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who appeared above in the first section. Some have firmly asserted that he is that same man. They then disagreed: it was said that the correct form for Urwa ibn Abi al-Ja'd is Urwa ibn Iyad, and that he was ascribed to his grandfather; this is al-Rushati's view. Others said that Iyad was the name of Abu al-Ja'd. On that view, Iyad is read with the same grammatical case as Urwa.

names.arabic: عروة بن عياش بن أبي الجعد البارقي
names.english: Urwa ibn Ayyash ibn Abi al-Ja'd al-Bariqi

records.arabic:
بن عمرو بن فعاس بن عبد يغوث بن محدش بن عصر بن غنم بن مالك بن عوف بن منبه بن غطيف المرادي ثم الغطفي له إدراك وكان ابنه هانئ بن عروة من رؤساء أهل الكوفة وهو الذي نزل مسلم بن عقيل بن أبي طالب عنده لما أرسله الحسين بن على لأخذ البيعة على أهل الكوفة فقبض عبد الله بن زياد عليهما فقتلهما وفي ذلك يقول الشاعر
فان كنت لا تدرين ما الموت فانظري
إلى هانئ في السوق وابن عقيل ذكره بن الكلبي
records.english:
ibn ʿAmr ibn Faʿʿās ibn Abd Yaghuth ibn Muhaddish ibn Asr ibn Ghanm ibn Malik ibn Awf ibn Munabbih ibn Ghatif al-Muradi, then al-Ghatifi. He lived into the Islamic period. His son Hani ibn Urwa was one of the leaders of the people of Kufa. Muslim ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib stayed with him when al-Husayn ibn Ali sent Muslim to take the oath of allegiance from the people of Kufa. Ubayd Allah ibn Ziyad arrested the two of them and killed them. Concerning that, the poet said:
If you do not know what death is, then look
at Hani in the marketplace and Ibn Aqil.
Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned him.

names.arabic: عروة بن نمران بن عمرو بن فعاس بن عبد يغوث بن محدش بن عصر بن غنم بن مالك بن عوف بن منبه بن غطيف المرادي
names.english: Urwa ibn Numran ibn Amr ibn Fu'as ibn Abd Yaghuth ibn Muhaddish ibn Asr ibn Ghanm ibn Malik ibn Awf ibn Munabbih ibn Ghatif al-Muradi

names.arabic: مسلم بن عقيل بن أبي طالب
names.english: Muslim ibn Aqil ibn Abi Talib

records.arabic:
بن مقاتل الأسدي المقعسي ذكره المرزباني فقال مخضرم أدرك الجاهلية والإسلام وهو القائل
نحن الذين اغتصبنا الناس كلهم
حتى اهتدى طائع منهم ومعشور
حتى أقاموا قناة الدين واعتدلوا
فالسيف عبد وقلب القوم مشهور
records.english:
ibn Muqātil al-Asadī al-Muq'asi. Al-Marzubani mentioned him and said: 'A mukhadram who lived in both the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods.' He is the one who said:
We are those who wrested all the people,
until among them the willing and [a source word of unresolved sense] were guided;
until they set the shaft of religion upright and became straight—
so the sword is a slave, and the people's heart is unsheathed [the relation of this metaphor remains uncertain].

names.arabic: عروس بن المفترس بن مقاتل الأسدي المقعسي
names.english: Arus ibn al-Muftaris ibn Muqatil al-Asadi al-Muq'asi

records.arabic: بن عريب بن ليشرح الحميري ذكر بن الكلبي ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتب اليه والى أخيه الحارث وكان إليهما أمر حمير وقد تقدم الحارث وشرحبيل أخواه وذكر بن إسحاق ان الكتاب كان إلى أخيه ولم يذكر هذا
records.english: ibn ʿArīb ibn Layashraḥ al-Himyari. Ibn al-Kalbi related that the Prophet ﷺ wrote to him and to his brother al-Harith; authority over Himyar belonged to the two of them. His brothers al-Harith and Shurahbil were discussed above. Ibn Ishaq related that the letter was addressed to his brother but did not mention this man.

names.arabic: عريب بن عبد كلال بن عريب بن ليشرح الحميري
names.english: Arib ibn Abd Kulal ibn Arib ibn Li-Yashrah al-Himyari

records.arabic: بن غزية الأحمسي البجلي وسكن حلوان في عهد عمر روى عنه أبو وائل قال الأعمش عن أبي وائل عن عزرة بن قيس خطبنا خالد بن الوليد فقال ان عمر بعثني إلى الشام الحديث في الفتن وفيه قول خالد انها لا تكون وعمر حي قال علي بن المديني لم يرو عنه غير أبي وائل وقال بن أبي خيثمة عن بن معين بقي إلى أيام معاوية فيما بلغني وذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الأولى
records.english: ibn Ghaziyyah al-Aḥmasī al-Bajalī. He settled in Hulwan during Umar's reign. Abu Wa'il related from him. Al-A'mash related from Abu Wa'il, from Azra ibn Qays: 'Khalid ibn al-Walid preached to us and said, “Umar sent me to Syria...”'—the hadith concerning tribulations, which includes Khalid's statement that they would not occur while Umar was alive. Ali ibn al-Madini said that no one other than Abu Wa'il related from him. Ibn Abi Khaythama related from Ibn Ma'in: 'He remained alive into Mu'awiya's days, according to what has reached me.' Ibn Sa'd listed him in the first generation.

names.arabic: عزرة بن قيس بن غزية الأحمسي البجلي
names.english: Azra ibn Qays ibn Ghaziya al-Ahmasi al-Bajali

heading.english: The letter ʿayn followed by zāy

records.arabic:
الحميري أحد المعمرين كان ممن بشر برسالة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثم أدرك البعثة وأرسل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بشعر يمدحه ويذكر فيه إسلامه ولم يبلغنا انه هاجر روى حديثه البلوي عن عمارة بن زيد عن عبد الله بن العلاء عن عبد الرحمن بن حميد بن عبد الرحمن قال كان حميد بن عبد الرحمن يقول سمعت أبي يقول سافرت إلى اليمن قبل المبعث بسنة فنزلت على عسكلان بن عواكن الحميري وكان شيخا كبيرا قد انسىء له في العمر حتى عاد كالفرخ وهو يقول
إذا ما الشيخ صم فلم يكلم
واودى سمعه الا يدايا
فذاك الداء ليس له دواء
سوى الموت المنطق بالرزايا
شهدت بنا مع الاملاك منا
وادركت المواقف في القضايا
فبادوا أجمعين فصرت حلسا
صريعا لا ابوح إلى الخلايا قال عبد الرحمن وكنت إذا قدمت نزلت عليه فلا يزال يسألني عن مكة واحوالها وهل ظهر فيها من خالف دينهم أو لا حتى قدمت القدمة التي بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وانا غائب فيها فنزلت عليه فقعد وقد شد عصابة على عينيه فقال لي انتسب يا أخا قريش فقلت انا عبد الرحمن بن عوف بن عبد عوف بن عبد الحارث بن زهرة قال حسبك قال الا أبشرك ببشارة وهي خير لك من التجارة قلت بلى قال اتيتك بالمعجبة وابشرك بالمرغبة ان الله قد بعث في الشهر الأول من قومك نبيا ارتضاه صفيا وانزل عليه كتابا وفيا ينهى عن الأصنام ويدعو إلى الإسلام يأمر بالحق ويفعله وينهى عن الباطل ويبطله وهو من بني هاشم وان قومك لاخواله يا عبد الرحمن وازره وصدقه واحمل اليه هذه الأبيات
اشهد بالله ذي المعالي
وفالق الليل والصباح
انك في السر من قريش
وابن المفدى من الذباح
أرسلت تدعو إلى يقين
ترشد للحق والفلاح
هد كرور السنين ركنى
عن مكر السير والرواح
اشهد بالله رب موسى
انك أرسلت بالبطاح
فكن شفيعي إلى مليك
يدعو البرايا إلى الصلاح قال عبد الرحمن فقدمت فلقيت أبا بكر وكان لي خليطا فأخبرته الخبر فقال هذا محمد بن عبد الله بعثه الله إلى خلقه رسولا فأته فأتيته وهو في بيت خديجة فأخبرته فقال اما ان أخا حمير من خواص المؤمنين ورب مؤمن بي ولم يرني ومصدق لي وما شهدني أولئك إخواني حقا أخرجه بن عساكر في تاريخه الكبير من هذا الوجه والبلوي ضعيف وراويه عنه عمر بن مدرك اتهمه يحيى بن معين
records.english:
al-Ḥimyarī, one of the exceptionally long-lived. He was among those who gave glad tidings of the message of the Prophet ﷺ; he then lived to see the commissioning and sent the Prophet ﷺ a poem praising him and mentioning his own acceptance of Islam. No report has reached us that he emigrated. Al-Balawi transmitted his account from Umara ibn Zayd, from Abd Allah ibn al-Ala, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman used to say, 'I heard my father say: I traveled to Yemen one year before the commissioning and stayed with Askalan ibn Awakin al-Himyari. He was a very old man whose life had been prolonged until he had become like a fledgling. He was saying:
When an old man becomes deaf and cannot speak,
and his hearing has perished except [an unresolved source reading],
that is the illness for which there is no cure
except death, which gives voice to calamities.
I witnessed [an unresolved source reading] with kings from among us,
and I lived through the stations in momentous affairs.
They all perished, and I became like a worn saddlecloth,
cast down, not going forth to the chambers.
Abd al-Rahman said: Whenever I came, I stayed with him, and he would keep asking me about Mecca and its conditions, and whether anyone had appeared there who opposed their religion. Then I came on the visit during which the Prophet ﷺ had been commissioned while I was away. I stayed with him. He sat up, having tied a band over his eyes, and said to me, “Tell me your lineage, brother of Quraysh.” I said, “I am Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf ibn Abd Awf ibn Abd al-Harith ibn Zuhra.” He said, “Enough.” Then he said: “Shall I give you glad tidings, better for you than commerce?” I said, “Yes.” He said: “I bring you the wondrous thing and give you the desired glad tidings. In the first month, God sent forth from your people a Prophet whom He approved as a chosen one, and He sent down to him a faithful Book. He forbids idols and calls to Islam; he commands truth and practices it, and forbids falsehood and abolishes it. He is of Banu Hashim, and your people are his maternal uncles, O Abd al-Rahman. Support him, affirm him, and carry these verses to him:
I bear witness by God, Possessor of the heights
and Splitter of the night and morning,
that you are of the pure stock of Quraysh,
and the son of the one ransomed from slaughter.
You were sent to call to certainty,
guiding to truth and success.
The passing of years has weakened my pillar,
through the repeated cunning of journeying and return.
I bear witness by God, the Lord of Moses,
that you were sent in al-Bitah.
So be my intercessor before a Sovereign
who calls created beings to righteousness.”
Abd al-Rahman said: I returned and met Abu Bakr, who was my close associate, and told him the news. He said: “This is Muhammad ibn Abd Allah; God has sent him as a messenger to His creation, so go to him.” I went to him while he was in Khadija's house and told him. He said: “Indeed, the brother from Himyar is one of the elect among the believers. Many a person believes in me without seeing me and affirms me without witnessing me; those are truly my brothers.” Ibn Asakir transmitted it in his Great History by this route. Al-Balawi is weak, and his transmitter Umar ibn Mudrik was accused by Yahya ibn Ma'in.'

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن حميد بن عبد الرحمن
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن عوف بن عبد عوف بن عبد الحارث بن زهرة
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf ibn Abd Awf ibn Abd al-Harith ibn Zuhra

heading.english: The letter ʿayn followed by sīn
