records.arabic: بن عمرو بن الجعد بن عوف بن مبذول بن عمرو بن غنم بن مازن الأنصاري شهد أحدا واستشهد باليمامة قاله العدوي قال وهو أخو أبي عبيد واستدركه بن فتحون
records.english: son of ʿAmr ibn al-Jaʿd ibn ʿAwf ibn Mabdhul ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghanm ibn Mazin al-Ansari. He witnessed Uhud and was martyred at al-Yamamah, as stated by al-ʿAdawi, who said that he was the brother of Abu ʿUbayd. Ibn Fathun added him in his supplement.

records.english: son of Jarthūmah, al-Nahdī. Sayf and al-Tabari mentioned that Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas placed him in command of his men from Banu Nahd during the conquest of al-Qadisiyyah. Ibn Fathun added him in his supplement. It has been stated repeatedly that they appointed only Companions to commands during the conquests.

names.arabic: قيس بن حذيم بن جرثومه النهدي
names.english: Qays ibn Hudhaym ibn Jarthumah al-Nahdi

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي في الصحابة ونقل عن البخاري انه ذكره فيهم قال روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ولم يذكره قلت وقد تقدم حديثه في ترجمة أخيه عبد الله بن الخشخاش وانه بمعجمات وذكره بن شاهين بالمهملات وقال بن حبان يقال ان له صحبة
records.english: Al-Baghawī listed him among the Companions and reported that al-Bukhari also listed him among them, saying, “He narrated from the Prophet ﷺ,” but did not mention a report from him. I say: his hadith appeared earlier in the entry on his brother ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Khashkhash, with the letters dotted. Ibn Shahin wrote the name with undotted letters. Ibn Hibban said that he is said to have had Companionship.

records.english: son of Qays ibn ʿAmr, al-Jaʿdī, known as al-Nabighah. Ibn Qaniʿ gave his lineage in this form. His entry will appear among the kunyahs.

names.arabic: قيس بن حصين بن قيس بن عمرو الجعدي
names.english: Qays ibn Husayn ibn Qays ibn ʿAmr al-Jaʿdi

records.arabic: بن يزيد بن شداد بن قنان ذي الغصة المازني وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قاله بن إسحاق وقال بن حبان والدارقطني له صحبة وهو من مذحج واخرج بن شاهين من طريق المدائني عن أبي معشر عن يزيد بن رومان ومسلمة بن علقمة عن خالد بن الحذاء عن أبي قلابة وعن أبي ريحانة وغيرهم قالوا اسلم بنو الحارث فاوفدهم خالد بن الوليد ومنهم قيس بن الحصين ذي الغصة ويزيد بن عبد المدان وعبد الله بن عبد المدان وشداد بن عبد الله وعبد الله بن قراد ويزيد بن المحجل وعمرو بن عبد الله قال وقال بعضهم لما وفدوا وشهدوا شهادة الحق قال لهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما الذي تغلبون به الناس وتقهرونهم قالوا لم نقل فنذل ولم نكثر فنتحاسد ونتخاذل ونجتمع ولا نفترق ولا نبدأ بظلم أحد ونصبر عند البأس فقال صدقت وذكرها بن إسحاق في المغازي بغير هذا السياق كما سيأتي في ترجمة يزيد بن عبد المدان وقال بن الكلبي رأس الحصين والد قيس بني الحارث مائة سنة وكان له أربعة أولاد كان يقال لهم فوارس الارباع كانوا إذا حضر الحرب ولى كل منهم ربعها ولما وفد قيس كتب له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كتابا على قومه
records.english: son of Yazīd ibn Shaddad ibn Qanan Dhu al-Ghussah al-Mazini. He came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, as stated by Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Hibban and al-Daraqutni said that he had Companionship and was from Madhhij. Ibn Shahin transmitted through al-Madaʾini, from Abu Maʿshar, from Yazid ibn Ruman; and from Maslamah ibn ʿAlqamah, from Khalid al-Hadhdhaʾ, from Abu Qilabah; and from Abu Rayhanah and others, who said: “Banu al-Harith accepted Islam, so Khalid ibn al-Walid sent a delegation from among them. They included Qays ibn al-Husayn Dhu al-Ghussah, Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Madan, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Madan, Shaddad ibn ʿAbd Allah, ʿAbd Allah ibn Qurad, Yazid ibn al-Muhajjal, and ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allah.” Some said that when they came as a delegation and testified to the true testimony, the Prophet ﷺ asked them, “By what do you prevail over and subdue other people?” They replied, “We have not been few, lest we be humbled; nor numerous, lest we envy and abandon one another. We unite and do not divide, do not begin by wronging anyone, and remain steadfast in hardship.” He said, “You have spoken truthfully.” Ibn Ishaq mentioned this in al-Maghazi with a different wording, as will appear in the entry on Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Madan. Ibn al-Kalbi said that al-Husayn, Qays’s father and the chief of Banu al-Harith, lived one hundred years. He had four sons known as the horsemen of the four quarters: when they attended battle, each took charge of one quarter. When Qays came as a delegate, the Prophet ﷺ wrote him a document granting authority over his people.

names.arabic: قيس بن الحصين بن يزيد بن شداد بن قنان ذي الغصة المازني
names.english: Qays ibn al-Husayn ibn Yazid ibn Shaddad ibn Qanan Dhu al-Ghussah al-Mazini

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي والباوردي والطبراني في الصحابة وقال البغوي لا أدري له صحبة أم لا واخرج هو ومطين وغيرهما من طريق بقية عن سليم بن دالان عن الأوزاعي عن عبادة بن نمى عن قيس بن خارجة قال نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الاغلوطات
records.english: Al-Baghawī, al-Bāwardī, and al-Ṭabarānī listed him among the Companions. Al-Baghawi said, “I do not know whether or not he had Companionship.” He, Mutayyan, and others transmitted through Baqiyyah, from Sulaym ibn Dalan, from al-Awzaʿi, from ʿUbadah ibn Numayy, from Qays ibn Kharijah, who said, “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade riddling questions.”

records.english: Al-Rāzī; al-Wāqidī said that he witnessed al-ʿAqabah and Badr. This is how it appears in al-Tajrid.

records.arabic: القيسي من بني قيس بن ثعلبة ذكره الطبراني وغير واحد في الصحابة قال أبو عمر له صحبة واخرج الحسن بن سفيان في مسنده من طريق حرملة بن عمران قال سمعت يزيد بن أبي حبيب يحدث محمد بن يزيد بن زياد الثقفي قال اصطحب قيس بن خرشة وكعب ذو الكتابين حتى إذا بلغا صفين وقف كعب ساعة فقال لا اله الا الله ليهراقن بهذه البقعة من دماء المسلمين شيء لا يهراقه ببقعة من الأرض الحديث فقال محمد بن يزيد ومن قيس بن خرشة فقال له رجل من قيس أو ما تعرفه وهو رجل من أهل بلادك قال لا قال فان قيس بن خرشة وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أبايعك على ما جاءك من الله وعلى ان أقول الحق فقال عسى ان يكون عليك من لا تقدر ان تقوم معه بالحق فقال قيس والله لا أبايعك على شيء الا وفيت لك به فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا لا يضرك شيء قال فكان قيس يعيب زيادا وابنه عبد الله فأرسل اليه عبيد الله فقال أأنت الذي تزعم انه لن يضرك شيء قال نعم قال لتعلمن اليوم انك قد كذبت ائتوني بصاحب العذاب قال فمال قيس عند ذلك فمات رجاله ثقات لكن في السند انقطاع ورجل لم يسم وأخرجه بن عبد البر من الوجه المذكور وفي رواية فغضب قيس ثم قال وما يدريك يا أبا إسحاق هذا من الغيب الذي استأثر الله به فقال كعب ما من شيء في الأرض الا وهو مكتوب في التوراة التي انزل الله على موسى ما يكون عليه إلى يوم القيامة فقال محمد بن يزيد ومن قيس فذكره وفيه فبلغ ذلك عبيد الله بن زياد فأرسل اليه فقال أنت الذي تفتري على الله وعلى رسوله قال لا والله ولكن ان شئت اخبرتك بمن يفترى قال ومن هو قال من ترك العمل بكتاب الله وسنة رسوله قال ومن ذاك قال أنت وأبوك ومن امركما وذكر بقية الحديث
records.english: Al-Qaysī, of Banū Qays ibn Thaʿlabah. Al-Tabarani and more than one other scholar listed him among the Companions. Abu ʿUmar said that he had Companionship. Al-Hasan ibn Sufyan transmitted in his Musnad through Harmalah ibn ʿImran, who said: “I heard Yazid ibn Abi Habib relate to Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Ziyad al-Thaqafi: Qays ibn Kharashah and Kaʿb, the man of the two scriptures, traveled together. When they reached Siffin, Kaʿb paused for a time and said, ‘There is no god but Allah! So much Muslim blood will be shed on this spot as will be shed nowhere else on earth,’” and he related the hadith. Muhammad ibn Yazid asked, “Who is Qays ibn Kharashah?” A man from Qays replied, “Do you not know him, though he is from your own land? Qays ibn Kharashah came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ and said, ‘I pledge allegiance to you concerning what has come to you from Allah and that I will speak the truth.’ He replied, ‘Someone over whom you have no power to uphold the truth may be placed in authority over you.’ Qays said, ‘By Allah, I will not pledge myself to anything for you unless I fulfill it.’ The Prophet ﷺ said, ‘Then nothing will harm you.’ Qays used to criticize Ziyad and his son ʿUbayd Allah. ʿUbayd Allah sent for him and said, ‘Are you the one who claims that nothing will harm you?’ He replied, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Today you will learn that you have lied. Bring me the torturer.’ At that, Qays collapsed and died.” Its narrators are trustworthy, but the chain is disconnected and contains an unnamed man. Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr transmitted it by the route just mentioned. Another version says that Qays became angry and said, “How do you know, Abu Ishaq? This belongs to the unseen that Allah has reserved to Himself.” Kaʿb replied, “There is nothing on earth except that what will happen to it until the Day of Resurrection is written in the Torah that Allah revealed to Moses.” Muhammad ibn Yazid asked who Qays was, and he related the report. It includes that the news reached ʿUbayd Allah ibn Ziyad, who sent for him and said, “Are you the one who fabricates lies against Allah and His Messenger?” He replied, “No, by Allah; but if you wish, I will tell you who does fabricate lies.” He asked, “Who is it?” Qays replied, “The one who abandons acting according to Allah’s Book and the practice of His Messenger.” He asked, “Who is that?” Qays replied, “You, your father, and the one who appointed you both,” and the rest of the hadith follows.

records.arabic: ذكر المبرد في الكامل بغير إسناد انه ممن شهد بدرا فذكر ان عليا دخل على فاطمة عليها السلام فرمى إليها بسيفه فقال هاكيه حميدا فسمعه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لئن كنت صدقت القتال لقد صدقه معك سماك بن خرشة وسهل بن حنيف والحارث بن الصمة وقيس بن الربيع وكل هؤلاء من الأنصار انتهى والحديث أخرجه وليس فيه ذكر قيس بن الربيع
records.english: Al-Mubarrad mentioned in al-Kāmil, without a chain, that he was among those who witnessed Badr. He related that ʿAli entered upon Fatimah عليها السلام, tossed his sword to her, and said, “Take it, praiseworthy.” The Prophet ﷺ heard him and said, “If you fought truly, then so did Simak ibn Kharashah, Sahl ibn Hunayf, al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, and Qays ibn al-Rabiʿ.” All of these men were Ansar. The hadith was transmitted, but Qays ibn al-Rabiʿ is not mentioned in it.

records.arabic:
آخر ذكره أبو موسى واخرج من طريقه حديثا كأنه موضوع فذكر من طريق علي بن موسى الرضا عن آبائه واحدا بعد واحد إلى علي قال بعث رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى حي من احياء العرب يقال لهم حي ذوي الاضغان بشيء ليقسم في فقرائهم فكان فيهم شيخ أسن يقال له قيس بن الربيع فأعطوه شيئا قليلا فغضب فهجا ثم جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معتذرا فأنشده
حي ذوي الاضغان تسب قلوبهم
تحيتك الحسنى وقد يدفع النغل
فان الذي يؤذيك منه سماعه
وان الذي قالوا وراءك لم يقل قال فطاب قلب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لحسن اعتذاره وقال له يا قيس لم تقل واقبل على اصحابه فقال من لم يقبل من متنصل عذرا صادقا أو كاذبا لم يرد على الحوض قال بن الأثير من أغرب ما فيه انه جعل حي ذوي الاضغان اسم قبيلة ومعنى البيت ظاهر لا يحتاج إلى شرح قلت هذا القدر هو المذكور من الخبر وهو قوله يقال لهم حي بني الاضغان وانما هذه الجملة من كلام الشيخ ناظم الأبيات فأمر من وقع منه أمر يوجب ان يحقد عليه ان يسلم على من يخشى منه ذلك ويحييه بالتحية الحسنى يزول ذلك واما أصل القصة فمحتمل وقد ذكر صاحب الجد والهزل وهو جعفر بن شاذان ان عامر بن الأزور أخا ضرار بن الأزور لما قدم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وآله استنشده فأنشده هذه الأبيات وذكر أهل السير في وفد بني أسد بن خزيمة ان حضرمي بن عامر انشد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنشده هذه الأبيات وبين البيتين المذكورين أولا وان دحسوا بالكره فاعف تكرما وان كتموا عنك الحديث فلا تسل وانشدها المرزباني للعلاء بن الحضرمي وزاد ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لما سمعه ان من البيان لسحرا
records.english: Another man of this name; Abū Mūsā mentioned him and transmitted through him a hadith that appears fabricated. He related through ʿAli ibn Musa al-Rida, from his forefathers one after another back to ʿAli, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent something to an Arab clan said to be the clan of ‘those bearing grudges,’ to be distributed among their poor. Among them was an elderly shaykh called Qays ibn al-Rabiʿ. They gave him very little, so he became angry and lampooned them. He then came to the Prophet ﷺ apologizing and recited: ‘Greet those bearing grudges openly with your finest greeting, / for a grudge may be driven away. / What harms you is what you hear from it, / while what they said behind your back was never said.’” The Prophet’s ﷺ heart was pleased by his fine apology, and he told him, “Qays, you did not say it.” He then turned to his Companions and said, “Whoever does not accept an apologist’s excuse, whether true or false, will not come to me at the Pool.” Ibn al-Athir said: “Among its strangest features is that he treated ‘the clan of those bearing grudges’ as the name of a tribe, although the meaning of the verse is plain and requires no explanation.” I say: this is all that is quoted of the report, including the words “said to be the clan of Banu ‘those bearing grudges.’” In fact, this phrase belongs to the speech of the old man who composed the verses. He instructed one whose action might cause another to harbor a grudge against him to greet the person he fears and offer a fine salutation, so that the grudge will disappear. The basis of the story remains possible. Jaʿfar ibn Shadhan, the author of al-Jidd wa-l-Hazl, mentioned that when ʿAmir ibn al-Azwar, brother of Dirar ibn al-Azwar, came to the Prophet ﵌, he asked him to recite poetry, and he recited these verses. The biographers, in their account of the delegation of Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah, stated that Hadrami ibn ʿAmir recited these verses to the Prophet ﷺ. Between the two verses first quoted was: “If they secretly bear hatred, graciously pardon them; / and if they conceal the matter from you, do not ask.” Al-Marzubani attributed them to al-ʿAlaʾ ibn al-Hadrami and added that when the Prophet ﷺ heard it, he said, “Some eloquence is indeed sorcery.”

records.arabic:
من بني واقف بن امرئ القيس بن مالك بن الأوس الأنصاري ذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء وقال اسلم وكان أعور وأنشد له
انا النذير لكم منى مجاهرة
كي لا الام على نهى وانذار
من يصل ناري بلا ذنب ولا ترة
يصلي بنار كريم غير غدار
records.english: of Banū Wāqif ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Malik ibn al-Aws al-Ansari. Al-Marzubani mentioned him in Muʿjam al-Shuʿaraʾ and said that he accepted Islam and was one-eyed. He cited these verses by him: “I openly warn you on my own behalf, / so I may not be blamed after counsel and warning. / Whoever kindles my fire without guilt or blood feud / will burn in the fire of a noble man who does not betray.”

records.arabic: بن عامر بن عائش بن نمير الأنصاري ذكره العدوي وقال كان شاعرا وأدرك الإسلام فاسلم وذكره بن الأثير فقال كان من شعراء العرب قلت يحتمل ان يكون الذي قبله واختلف في ضبط جده فقيل بنون وقيل بهاء
records.english: son of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAʾish ibn Numayr al-Ansari. Al-ʿAdawi mentioned him and said that he was a poet who lived to see Islam and accepted it. Ibn al-Athir mentioned him and said that he was one of the Arab poets. I say: he may be the preceding man. There is disagreement over the vocalization of his grandfather’s name, some giving it with nūn and others with hāʾ.

records.english: son of Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Dhibyan ibn ʿAwf ibn Anmar. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ and was a chief. The Prophet ﷺ invested him with a banner over Banu Saʿd ibn Malik. Al-Tabari likewise mentioned him, and Ibn Fathun and Ibn al-Amin added him in their supplements.

records.arabic: الجذامي وهو والد نائل بن قيس الشامي ويقال له قيس الأغر ذكره بن السكن في الصحابة فقال قيس بن عامر ويقال قيس بن زيد له صحبة وقال البخاري وابن حبان قيس الجذامي رجل كانت له صحبة وساق البخاري والبغوي من طريق كثير بن مرة عن قيس الجذامي رجل كانت له صحبة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعطى الشهيد ست خصال الحديث ووقع لابن أبي حاتم قيس الجذامي ليست له صحبة روى عنه عقبة بن عامر وغيره روى عنه كثير بن مرة وغيره كذا فيه ورأيت في نسخة على قوله ليست له صحبة والله اعلم قال أبو الحسن أحمد بن عمير بن جوصاء الحافظ حدثنا منصور بن الوليد بن سلمة بن يحيى أنبأنا الطفيل بن قيس الجذامي حدثني أبي عن أبيه يحيى عن أبيه أبي الطفيل عن أبيه قيس بن زيد بن جبار الجذامي انه وفد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فولاه الرياسة على قرية وساق إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صدقات بني سعد ثلاث مرات قال قيس فأجلسني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بين يديه ومسح على رأسي ودعا لي وقال بارك الله فيك يا قيس ثم قال أنت أبو الطفيل فهلك قيس وهو بن مائة سنة ورأسه أبيض واثر يد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيه اسود وكان يدعى لذلك قيسا الأغر وأخرجه بن منده عن الحسن عن أحمد بن عمير عن أبيه بطوله وأخرجه أبو علي بن السكن عن بن جوصاء باختصار وقد ذكره بن سعد فقال في طبقة أهل الفتح قيس بن زيد بن جبار بن امرئ القيس بن ثعلبة بن حبيب وساق النسب إلى جذام قال وكان سيدا عقد له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على قومه لما وفد عليه وكان ابنه نائل سيد جذام بالشام قلت والذي يظهر لي انه غير قيس الجذامي الذي اخرج له أحمد والنسائي وذكره البخاري وقال بن حبان سكن الشام وحديثه عند أهلها
records.english: Al-Judhāmī; he was the father of Nāʾil ibn Qays al-Shāmī; he was also called Qays al-Agharr. Ibn al-Sakan listed him among the Companions, saying, “Qays ibn ʿAmir, also called Qays ibn Zayd, had Companionship.” Al-Bukhari and Ibn Hibban said, “Qays al-Judhami was a man who had Companionship.” Al-Bukhari and al-Baghawi gave, through Kathir ibn Murrah, from Qays al-Judhami, a man who had Companionship, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “The martyr is granted six qualities...” to the end of the hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim has: “Qays al-Judhami did not have Companionship. ʿUqbah ibn ʿAmir and others narrated from him; Kathir ibn Murrah and others narrated from him.” This is how it appears, and I saw a mark in one copy over the words “did not have Companionship.” والله أعلم. Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn ʿUmayr ibn Jawsaʾ al-Hafiz said: Mansur ibn al-Walid ibn Salamah ibn Yahya related to us; al-Tufayl ibn Qays al-Judhami informed us; my father related to me, from his father Yahya, from his father Abu al-Tufayl, from his father Qays ibn Zayd ibn Jabbar al-Judhami, that he came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who placed him in charge of a village. Three times he drove the alms of Banu Saʿd to the Prophet ﷺ. Qays said, “The Prophet ﷺ seated me before him, passed his hand over my head, prayed for me, and said, ‘May Allah bless you, Qays.’ Then he said, ‘You are Abu al-Tufayl.’” Qays died at one hundred years of age. His head was white except that the mark of the hand of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon it remained black; for this reason he was called Qays al-Agharr. Ibn Mandah transmitted the report in full from al-Hasan, from Ahmad ibn ʿUmayr, from his father. Abu ʿAli Ibn al-Sakan transmitted it from Ibn Jawsaʾ in abbreviated form. Ibn Saʿd placed him among the generation of those present at the Conquest, saying: “Qays ibn Zayd ibn Jabbar ibn Imriʾ al-Qays ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Habib,” and continued his lineage to Judham. He said that Qays was a chief and that when he came as a delegation, the Prophet ﷺ invested him with authority over his people. His son Naʾil was chief of Judham in Syria. I say: it appears to me that he is someone other than the Qays al-Judhami whose hadith Ahmad and al-Nasaʾi transmitted, whom al-Bukhari mentioned and Ibn Hibban said settled in Syria; his hadith is known among the Syrians.

records.arabic: قتل بأحد ذكر بن إسحاق في السيرة الكبرى ان الحارث بن سويد كان منافقا وانه خرج مع المسلمين في غزوة أحد فلما التقى الناس غدا على المجذر بن زياد البلوي وقيس بن زيد أحد بني ضبيعة فقتلهما ولحق بمكة فساق قصته وكذا ذكره مكي القيرواني في تفسيره الهداية لكن بغير عزو إلى بن إسحاق ولا غيره وقد انكر بن هشام في تهذيب السيرة ذكر قيس بن زيد فيمن قتله الحارث واستدل على ذلك بأن بن إسحاق لم يذكر قيس بن زيد فيمن استشهد بأحد وهو استدلال عجيب فإنه يحتمل انه سها عن ذكره فيهم أو اقتصر على من استشهد بايدي الكفار وهذا إنما قتل غرة على من يدمن يظهر الإسلام واصل قصة نزول الآية أخرجه النسائي بسند صحيح عن بن عباس لكن لم يسم فيه قيس بن زيد والله اعلم
records.english: He was killed at Uḥud. Ibn Ishaq mentioned in al-Sirah al-Kubra that al-Harith ibn Suwayd was a hypocrite. He went out with the Muslims on the expedition of Uhud, and when battle was joined he attacked al-Mujadhdhar ibn Ziyad al-Balawi and Qays ibn Zayd of Banu Dubayʿah, killed them both, and joined the people of Mecca. Ibn Ishaq then related his story. Makki al-Qayrawani likewise mentioned it in his Tafsir al-Hidayah, though without attributing it to Ibn Ishaq or anyone else. Ibn Hisham, in his abridgment of the Sirah, rejected the mention of Qays ibn Zayd among those killed by al-Harith, arguing that Ibn Ishaq did not list Qays among those martyred at Uhud. This is a strange argument: Ibn Ishaq may have inadvertently omitted him, or may have limited his list to those martyred at the hands of unbelievers, whereas this man was treacherously killed by someone who outwardly professed Islam. The underlying account concerning the revelation of the verse was transmitted by al-Nasaʾi with a sound chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, but Qays ibn Zayd is not named in it. والله أعلم.

records.arabic: ويقال بن يزيد الجهني ذكره الطبراني في الصحابة واخرج من طريق جرير بن أيوب أحد الضعفاء عن الشعبي عن قيس بن زيد الجهني قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صام تطوعا غرست له نخلة في الجنة ثمرها أصغر من الرمان واشحم من التفاح الحديث
records.english: also called ibn Yazīd, al-Juhanī. Al-Tabarani listed him among the Companions and transmitted through Jarir ibn Ayyub, one of the weak narrators, from al-Shaʿbi, from Qays ibn Zayd al-Juhani, who said that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “For whoever observes a voluntary fast, a palm tree will be planted in Paradise whose fruit is smaller than a pomegranate and fleshier than an apple...” to the end of the hadith.

records.arabic: بن عويمر بن عائد بن عمران بن مخزوم وقيل في نسبه عبد الله بن عمر بدل عمران قال بن حبان له صحبة أمه رائطة بنت وهب بن عمرو بن عائذ بن عمران بن مخزوم وقال بن سعد أمه حسانة خزاعية قال مجاهد سمعت قيس بن السائب يقول ان شهر رمضان يفتديه الإنسان يطعم فيه كل يوم مسكينا فاطعموا عنى مسكينا كل يوم صاعا قال قيس وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شريكي في الجاهلية فكان خير شريك لا يماري ولا يشاري أخرجه البغوي والحسن بن سفيان وغيرهما من طريق محمد بن مسلم الطائفي عن إبراهيم بن ميسرة عن مجاهد وأخرجه أبو بشر الدولابي في الكنى من هذا الوجه لكنه قال أبو قيس بن بن السائب كذا عنده وقيس بن السائب أصح قال ابن أبي خيثمة واختلف أصحاب مجاهد فقال إبراهيم بن ميسرة فذكر ما تقدم وقال إبراهيم بن مهاجر عن مجاهد عن فائد عن السائب وقال الأعمش عنه عن عبد الله بن السائب قال والصواب ما قال إبراهيم بن ميسرة وحكى بن أبي حاتم في العلل عن أبيه رواية إبراهيم بن ميسرة والأعمش قال وقال سليمان عن مجاهد كان السائب بن أبي السائب قال أبو حاتم قيس بن السائب أظنه أخا عبد الله بن السائب وعبد الله بن السائب كان في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حدثا قلت فما الصحيح في الشريك قال الشركة بابنه اشبه واخرج بن شاهين من طريق مسلم الأعور عن مجاهد عن قيس بن السائب قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلى الفجر إذا يغشى السماء النور والظهر إذا زالت الشمس الحديث ومسلم ضعيف وقال عبيد الله بن أبي زياد عن مجاهد عن قيس بن السائب قال كان ابواي يمخضان اللبن حتى إذا أدرك افرغا منه في صحن فيقولان اذهب بهذا إلى آلهتهم قال فيأتي الكلب فيشرب اللبن ويأكل الزبد ثم يشعر برجله فيبول عليها أخرجه أبو سهل بن زياد القطان في الجزء الرابع من فوائده واخرج الطبراني من طريق يزيد بن عياض وهو واه عن عبد الملك بن عبيد عن مجاهد ان قيس بن السائب كبر حتى مرت به ستون على المائة وضعف فاطعم عنه واخرج بن سعد من طريق موسى بن أبي كثير عن مجاهد قال هذه الآية نزلت في مولاي قيس بن السائب وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين وذكر المفيد بن النعمان الرافضي في مناقب على ان قيس بن السائب المخزومي أحد الرجلين اللذين اجارتهما أم هانئ في فتح مكة
records.english: son of ʿUwaymir ibn ʿAʾidh ibn ʿImran ibn Makhzum. In one version of his lineage, ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar replaces ʿImran. Ibn Hibban said that he had Companionship. His mother was Raʾitah bint Wahb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAʾidh ibn ʿImran ibn Makhzum; Ibn Saʿd said that his mother was Hassanah, a woman of Khuzaʿah. Mujahid said: “I heard Qays ibn al-Saʾib say, ‘A person pays compensation during the month of Ramadan by feeding one poor person each day, so feed on my behalf each day one saʿ to a poor person.’” Qays said, “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was my partner in the Age of Ignorance. He was the best partner, neither disputing nor quarreling.” Al-Baghawi, al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, and others transmitted it through Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Taʾifi, from Ibrahim ibn Maysarah, from Mujahid. Abu Bishr al-Dulabi transmitted it by this route in al-Kuna, but his version says, “Abu Qays ibn al-Saʾib.” Qays ibn al-Saʾib is more correct. Ibn Abi Khaythamah said that Mujahid’s narrators differed: Ibrahim ibn Maysarah gave the version above; Ibrahim ibn Muhajir said, “from Mujahid, from Faʾid, from al-Saʾib”; and al-Aʿmash said, “from him, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Saʾib.” He said that Ibrahim ibn Maysarah’s version is correct. Ibn Abi Hatim related in al-ʿIlal from his father the versions of Ibrahim ibn Maysarah and al-Aʿmash. He said that Sulayman narrated from Mujahid, “It was al-Saʾib ibn Abi al-Saʾib.” Abu Hatim said, “I think Qays ibn al-Saʾib was the brother of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Saʾib. ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Saʾib was a youth during the Prophet’s ﷺ lifetime.” I say: then which report about the partnership is correct? Partnership with his son is more likely. Ibn Shahin transmitted through Muslim al-Aʿwar, from Mujahid, from Qays ibn al-Saʾib, who said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to pray the dawn prayer when light spread across the sky, and the noon prayer when the sun passed the meridian...” Muslim is weak. ʿUbayd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated from Mujahid, from Qays ibn al-Saʾib, who said: “My parents used to churn milk. When it was ready they poured it into a bowl and said, ‘Take this to their gods.’ A dog would come, drink the milk, eat the butter, then raise its leg and urinate upon them.” Abu Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Qattan transmitted it in the fourth part of his Fawaʾid. Al-Tabarani transmitted through Yazid ibn ʿIyad, who is feeble, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUbayd, from Mujahid, that Qays ibn al-Saʾib grew old, reaching sixty years beyond one hundred, became weak, and was fed for by others. Ibn Saʿd transmitted through Musa ibn Abi Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: “This verse was revealed concerning my patron Qays ibn al-Saʾib: ‘For those who can bear it, a ransom: feeding a poor person.’” Al-Mufid ibn al-Nuʿman al-Rafidi stated in Manaqib ʿAli that Qays ibn al-Saʾib al-Makhzumi was one of the two men to whom Umm Haniʾ granted protection at the Conquest of Mecca.

records.arabic: بن دليم الأنصاري الخزرجي تقدم نسبه في ترجمة والده مختلف في كنيته فقيل أبو الفضل وأبو عبد الله وأبو عبد الملك وذكر بن حبان ان كنيته أبو القاسم وأمه بنت عم أبيه واسمها فكيهة بنت عبيد بن دليم وقال بن عيينة عن عمرو بن دينار كان قيس ضخما حسنا طويلا إذا ركب الحمار خطت رجلاه الأرض وقال الواقدي كان سخيا كريما داهية وأخرجه البغوي من طريق بن شهاب قال كان قيس حامل راية الأنصار مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وآله ولم وكان من ذوي الرأي من الناس وقال بن يونس شهد فتح مصر واختط بها دارا ثم كان اميرها لعلي وفي مكارم الأخلاق للطبراني من طريق عروة بن الزبير كان قيس بن سعد بن عبادة يقول اللهم ارزقني مالا فإنه لا يصلح الفعال الا بالمال وذكر الزبير انه كان سناطا ليس في وجهه شعرة فقال ان الأنصار كانوا يقولون وددنا ان نشتري لقيس بن سعد لحية بأموالنا قال أبو عمر وكذلك كان شريح وعبد الله بن الزبير لم يكن في وجوههم شعر وفي صحيح البخاري عن أنس كان قيس بن سعد من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بمنزلة صاحب الشرطة من الأمير واخرج البخاري في التاريخ من طريق خريم بن أسد قال رأيت قيس بن سعد وقد خدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين وقال أبو عمر كان أحد الفضلاء الجلة من دهاة العرب من أهل الرأي والمكيدة في الحرب مع النجدة والسخاء والشجاعة وكان شريف قومه غير مدافع وكان أبوه وجده كذلك وفي الصحيح عن جابر في قصة جيش العسرة انه كان في ذلك الجيش وانه كان ينحر ويطعم حتى استدان بسبب ذلك ونهاه أمير الجيش وهو أبو عبيدة وفي بعض طرقه ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أجود من شيمة أهل ذلك البيت رويناه في الغيلانيات وأخرجه بن وهب من طريق بكر بن سوادة عن أبي حمزة بن جابر واخرج بن المبارك عن بن عيينة عن موسى بن أبي عيسى ان رجلا استقرض من قيس بن سعد ثلاثين الفا فلما ردها عليه أبى ان يقبلها وشهد مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المشاهد وأخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الفتح الراية من أبيه فدفعها له روى قيس بن سعد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن أبيه روى عنه أنس وثعلبة بن أبي مالك وأبو ميسرة وعبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى وعروة وآخرون وصحب قيس عليا وشهد معه مشاهده وكان قد امره على مصر فاحتال عليه معاوية فلم ينخدع له فاحتال على أصحاب على حتى حسنوا له تولية محمد بن أبي بكر فولاه مصر وارتحل قيس فشهد مع على صفين ثم كان مع الحسن بن علي حتى صالح معاوية فرجع قيس إلى المدينة فأقام بها وروى بن عيينة عن عمرو بن دينار قال قال قيس لولا الإسلام لمكرت مكرا لا تطيقه العرب قال خليفة وغيره مات في آخر خلافة معاوية بالمدينة وقال بن حبان كان هرب من معاوية ومات سنة خمس وثمانين في خلافة عبد الملك قال وقيل مات في آخر خلافة معاوية قلت وقول خليفة ومن وافقه هو الصواب
records.english: son of Dulaym, al-Anṣārī al-Khazrajī. His lineage was given earlier in his father’s entry. There is disagreement over his kunyah: Abu al-Fadl, Abu ʿAbd Allah, or Abu ʿAbd al-Malik. Ibn Hibban said that it was Abu al-Qasim. His mother was his father’s paternal cousin, Fukayhah bint ʿUbayd ibn Dulaym. Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dinar that Qays was large, handsome, and tall; when he rode a donkey, his feet traced the ground. Al-Waqidi said that he was generous, noble, and shrewd. Al-Baghawi transmitted through Ibn Shihab that Qays carried the Ansar’s banner with the Messenger of Allah ﵌ and was one of the people of sound judgment. Ibn Yunus said that he witnessed the conquest of Egypt and established a house there; he was later its governor for ʿAli. In al-Tabarani’s Makarim al-Akhlaq, through ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qays ibn Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah used to say, “O Allah, provide me with wealth, for noble deeds are possible only with wealth.” Al-Zubayr mentioned that he was beardless, with not a hair on his face. The Ansar used to say, “We wish we could buy Qays ibn Saʿd a beard with our wealth.” Abu ʿUmar said that Shurayh and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr were likewise without facial hair. In Sahih al-Bukhari, from Anas, Qays ibn Saʿd stood in relation to the Prophet ﷺ as the chief of police stands to a ruler. Al-Bukhari transmitted in al-Tarikh through Khuraym ibn Asad, who said, “I saw Qays ibn Saʿd, who had served the Prophet ﷺ for ten years.” Abu ʿUmar said that he was one of the eminent men of merit, among the shrewdest Arabs, skilled in counsel and stratagem in war, as well as bold, generous, and courageous. He was the undisputed noble of his people, as his father and grandfather had been. In the Sahih, from Jabir, in the story of the Army of Hardship, he was with that army and slaughtered animals and fed the men until he incurred debt. The army commander, Abu ʿUbaydah, forbade him from continuing. One route reports that the Prophet ﷺ said, “Generosity is among the traits of the people of that house.” We narrated it in al-Ghaylaniyyat, and Ibn Wahb transmitted it through Bakr ibn Sawadah, from Abu Hamzah ibn Jabir. Ibn al-Mubarak transmitted from Ibn ʿUyaynah, from Musa ibn Abi ʿIsa, that a man borrowed thirty thousand from Qays ibn Saʿd; when he returned it, Qays refused to accept it. Qays witnessed the campaigns with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. On the day of the Conquest, the Prophet ﷺ took the banner from his father and gave it to him. Qays ibn Saʿd narrated from the Prophet ﷺ and from his father; Anas, Thaʿlabah ibn Abi Malik, Abu Maysarah, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, ʿUrwah, and others narrated from him. Qays accompanied ʿAli and witnessed his battles. ʿAli appointed him governor of Egypt. Muʿawiyah tried to deceive him but failed, so he maneuvered among ʿAli’s companions until they persuaded ʿAli to appoint Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr. ʿAli appointed Muhammad over Egypt, and Qays departed. He fought beside ʿAli at Siffin and later remained with al-Hasan ibn ʿAli until al-Hasan made peace with Muʿawiyah. Qays then returned to Medina and remained there. Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dinar that Qays said, “Were it not for Islam, I would devise a stratagem the Arabs could not withstand.” Khalifah and others said that he died in Medina near the end of Muʿawiyah’s caliphate. Ibn Hibban said that he fled from Muʿawiyah and died in the year 85 during ʿAbd al-Malik’s caliphate; he also reported the view that Qays died near the end of Muʿawiyah’s caliphate. I say: the view of Khalifah and those who agree with him is correct.

records.english: son of al-Nuʿmān, al-Kindī. Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned that he and his relative ʿAdi ibn ʿUmayrah ibn Zurarah ibn al-Arqam came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ. Qays’s son was the last person to leave Kufa for Syria, angry with the Kufans for reviling ʿUthman, and Muʿawiyah honored him.

records.arabic: بن زعوراء وقيل بين السكن وزعوراء قيس آخر الأنصاري ذكره موسى بن عقبة فيمن شهد بدرا وقال بن أبي حاتم سمعت أبي يقول هو أحد من جمع القرآن على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي صحيح البخاري عن أنس في تسمية من جمع القرآن أبو زيد قال أنس هو أحد عمومتي وقد أخرجه أبو نعيم في المستخرج عن البخاري وابن حبان وابن السكن وابن منده من الوجه الذي أخرجه منه البخاري زادوا ان اسمه قيس بن السكن وكان من بني عدي بن النجار ومات ولم يدع عقبا قال أنس فورثناه وذكره موسى بن عقبة أيضا فيمن استشهد يوم جسر أبي عبيد وفي التابعين قيس بن السكن أبو أبي كوفي يروي عن بن مسعود والاشعث في صوم يوم عاشوراء اخرج له مسلم ومات قديما بعد السبعين من الهجرة
records.english: son of Zaʿūrāʾ; it is also said that another Qays intervenes between al-Sakan and Zaʿuraʾ. He was an Ansari. Musa ibn ʿUqbah listed him among those who witnessed Badr. Ibn Abi Hatim said, “I heard my father say that he was one of those who collected the Qurʾan during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ.” In Sahih al-Bukhari, Anas named Abu Zayd among those who collected the Qurʾan and said, “He was one of my paternal uncles.” Abu Nuʿaym transmitted the report in his Mustakhraj on al-Bukhari, as did Ibn Hibban, Ibn al-Sakan, and Ibn Mandah by the route used by al-Bukhari, adding that his name was Qays ibn al-Sakan, that he was of Banu ʿAdi ibn al-Najjar, and that he died leaving no descendants. Anas said, “So we inherited from him.” Musa ibn ʿUqbah also listed him among those martyred on the day of Abu ʿUbayd’s Bridge. Among the Successors was Qays ibn al-Sakan, Abu Ubayy, a Kufan who narrated from Ibn Masʿud and al-Ashʿath concerning the fast of ʿAshuraʾ. Muslim transmitted from him. He died early, after the year 70 AH.

records.arabic: بفتحتين الأنصاري ذكره البخاري وابن السكن وابن حبان وغيرهم في الصحابة وقال البغوي سكن المدينة وقال بن حبان دعا له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أبو عمر قال بعضهم قيس بن اسلع قال أبو عمر ليس بشيء قلت هو قول بن أبي حاتم ونبه بن فتحون على ان بن أبي حاتم ذكره في الموضعين في الألف من الياء فيمن اسمه قيس وفي السين من الياء فيمن اسمه قيس أيضا وقال في كل منهما الأنصاري وفي الثاني له صحبة ولم ينبه على انه الأول واخرج الطبراني وابن منده من طريق أبي عاصم سعد بن زياد عن نافع مولى حمنة عن قيس بن سلع الأنصاري ان إخوته شكوه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا انه يبذر ماله ويبسط فيه فقال له يا قيس ما شأن اخوتك يشكونك قال يا رسول الله انني آخذ نصيبي من التمر فانفقه في سبيل الله وعلى من صحبني فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انفق قيس ينفق الله عليك وقال الطبراني لم يروه عن قيس الا بهذا الإسناد تفرد به سعد أبو عاصم وهو عند البخاري من هذا الوجه باختصار
records.english: with two fatḥahs, al-Anṣārī. Al-Bukhari, Ibn al-Sakan, Ibn Hibban, and others listed him among the Companions. Al-Baghawi said that he settled in Medina. Ibn Hibban said that the Prophet ﷺ prayed for him. Abu ʿUmar said, “Some call him Qays ibn Aslaʿ,” but added, “This is nothing.” I say: that is Ibn Abi Hatim’s view. Ibn Fathun pointed out that Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him in both places: under alif after yāʾ among those named Qays, and under sīn after yāʾ among those named Qays. In each he called him al-Ansari, and in the second said that he had Companionship, without noting that he was the same man. Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mandah transmitted through Abu ʿAsim Saʿd ibn Ziyad, from Nafiʿ, the client of Hamnah, from Qays ibn Salʿ al-Ansari, that his brothers complained about him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, saying that he squandered his wealth and spent it too freely. He asked, “Qays, why are your brothers complaining about you?” He replied, “O Messenger of Allah, I take my share of the dates and spend it in Allah’s cause and on those who accompany me.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, “Spend, Qays, and Allah will spend upon you.” Al-Tabarani said, “It is narrated from Qays only through this chain. Saʿd Abu ʿAsim alone related it.” Al-Bukhari has it by this route in abbreviated form.

records.arabic:
بن شراحيل أو شرحبيل بن الشيطان بن الحارث بن الاصهب الجعفي واستدركه بن الأثير تبعا لابن الأمين وقال قال بن الكلبي وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكره المرزباني في معجم الشعراء وذكر في نسبه ان اسم الاصهب عوف بن كعب بن الحارث قال وكان يعرف بأمه مليكة وأنشد له يرثى اخاه سلمة بن مليكة
وباكية تبكي إلى بشجوها
الا رب شجو لي حواليك فانظري
نظرت وساقي الترب بيني وبينه
فلله درى أي ساعة منظري وقد تقدم خبر جده شراحيل في ترجمة بن عمه سلمان بن ثمامة بن شراحيل ولما ذكره بن الكلبي وذكر وفاته قال هو بن مليكة بنت الحلواني الجعفية وهي أمه ولها خبر وكان عمه عبد الله بن شراحيل شاعرا
records.english: son of Shurāḥīl, or Sharḥabīl—ibn al-Shaytan ibn al-Harith ibn al-Ashhab al-Juʿfi. Ibn al-Athir added him in his supplement, following Ibn al-Amin, and said that Ibn al-Kalbi reported that he came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Marzubani mentioned him in Muʿjam al-Shuʿaraʾ and stated in his lineage that al-Ashhab’s name was ʿAwf ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Harith. Qays was known by his mother, Mulaykah. Al-Marzubani cited these verses in which he lamented his brother Salamah ibn Mulaykah: “A weeping woman pours out her grief to me; / indeed, much grief surrounds me because of you, so look. / I looked, while the dust-spreader stood between me and him— / by Allah, how remarkable was the hour of my looking!” The account of his grandfather Sharahil appeared earlier in the entry on his paternal cousin Salman ibn Thumamah ibn Sharahil. When Ibn al-Kalbi mentioned him and his delegation, he said, “He is the son of Mulaykah bint al-Hulwani al-Juʿfiyyah, his mother, who has a story.” His paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Sharahil was a poet.

names.arabic: قيس بن سلمة بن شراحيل أو شرحبيل بن الشيطان بن الحارث بن الاصهب الجعفي
names.english: Qays ibn Salamah ibn Sharahil—or Shurahbil—ibn al-Shaytan ibn al-Harith ibn al-Ashhab al-Juʿfi

records.english: son of Mushajjaʿah ibn al-Mujammaʿ ibn Malik al-Juʿfi, known as Ibn Mulaykah. He and his father had Companionship and came as a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, as stated by Ibn al-Kalbi. Ibn al-Athir also added him in his supplement.

records.arabic: وقيل صرمة بن قيس وقيل قيس بن مالك أبو صرمة وقيل قيس بن أنس أبو صرمة وفرق بن حبان بين قيس بن مالك وقيس بن صرمة فقال في كل منهما له صحبة وقد تقدم في صرمة بن قيس في حرف الصاد المهملة
records.english: also called Ṣirmah ibn Qays, Qays ibn Malik Abu Sirmah, or Qays ibn Anas Abu Sirmah. Ibn Hibban distinguished Qays ibn Malik from Qays ibn Sirmah and said of each that he had Companionship. He appeared earlier as Sirmah ibn Qays under the undotted ṣād.

records.arabic: بن وهب بن عدي بن غانم بن غنم بن عدي بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي وقال العدوي شهد أحدا وهو أخو مالك بن صعصعة راوي حديث المعراج المخرج في الصحيحين عن أنس عنه
records.english: son of Wahb ibn ʿAdi ibn Ghanim ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAdi ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari al-Khazraji. Al-ʿAdawi said that he witnessed Uhud. He was the brother of Malik ibn Saʿsaʿah, the narrator of the hadith of the Ascension transmitted in the two Sahihs from Anas, from him.

names.arabic: قيس بن صعصعة بن وهب بن عدي بن غانم بن غنم بن عدي بن النجار الأنصاري الخزرجي
names.english: Qays ibn Saʿsaʿah ibn Wahb ibn ʿAdi ibn Ghanim ibn Ghanm ibn ʿAdi ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari al-Khazraji

records.arabic: واسم أبي صعصعة عمرو بن زيد بن عوف بن مبذول بن عمرو بن غنم بن مازن بن النجار الأنصاري ذكره موسى بن عقبة فيمن شهد العقبة وفيمن شهد بدرا وذكر أبو الأسود عن عروة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم جعله يومئذ على الساقة واخرج أبو عبيد في فضائل القرآن ومحمد بن نصر المروزي في قيام الليل والطبراني وغيرهم من طريق حبان بن واسع بن حبان عن أبيه عن قيس بن أبي صعصعة انه قال يا رسول الله في كم اقرأ القرآن قال في كل خمس عشرة قال اجدني أقوى من ذلك الحديث وذكره بن أبي حاتم بهذه القصة لكن قال قيس بن صعصعة والصحيح بن أبي صعصعة وذكره بن السكن بالوجهين فقال قيس بن صعصعة ويقال بن أبي صعصعة وقال بن حبان قيس بن أبي صعصعة واسمه عمرو شهد العقبة وكان على ساقة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال بن السكن روى عنه حديث تفرد به بن لهيعة
records.english: Abū Ṣaʿṣaʿah’s name was ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn ʿAwf ibn Mabdhul ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghanm ibn Mazin ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari. Musa ibn ʿUqbah listed him among those who witnessed al-ʿAqabah and Badr. Abu al-Aswad related from ʿUrwah that on that day the Prophet ﷺ placed him in charge of the rear guard. Abu ʿUbayd transmitted in Fadaʾil al-Qurʾan, as did Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi in Qiyam al-Layl, al-Tabarani, and others, through Habban ibn Wasiʿ ibn Habban, from his father, from Qays ibn Abi Saʿsaʿah, who said, “O Messenger of Allah, over how many days should I recite the Qurʾan?” He replied, “Every fifteen days.” Qays said, “I find myself stronger than that...” to the end of the hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him with this story but called him Qays ibn Saʿsaʿah. The correct form is Ibn Abi Saʿsaʿah. Ibn al-Sakan mentioned both forms, saying, “Qays ibn Saʿsaʿah, also called Ibn Abi Saʿsaʿah.” Ibn Hibban said, “Qays ibn Abi Saʿsaʿah, whose name was ʿAmr, witnessed al-ʿAqabah and commanded the Prophet’s ﷺ rear guard.” Ibn al-Sakan said, “One hadith is narrated from him, and Ibn Lahiʿah alone related it.”

names.arabic: عمرو بن زيد بن عوف بن مبذول بن عمرو بن غنم بن مازن بن النجار الأنصاري
names.english: ʿAmr ibn Zayd ibn ʿAwf ibn Mabdhul ibn ʿAmr ibn Ghanm ibn Mazin ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari

records.arabic: الغفاري ذكره بن سعد والطبراني وقالا كان ينزل غيقة بفتح المعجمة وسكون المثناة من تحت ثم قاف وكان إسلامه بعد انصراف المشركين من الخندق وهو الذي نزل عليه الحارث بن هشام لما فر يوم بدر فحمله قيس على بعيره حتى اوصله إلى مكة ثم التقيا في الإسلام بالسقيا فحمدا لله على الهداية إلى الإسلام وقالا طالما اوضعنا في الباطل في هذه الطريق واستدركه بن فتحون ووقع عند بن شاهين أبو الصلت كذا في التجريد
records.english: Al-Ghifārī; Ibn Saʿd and al-Ṭabarānī mentioned him and said that he lived at Ghayqah—with fatḥah on the dotted letter, a quiescent yāʾ with two dots beneath, and then qāf. He accepted Islam after the polytheists withdrew from the Trench. He was the man with whom al-Harith ibn Hisham lodged after fleeing on the day of Badr; Qays carried him on his camel until he delivered him to Mecca. They later met as Muslims at al-Suqya, praised Allah for guiding them to Islam, and said, “How long we used to rush along this road in falsehood!” Ibn Fathun added him in his supplement. Ibn Shahin has Abu al-Salt, as stated in al-Tajrid.

records.arabic:
واسم الاسلت عامر بن جشم بن وائل بن زيد بن قيس بن عمرو بن مالك بن الأوس الأنصاري وصيفي وهو أبو قيس بن الاسلت مشهور بكنيته فاخرج الفرياني وابن أبي حاتم من طريق عدي بن ثابت قال توفي أبو قيس بن الاسلت كان من صالحي الأنصار فخطب قيس ابنه امرأته فقالت له إنما اعدك ولدا وأنت من صالحي قومك ثم اتت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فذكرت له ذلك فانزل الله عز وجل ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النساء الا ما قد سلف وفي سنده قيس بن الربيع عن أشعث بن سوار وهما ضعيفان والخبر مع ذلك منقطع وقد تقدم في ترجمة حصن بن أبي قيس بن الاسلت ان القصة وقعت له مع امرأة أبيه وهي كبيشة بنت معن هكذا سمها بن الكلبي وخالفه مقاتل فجعل القصة لقيس وعند أبي الفرج الأصبهاني ما يوهم ان قيسا قتل في الجاهلية فإنه ذكر ان يزيد بن مرداس السلمي وهو أخو عباس بن مرداس قتل قيس بن أبي قيس بن الاسلت في بعض الحروب فطلب بثأره بن عمه عوف بن النعمان بن الاسلت حتى تمكن من يزيد بن مرداس فقتله وقال ولقيس يقول أبوه
اقيس ان هلكت وأنت حي
فلا يعدم فواضلك الفقير الأبيات ويحتمل ان يكون وقع هذا في الإسلام ومع ذلك فموت قيس قبل أبيه يمنع ما اقتضاه هذا النقل انه عاش بعد أبيه فيتعين ان يكون ولدا آخر أو أبو قيس آخر وأنشد بن الكلبي هذا البيت لأبي قيس ولكن قال في آخره العديم بدل الفقير ووقع في رواية بن جريح عن عكرمة ان القصة وقعت لأبي قيس بن الاسلت خلف على امرأة أبيه الاسلت واسمها سمرة أم عبيد الله أخرجه سيف في تفسيره من هذا الوجه وكذا أخرجه المستغفري من طريق بن جريج وقد ذكر ذلك أبو عمر في ترجمة أبي قيس ويأتي الكلام عليه في الكنى ان شاء الله تعالى
records.english:
Al-Aslat’s name was ʿĀmir ibn Jusham ibn Wa'il ibn Zayd ibn Qays ibn Amr ibn Malik ibn al-Aws—the Ansari. Sayfi was Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat, who was well known by his kunyah. Al-Firyabi and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted through Adi ibn Thabit, who said: Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died, and he had been one of the righteous men of the Ansar. His son Qays then proposed marriage to his wife. She said to him, 'I regard you only as a son, and you are among the righteous men of your people.' She then came to the Prophet ﷺ and told him of it, so God ﷿ revealed: 'Do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred.' In its chain are Qays ibn al-Rabi and Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, both of whom are weak, and the report is nevertheless disconnected. It has already been stated in the biography of Hisn ibn Abi Qays ibn al-Aslat that the episode occurred to him with his father's wife, Kabishah bint Ma'n; this is how Ibn al-Kalbi named her. Muqatil disagreed with him and assigned the episode to Qays. Abu al-Faraj al-Isbahani has material implying that Qays was killed in the pre-Islamic period, for he related that Yazid ibn Mirdas al-Sulami, the brother of Abbas ibn Mirdas, killed Qays ibn Abi Qays ibn al-Aslat in one of the wars. His paternal cousin Awf ibn al-Nu'man ibn al-Aslat pursued vengeance for him until he gained control of Yazid ibn Mirdas and killed him. He said that Qays's father composed about him:
'O Qays, if you perish while I remain alive,
May the poor man never lack your benefactions.'
These are verses. It is possible that this occurred in Islam. Even so, Qays's death before his father precludes what this report entails, namely that he lived after his father; it must therefore have been another son or another Abu Qays. Ibn al-Kalbi cited this verse for Abu Qays, but gave 'the destitute' instead of 'the poor man' at its end. In Ibn Jurayj's narration from Ikrimah, the episode occurred when Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat married his father al-Aslat's widow, whose name was Samrah, the mother of Ubayd Allah. Sayf transmitted it with this chain in his Tafsir, and al-Mustaghfiri likewise transmitted it through Ibn Jurayj. Abu Umar mentioned this in the biography of Abu Qays. Discussion of him will come in the section on kunyahs, ان شاء الله تعالى.

records.english: son of Jubayrah, Abu Jubayrah. Al-Baghawi said: I was informed that his name was Qays ibn al-Dahhak.

records.arabic: ذكره البغوي في الصحابة وقال سكن المدينة وقال بن حبان له صحبة قال ويقال قيس بن طهفة روى عنه ابنه يعيش قلت وقد تقدم الاختلاف فيه في ترجمة طحفة بن قيس
records.english: Al-Baghawī listed him among the Companions and said that he settled in Medina. Ibn Hibban said: He had companionship. He said that he is also called Qays ibn Tahfah. His son Ya'ish narrated from him. I say: The disagreement concerning him has already been given in the biography of Tahfah ibn Qays.

records.arabic:
مدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في يوم بدر كذا في التجريد وقد ذكر قصته بن هشام قال وقال قيس بن طريف الأشجعي يمدح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويذكر إجلاء بني النضير
نبي تلاقيه من الله رحمة
فلا تسألوه أمر غيب مرجم
فقد كان في بدر لعمرى عبرة
لكم يا قريش والقليب الململم
رسول من الرحمن يتلو كتابه
وشرعته والحق لم يتلعثم 1 ( واستدركه بن فتحون )
records.english:
He praised the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم on the day of Badr. So it is stated in al-Tajrid. Ibn Hisham related his story, saying: Qays ibn Tarif al-Ashja'i said, praising the Prophet ﷺ and mentioning the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir:
'A Prophet whom mercy from God meets;
Do not ask him about conjectured matters of the unseen.
By my life, at Badr there was indeed a lesson
For you, O Quraysh, and the crowded well: —
A messenger from the All-Merciful reciting His Book
And His law; the truth did not cause him to falter.'
Ibn Fathun added him as a supplement.

records.arabic:
بن جعونة بن الحارث بن عامر بن نمير بن عامر بن صعصعة النميري قال بن الكلبي وفد على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومسح وجهه وقال اللهم بارك عليه وعلى أصحابه وكذا ذكره أبو عبيد والطبري وقد مضى له ذكر فقي ترجمة قرة بن دعموص ويأتي له ذكر في ترجمة يزيد بن نمير قال بن الكلبي وفيه يقول الشاعر
إليك بن خير الناس قيس بن عاصم
جشمت عن الأمر العظيم مجاشما
records.english:
son of Jaʿūnah ibn al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Numayr ibn Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah al-Numayri. Ibn al-Kalbi said: He came in a delegation to the Prophet ﷺ, who wiped his face and said, 'O God, bless him and his companions.' Abu Ubayd and al-Tabari likewise mentioned him. He was previously mentioned in the biography of Qurrah ibn Da'mus, and he will be mentioned in the biography of Yazid ibn Numayr. Ibn al-Kalbi said that the poet said concerning him:
'To you, son of the best of mankind, Qays ibn Asim,
I undertook arduous labors in the grave affair.'

names.arabic: قيس بن عاصم بن أسيد بن جعونة بن الحارث بن عامر بن نمير بن عامر بن صعصعة النميري
names.english: Qays ibn Asim ibn Usayd ibn Ja'unah ibn al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Numayr ibn Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah al-Numayri

records.arabic:
بن منقر بن خالد بن عبيد بن مقاعس واسمه الحارث بن عمرو بن كعب بن سعد بن زيد مناة بن تميم التميمي المنقري يكنى أبا علي وحكى بن عبد البر انه قيل في كنيته أيضا أبو طلحة وأبو قبيصة والأول اشهر وبه جزم البخاري وقال له صحبة وجزم بن أبي حاتم بأنه أبو طلحة قال بن سعد كان قد حرم الخمر في الجاهلية ثم وفد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وفد بني تميم فأسلم فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا سيد أهل الوبر وكان سيدا بوادا ثم ساق بسند حسن إلى الحسن عن قيس بن عاصم قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما دنوت منه قال هذا سيد أهل الوبر فذكر الحديث وفيه فقال لقيس كيف تصنع بالمنيحه فقال قيس إني لأمنح في كل عام مائة قال فكيف تصنع بالعارية فذكر الحديث وفى آخره قال قيس لئن عشت لأدعن عدتها قليلا قال الحسن ففعل والله ثم ذكر وصيته وقال بن السكن كان عاقلا حليما يقتدى به وقال أبو عمر قيل للاحنف ممن تعلمت الحلم قال من قيس بن عاصم رايته يوما محتبيا فاتى برجل مكتوف وآخر مقتول فقيل هذا بن أخيك قتل ابنك فالتفت إلى بن أخيه فقال يا بن أخي بئسما فعلت اثمت بربك وقطعت رحمك ورميت نفسك بسهمك ثم قال لابن له آخر قم يا بني فوار أخاك وحل اكتاف بن عمك وسق إلى أمه مائة ناقة دية ابنها فانها غريبة وذكر الزبير في الموفقيات عن عمه عن عبد الله بن مصعب قال قال أبو بكر لقيس بن عاصم ما حملك على ان وادت وكان أول من واد فقال خشيت ان يخلف عليهن غير كفء قال فصف لنا نفسك فقال اما في الجاهلية فما هممت بملامة ولا حمت على تهمة ولم ار الا في خيل مغيرة أو نادى عشيرة أو حامي جريرة واما في الإسلام فقد قال الله تعالى فلا تزكوا أنفسكم فأعجب أبو بكر بذلك روى قيس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث روى عنه ابناه حكيم وحصين وابن ابنه خليفة بن حصين والاحنف بن قيس ومنفعة بن التوأم وآخرون قال بن منده أنبأنا علي بن العباس العدني بها حدثنا محمد بن حماد الطهراني حدثنا عبد الرزاق أنبأنا إسرائيل حدثنا سماك بن حرب سمعت النعمان بن بشير يقول سمعت عمر بن الخطاب يقول وسئل عن هذه الآية وإذا الموءودة سئلت فقال جاء قيس بن عاصم إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال اني وادت ثماني بنات لي في الجاهلية فقال اعتق عن كل واحدة منهن رقبة قال اني صاحب إبل قال اهد ان شئت عن كل واحدة منهن بدنة ووقع لي بعلو من حديث الطهراني وله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في السنن ومسند أحمد ثلاثة أحاديث أحدها أخرجوه من طريق خليفة بن حصين عن جده قيس بن عاصم انه اسلم فأمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ان يغتسل بماء وسدر والثاني أخرجه أحمد والنسائي من طريق حكيم بن قيس عن أبيه انه قال لا تنوحوا على فان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم ينح عليه الحديث اختصره النسائي وأورده أحمد مطولا وفيه أنه قال لبنيه اتقوا الله وسودوا أكبركم فإن القوم إذا سودوا أكبرهم احيوا ذكر أبيهم وإياكم والمسألة فانها آخر كسب الرجل فذكر بقية الوصية وهي نافعة والثالث أخرجه أحمد في الحلف ونزل قيس البصرة ومات بها ولما مات رثاه عبدة بن الطيب بقوله
عليك سلام الله قيس بن عاصم
ورحمته ما شاء ان يترحما ويقول فيها
وما كان قيس هلكه هلك واحد
ولكنه بنيان قوم تهدما قال بن حبان كان له ثلاثة وثلاثون ولدا ونقل البغوي عن بن أبي خيثمة عن يحيى بن معين ان قيس بن عاصم كان يكنى أبا هراسة وذكر بن شاهين من طريق المدائني عن أبي معشر ورجاله قالوا قدم على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قيس بن عاصم ونعيم بن بدر وعمرو بن الاهتم قبل وفد بني تميم وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استبطأ قيس بن عاصم فقال له عتبة ائذن لي ان اغزوه فاقتل رجاله وأسبي نساءه فاعرض عنه وقجم قيس فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم هذا سيد أهل الوبر ثم تقدم فاسلم فسأله النعمان بن مقرن فقال يا رسول الله ائذن لي ان يكون منزله على قال نعم فبينما هو يتمشى إذ قال أخو النعمان بئسما قال عتبة فقال له قيس وما قال فأخبره فغدا على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أمالي سبيل إلى الرجوع قال لا قال لو كان لي إلى الرجوع سبيل لادخلت على عتبة ونسائه الذل
records.english:
son of Minqar ibn Khalid ibn Ubayd ibn Muqa'is—whose name was al-Harith—ibn Amr ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim, al-Tamimi al-Minqari. His kunyah was Abu Ali. Ibn Abd al-Barr related that he was also said to have the kunyahs Abu Talhah and Abu Qabisah; the first is best known and was stated decisively by al-Bukhari, who said: He had companionship. Ibn Abi Hatim stated decisively that he was Abu Talhah. Ibn Sa'd said: He had forbidden wine for himself in the pre-Islamic period. He then came to the Messenger of God ﷺ in the delegation of Banu Tamim and accepted Islam. The Messenger of God ﷺ said, 'This is the master of the people of the tents.' He had been a chief among the desert dwellers. Ibn Sa'd then supplied, with a fair chain, the report from al-Hasan, from Qays ibn Asim, who said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ. When I approached him, he said, 'This is the master of the people of the tents.' He then related the hadith, in which the Prophet asked Qays, 'What do you do with the milch gift?' Qays said, 'Each year I lend out one hundred animals for milking.' He asked, 'And what do you do with a loan?' and related the rest of the hadith. At its end Qays said, 'If I live, I shall certainly reduce their number.' Al-Hasan said: By God, he did so. Then he mentioned his testament. Ibn al-Sakan said: He was intelligent and forbearing, a man whose example was followed. Abu Umar said: Al-Ahnaf was asked, 'From whom did you learn forbearance?' He replied, 'From Qays ibn Asim. I once saw him sitting with his knees drawn up when a man in bonds and another man who had been killed were brought to him. It was said, ”This son of your brother killed your son.” He turned to his nephew and said, ”Son of my brother, what an evil thing you have done! You sinned against your Lord, severed your kinship, and shot yourself with your own arrow.” Then he told another of his sons, ”Rise, my son, pay the blood money for your brother, untie your cousin's bonds, and drive one hundred she-camels to his mother as her son's blood money, for she is a stranger here.”' Al-Zubayr related in al-Muwaffaqiyyat, from his paternal uncle, from Abd Allah ibn Mus'ab, that Abu Bakr said to Qays ibn Asim, 'What led you to bury your daughters alive?' He was the first to do so. Qays replied, 'I feared that men who were not their equals would succeed me over them.' Abu Bakr said, 'Then describe yourself to us.' He said, 'As for the pre-Islamic period, I never contemplated a blameworthy act, hovered around a suspicion, or was seen except among raiding cavalry, in a tribal gathering, or protecting one burdened by blood guilt. As for Islam, God تعالى has said, ”Do not declare yourselves pure.”' Abu Bakr admired that. Qays narrated hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ. His sons Hakim and Husayn, his grandson Khalifah ibn Husayn, al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, Manfa'ah ibn al-Taw'am, and others narrated from him. Ibn Mandah said: Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Adani informed us there; Muhammad ibn Hammad al-Tahrani related to us; Abd al-Razzaq related to us; Isra'il informed us; Simak ibn Harb related to us: I heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab, when he was asked about the verse, 'And when the girl buried alive is asked,' say: Qays ibn Asim came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said, 'I buried eight daughters alive in the pre-Islamic period.' He said, 'Free a slave for each of them.' Qays said, 'I own camels.' He said, 'If you wish, offer a she-camel for each of them.' I obtained this with a shorter chain as part of al-Tahrani's hadith. Three hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ are recorded for Qays in the Sunan and the Musnad of Ahmad. The first was transmitted through Khalifah ibn Husayn from his grandfather Qays ibn Asim: when he accepted Islam, the Prophet ﷺ ordered him to bathe with water and lote leaves. The second was transmitted by Ahmad and al-Nasa'i through Hakim ibn Qays from his father. He said, 'Do not wail over me, for the Prophet ﷺ was not wailed over,' continuing the hadith. Al-Nasa'i abridged it, while Ahmad gave it at length. In it Qays told his sons, 'Fear God and appoint your eldest as your chief, for when people appoint their eldest as chief, they keep their father's memory alive. Beware of begging, for it is a man's last means of earning.' He then gave the rest of the testament, which is beneficial. The third was transmitted by Ahmad concerning an oath. Qays settled in Basra and died there. When he died, Abdah ibn al-Tayyib elegized him, saying:
'God's peace be upon you, Qays ibn Asim,
And His mercy, for as long as one may pray for mercy.'
He also says in it:
'The death of Qays was not the death of one man;
Rather, it was the collapse of a people's edifice.'
Ibn Hibban said that he had thirty-three children. Al-Baghawi transmitted from Ibn Abi Khaythamah, from Yahya ibn Ma'in, that Qays ibn Asim had the kunyah Abu Hirasah. Ibn Shahin mentioned, through al-Mada'ini, from Abu Ma'shar and his authorities, that they said: Qays ibn Asim, Nu'aym ibn Badr, and Amr ibn al-Ahtam came to the Messenger of God ﷺ before the delegation of Banu Tamim. The Prophet ﷺ had thought Qays ibn Asim slow in coming. Utbah said to him, 'Give me permission to raid him, kill his men, and take his women captive,' but he turned away from him. Then Qays arrived, and the Prophet ﷺ said, 'This is the master of the people of the tents.' Qays came forward and accepted Islam. Al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin asked the Prophet, 'Messenger of God, permit his lodging to be with me.' He said, 'Yes.' While Qays was walking about, al-Nu'man's brother said, 'How evil was what Utbah said!' Qays asked him, 'What did he say?' and he told him. Qays went early the next day to the Prophet ﷺ and asked, 'Do I have any way to return?' He said, 'No.' Qays said, 'Had I any way to return, I would have brought humiliation upon Utbah and his women.'

records.arabic: بن قيس بن عدي بن سعيد بن سهم القرشي السهمي ذكره بن سعد في الصحابة فيمن اسلم يوم الفتح قال أبو سعيد بن يونس يقال ان له صحبة وشهد حنينا وهو من مسلمة الفتح واخرج بن سعد بسند صحيح عن يزيد بن حبيب عمن أدرك ذلك قال فكتب عمر لعمرو بن العاص ان انظر من قبلك ممن بايع تحت الشجرة فافرض له مائة ديتار وأتمها لنفسك لامرتك ولخارجة بن حذيفة لشجاعته ولقيس بن أبي العاص لضيافته واخرج بن يونس من طريق بن لهيعة عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب ان عمر كتب إلى عمرو ان يولى قيسا القضاء على مصر قال يزيد فهو أول قاض في الإسلام بمصر قال بن لهيعة فقضى يسيرا ثم مات قال سعيد بن عفير اختط قيس له دارا بحذاء دار بن رمانة وذكر أبو عمر الكندي في قضاة مصر من طريق الحارث بن عثمان بن قيس بن أبي العاص ان جده قيسا مات في شهر ربيع الأول سنة ثلاث وعشرين
records.english: son of Qays ibn Adi ibn Sa'id ibn Sahm, al-Qurashi al-Sahmi. Ibn Sa'd listed him among the Companions who accepted Islam on the day of the Conquest. Abu Sa'id ibn Yunus said: It is said that he had companionship. He witnessed Hunayn and was among those who accepted Islam at the Conquest. Ibn Sa'd transmitted with a sound chain from Yazid ibn Habib, from one who lived through that time, who said: Umar wrote to Amr ibn al-As, 'Identify those with you who pledged allegiance beneath the tree and allot each one hundred dinars. Complete that amount for yourself because of your command, for Kharijah ibn Hudhafah because of his courage, and for Qays ibn Abi al-As because of his hospitality.' Ibn Yunus transmitted through Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, that Umar wrote to Amr ordering him to appoint Qays as judge over Egypt. Yazid said: He was the first judge in Islam in Egypt. Ibn Lahi'ah said: He judged for a short time and then died. Sa'id ibn Ufir said that Qays laid out a house for himself opposite the house of Ibn Rummanah. Abu Umar al-Kindi mentioned in Judges of Egypt, through al-Harith ibn Uthman ibn Qays ibn Abi al-As, that his grandfather Qays died in the month of Rabi al-Awwal in the year twenty-three.

records.arabic: ذكره بن منده وقال روى حديثه سليمان بن عبد الرحمن عن الوليد بن مسلم عن حفص بن غيلان عن عبيس بن ميمونة عن قيس بن عبادة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قاتل نفسه قال بن منده لا تصح له صحبة وتبعه أبو نعيم
records.english: Ibn Mandah mentioned him and said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated his hadith from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Hafs ibn Ghaylan, from Ubays ibn Maymunah, from Qays ibn Ubadah, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning one who kills himself. Ibn Mandah said: His companionship is not soundly established. Abu Nu'aym followed him in this.

records.english: Al-Aḥmasī, known as Abū Kāhil and famous by his kunyah. Al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim said: He had companionship. Ibn Hibban said: He was the prayer leader of the clan and was counted among the people of Kufa. He will appear in the section on kunyahs.

records.english: son of ʿUbayd ibn al-Harith al-Khawlani, an ally of Banu Harithah ibn al-Harith ibn al-Aws. Ibn Sumay' listed him in the first generation of the Companions. Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad ibn Mihna mentioned him and said: He witnessed Badr while still young, and he witnessed the conquests of Syria with Abu Ubaydah as a mature man. Abu Ubaydah used to consult him in his affairs. He died during the caliphate of Mu'awiyah.

records.arabic: ذكره موسى بن عقبة فيمن هاجر إلى الحبشة وكانت ابنته آمنة ظئر أم حبيبة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وكان هو ظئر عبيد الله بن جحش زوج أم حبيبة الذي تنصر في الحبشة وقال بن سعد كان قديم الإسلام بمكة وهاجر في الثانية إلى الحبشة ومعه امرأته بركة بنت يسار ولا اعلم له رواية وكذا قال بن هشام عن بن إسحاق وذكر البلاذري ان بعضهم سماه رقيشا بزيادة راء أوله وبعجمة الشين قال وهو غلط
records.english: Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah listed him among those who migrated to Abyssinia. His daughter Aminah was the foster mother of Umm Habibah, wife of the Prophet ﷺ, and he was the foster father of Ubayd Allah ibn Jahsh, Umm Habibah's husband who became a Christian in Abyssinia. Ibn Sa'd said: He accepted Islam early in Mecca and made the second migration to Abyssinia, accompanied by his wife Barakah bint Yasar. I know of no narration from him. Ibn Hisham likewise reported this from Ibn Ishaq. Al-Baladhuri mentioned that some called him Ruqaysh, adding an initial ra and rendering the final consonant shin. He said: This is an error.

records.arabic: قال البخاري في تاريخه روى محمد بن ربيعة عن قيس بن عبد الله انه رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كذا فيه ذكرته هنا لاحتمال انه كان مميزا حين رأى وان لم يسمع
records.english: Al-Bukhārī said in his Tārīkh: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated from Qays ibn Abd Allah that he saw the Prophet ﷺ. So it reads there. I have included him here because it is possible that he had reached the age of discernment when he saw him, even if he did not hear from him.

records.arabic: روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تزال لا اله الا الله تدفع عقوبة سخط الله ما لم يقولوها ثم ينقضوا دينهم لصلاح دمائهم فإذا فعلوا ذلك قال الله لهم كذبتم أخرجه بن منده من رواية أبي سهيل نافع بن مالك عن أنس عنه وفي سنده حجاج بن نصير وهو ضعيف
records.english: He narrated from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم: 'There is no god but God will continue to repel the punishment of God's wrath so long as people do not say it and then violate their religion merely to preserve their blood. When they do that, God will say to them, ”You have lied.”' Ibn Mandah transmitted it from the narration of Abu Suhayl Nafi ibn Malik, from Anas, from him. Its chain contains Hajjaj ibn Nusayr, who is weak.

license.attribution: OpenITI, JK000533 transcription of Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's al-Isabah fi Tamyiz al-Sahabah

records.arabic: الأنصاري ذكره بن منده فقال قتل ببدر ونزلت فيه وفي اصحابه ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله اموات ثم اخرج من طريق بن الكلبي في تفسيره عن أبي صالح عن بن عباس في قوله تعلى ولا تقولوا لمن يقتل في سبيل الله اموات نزلت فيمن قتل ببدر وذلك انهم كانوا يقولون لقتلى بدر مات فلان فنزلت قال وقتل يومئذ من الأنصار ثمانية فذكر منهم قيس بن عبد المنذر وقال أبو نعيم الصواب مبشر بن عبد المنذر
records.english: Al-Anṣārī; Ibn Mandah mentioned him and said: He was killed at Badr, and concerning him and his companions was revealed, 'Do not say of those slain in the path of God that they are dead.' He then transmitted through Ibn al-Kalbi in his Tafsir, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, concerning the saying of God, 'Do not say of those slain in the path of God that they are dead': It was revealed concerning those killed at Badr, because people used to say of the slain of Badr, 'So-and-so has died,' and then the verse was revealed. He said: Eight of the Ansar were killed that day, and he listed Qays ibn Abd al-Mundhir among them. Abu Nu'aym said: The correct name is Mubashshir ibn Abd al-Mundhir.

records.english: Ibn Isḥāq mentioned him in al-Sīrah al-Kubrā, and Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm listed him among those whom the Prophet ﷺ gave less than one hundred from the spoils of Hunayn as part of winning hearts. Al-Waqidi listed him among those whom he gave one hundred. Adi ibn Qays al-Sahmi was mentioned previously, and I do not know whether they are one man whose name was reversed or two men.
