records.arabic: بن عمرو السهمي ذكره بن منده وقال ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وأورد له البغوي وابن قانع الحديث الذي رواه حفيده يحيى بن زرارة بن كريم بن الحارث عن أبيه ان جده حدثه فكأنه توهم ان الضمير ليحيى وليس كذلك بل هو لزرارة فقد أخرجه النسائي بلفظ سمعت أبي يذكر انه سمع جده وفي الطبراني عن يحيى بن زرارة بن كريم بن الحارث حدثني أبي عن جده وعند أبي داود عن زرارة بن كريم عن جده الحارث بن عمرو وهذا أبين في المراد ووقع عند البزار من طريق أبي عاصم حدثني يحيى بن زرارة بن كريم بن الحارث رجل من بني سهم حدثني أبي وجدي قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلت استغفر لي فقال غفر الله لكم الحديث في الفرع والعتيرة وهذا نظير رواية البغوي والصواب أن الحديث للحارث بن عمرو ولولا النقل عن البخاري ان لكريم صحبة لأوردته في القسم الأخير فليس البخاري ممن يطلق الكلام بغير تأمل وقد تقدم في الحارث بن عمرو من رواية زيد بن الحباب ما يقتضى ان الحديث لعمرو والد الحارث
records.english: Son of ʿAmr, al-Sahmī; Ibn Mandah mentioned him. He added that al-Bukhari had listed him among the Companions. Al-Baghawi and Ibn Qani‘ cited for him the hadith related by his grandson Yahya ibn Zurarah ibn Karim ibn al-Harith, from his father, that his grandfather related it to him. It appears that they assumed the pronoun referred to Yahya, but that is not so; it refers to Zurarah. Al-Nasa’i transmitted it with the wording, “I heard my father mention that he heard his grandfather.” Al-Tabarani has: from Yahya ibn Zurarah ibn Karim ibn al-Harith: my father related to me, from his grandfather. Abu Dawud has: from Zurarah ibn Karim, from his grandfather al-Harith ibn Amr. This makes the intended person clearer. In al-Bazzar, by way of Abu Asim: Yahya ibn Zurarah ibn Karim ibn al-Harith, a man of Banu Sahm, related to me: My father and my grandfather related to me, saying, “I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and said, ‘Ask forgiveness for me.’ He said, ‘May Allah forgive you all’”—the hadith concerning the fara‘ and the atirah. This resembles al-Baghawi's version. The correct position is that the hadith belongs to al-Harith ibn Amr. Were it not for the report from al-Bukhari that Karim had companionship, I would have placed him in the last section, for al-Bukhari is not one to make statements without reflection. Under al-Harith ibn Amr there has already appeared, in the version of Zayd ibn al-Hubab, material suggesting that the hadith belongs to Amr, al-Harith's father.

records.arabic: الجهني ذكره عمر بن شبة في أخبار المدينة واستدركه بن فتحون عنه من طريق واقد بن عبد الله الجهني عن عمه عن جده كسد بن مالك قال نزل طلحة ومعبد بن زيد حين بعثهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرقبان عير أبي سفيان على كسد بن مالك فلما أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ينبع خطها لكسد فقال يا رسول الله اني كبير ولكن أقطعها لابن أخي فأقطعه إياها فابتاعها منه عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن زرارة بثلاثين الفا ولاها ولد علي بن أبي طالب قال بن فتحون اختصرته من حديث طويل وذكره بن منده فقال روى حديثه الواقدي عن عبد العزيز بن عمران عن واقد ان كان محفوظا وتبعه أبو نعيم قلت رواية عمرو بن شبة له من غير طريق الواقدي
records.english: Al-Juhanī; ʿUmar ibn Shabbah mentioned him in his History of Medina. Ibn Fathun added him on that authority; the report runs through Waqid ibn Abd Allah al-Juhani, from his paternal uncle, from his grandfather Kasd ibn Malik, who said: Talhah and Ma‘bad ibn Zayd stayed with Kasd ibn Malik when the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم sent them to watch Abu Sufyan's caravan. When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم took Yanbu‘, he marked out a grant there for Kasd. Kasd said, “Messenger of Allah, I am an old man; grant it instead to my nephew,” so he granted it to him. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa‘d ibn Zurarah purchased it from him for thirty thousand, and the descendants of Ali ibn Abi Talib administered it. Ibn Fathun said, “I abridged this from a long hadith.” Ibn Mandah mentioned him, saying: Al-Waqidi related his hadith from Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran, from Waqid, if it is preserved. Abu Nu‘aym followed him. I say: Amr ibn Shabbah's version does not come through al-Waqidi.

aliases: Al-Juhanī; ʿUmar ibn Shabbah mentioned him in his History of Medina.

records.arabic: بن ثعلبة بن خرشة وقيل بن ثعلبة بن عثمان حليف بني ساعدة الجهني ويقال الغساني ذكره موسى بن عقبة فيمن شهد بدرا من بنس ساعدة حليف لهم من غسان وكذا صنع بن إسحاق لكن قال حليف لهم من جهينة ووافقه بن الكلبي وأبوه ضبطه بن حبيب عن بن الكلبي بحاء مهملة مكسورة وتشديد الميم وآخره نون وضبطه الدارقطني وابن ماكولا وأبو عمر بفتح الجيم وآخره زاي منقوطة ورأيته في نسخة قديمة من معجم البغوي بتحتانيه بدل الميم وبراء غير منقوطة وقيل هو تصحيف ووقع في نسخة من المغازي رواية الأموي حليف بني طريف هو بن الخزرج بن ساعدة
records.english: ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Kharashah; alternatively, ibn Thaʿlabah ibn ʿUthmān. He was an ally of Banu Sa‘idah, a Juhani, and is also said to have been a Ghassani. Musa ibn Uqbah included him among those of Banu Sa‘idah who witnessed Badr, saying that he was their ally from Ghassan. Ibn Ishaq did likewise but said that he was their ally from Juhaynah; Ibn al-Kalbi agreed with him. His father's name was vocalized by Ibn Habib, from Ibn al-Kalbi, with an unpointed, kasrah-vowelled ha, a doubled mim, and a final nun: Himman. Al-Daraqutni, Ibn Makula, and Abu Umar vocalized it with an open jim and a final pointed z: Jammaz. In an old copy of al-Baghawi's Mu‘jam I saw it with a ya in place of the mim and an unpointed ra: Hiyar; this is said to be a scribal corruption. A copy of al-Maghazi in al-Umawi's recension reads: an ally of Banu Tarif, who are of al-Khazraj ibn Sa‘idah.

names.arabic: كعب بن حمان بن ثعلبة بن خرشة
names.english: Ka‘b ibn Himman ibn Tha‘labah ibn Kharashah

records.arabic: الكلابي من بني بكر بن كلاب صحابي له ذكر في حديث أبي رزين العقيلي الطويل فقد وقع في أثنائه فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ها ان ذين ها ان ذين يعني أبا رزين ورفيقه لمن نفر حدثت انهم من اتقى الناس لله في الدنيا والآخرة فقال له كعب بن الخدارية بضم المعجمة وتخفيف الدال أحد بني بكر بن كلاب من هم يا رسول الله قال بنو المنتفق قالها ثلاثا وسند الحديث حسن كما سأبينه في حرف اللام في ترحمة لقيط بن عامر ان شاء الله تعالى وأخرجه بن أبي خيثمة وغيره من رواية دلهم بن الأسود بن عبد الله بن حاجب بن عامر بن المنتفق عن جده عن عمه لقيط بن عامر أنه خرج وافدا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ومعه صاحب له يقال له نهيك بن عاصم فذكر الحديث بطوله
records.english: Al-Kilābī, of Banū Bakr ibn Kilāb, a Companion mentioned in a report. The report is the long hadith of Abu Razin al-Uqayli. In its course the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Indeed those two, indeed those two”—meaning Abu Razin and his companion—“are among a group about whom I have been told that they are among the people most mindful of Allah in this world and the Hereafter.” Ka‘b ibn al-Khadariyyah—with a dammah on the kha and a single dal—one of Banu Bakr ibn Kilab, asked him, “Who are they, Messenger of Allah?” He replied, “Banu al-Muntafiq,” saying it three times. The hadith's chain is sound, as I shall explain under the letter lam in the biography of Laqit ibn Amir, ان شاء الله تعالى. Ibn Abi Khaythamah and others transmitted it from Dalham ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hajib ibn Amir ibn al-Muntafiq, from his grandfather, from his paternal uncle Laqit ibn Amir, who said that he set out as a delegate to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم together with a companion named Nuhayk ibn Asim; he then related the hadith at length.

records.arabic: الأنصاري من بني الحارث بن الخزرج قال بن منده ذكره البخاري في الصحابة وقال في التاريخ في ترجمة محمد بن ميمون بن كعب بن الخزرج حدثنا محمد بن عبد الرحمن الأنصاري حدثنا محمد بن ميمون عن أبيه عن جده قال صحبني الحكم بن أبي الحكم في غزوة تبوك وكان نعم الصاحب قال أبو حاتم محمد بن ميمون مجهول وذكره بن حبان في الثقات
records.english: Al-Anṣārī, of Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj; Ibn Mandah said that al-Bukhārī mentioned him. Al-Bukhari mentioned him among the Companions. In al-Tarikh, in the biography of Muhammad ibn Maymun ibn Ka‘b ibn al-Khazraj, al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ansari related to us; Muhammad ibn Maymun related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said, “Al-Hakam ibn Abi al-Hakam accompanied me on the expedition to Tabuk, and he was an excellent companion.” Abu Hatim said that Muhammad ibn Maymun was unknown. Ibn Hibban included him among the trustworthy.

names.arabic: محمد بن ميمون بن كعب بن الخزرج
names.english: Muhammad ibn Maymun ibn Ka‘b ibn al-Khazraj

records.arabic:
بن أبي سلمة بضم أوله واسمه ربيعة بن رياح بكسرة ثم تحتانية بن قرط بن الحارث بن مازن بن خلاوة بن ثعلبة بن ثور بن لاطم بن عثمان بن مزينة المزني الشاعر المشهور صحابي معروف قال بن أي عاصم في الآحاد والمثاني حدثنا يحيى بن عمر بن جريج حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر حدثنا الحجاج بن ذي الرقيبة بن عبد الرحمن بن كعب بن زهير عن أبيه عن جده قال خرج كعب وبجير حتى أتيا أبرق فقال بجير لكعب أثبت في غنمنا هنا حتى آتي هذا الرجل فاسمع ما يقول فجاء بجير رسول الله صلى الله عيله وآله وسلم فاسلم فبلغ ذلك كعبا فقال
الا ابلغا عنى بجيرا رسالة
على أي شيء ويب غيرك دلكا
على خلق لم تلف اما ولا أبا
عليه ولم تدرك عليه أخا لكا
سقاك أبو بكر بكأس روية
فانهلك المأمور منها وعلكا فبلغت أبياته رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال من لقي كعبا فليقتله وأهدر دمه وكتب بذلك بجير اليه ويقول له النجاء ثم كتب انه لا يأتيه أحد مسلما إلا قبل منه وأسقط ما كان قبل ذلك فاسلم كعب وقدم حتى أناخ بباب المسجد قال فعرفت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصفة فتخطيت حتى جلست إليه فاسلمت ثم قلت الأمان يا رسول الله انا كعب بن زهير قال أنت الذي تقول والتفت إلى أبي بكر فقال كيف قال فذكر الأبيات الثلاثة فلما قال فانهلك المأمور قلت يا رسول الله ما هكذا قلت وانما قلت المأمون قال مأمون والله وانشده القصيدة التي أولها بانت سعاد وساق القصيدة ووقعت لنا بعلو في جزء إبراهيم بن ديزيل الكبير وأخرج بن قانع من طريق الزبير بن بكار عن بعض أهل المدينة عن يحيى بن سعيد عن سعيد بن المسيب قال لما انتهى إلى كعب بن زهير قتل بن خطل وكان بلغه ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أوعده بما أوعد به خطل قيل لكعب ان لم تدارك نفسك قتلت فقدم المدينة فسأل عن أرق أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فدل على أبي بكر فأخبره خبره فمشى أبو بكر وكعب على أثره وقد التثم حتى صار بين يدي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال رجل يبايعك فمد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يده فمد كعب يده فبايعه وأسفر عن وجهه فأنشده قصيدته التي يقول فيها
نبئت ان رسول الله اوعدني
والعفو عند رسول الله مأمول وفيها
إن الرسول لنور يستضاء به
مهند من سيوف الله مسلول فكساه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بردة له فاشتراها معاوية من ولده فهي التي يلبسها الخلفاء في الاعياد وقال بن أبي الدنيا حدثنا أحمد بن المقدام حدثنا عمر بن علي حدثنا زكريا هو بن أبي زائدة عن الشعبي قال انشد النابغة الذبياني النعمان بن المنذر
تراك الأرض اما مت خفا
وتحيا ما حييت بها ثقيلا فقال له النعمان هذا البيت إن لم تأت بعده ببيت يوضح معناه وإلا كان إلى الهجاء أقرب فتعسر على النابغة النظم فقال له النعمان قد أجلتك ثلاثا فإن قلت فلك مائة من الإبل العصافير وإلا فضربه بالسيف بالغة ما بلغت فخرج النابغة وهو وجل فلقي زهير بن أبي سلمى فذكر له ذلك فقال اخرج بنا إلى البرية فتبعهما كعب فرده زهير فقال له النابغة دع بن أخي يخرج معنا وأردفه فلم يحضرهما شيء فقال كعب للنابغة يا عم ما يمنعك ان تقول
وذلك ان فللت العي عنها
فتمنع جانبيها ان تميلا فأعجب النابغة وغدا على النعمان فأنشده فأعطاه المائة فوهبها لكعب بن زهير فأبى ان يقبلها وذكرها بن دريد في أماليه على غير هذا الوجه قال أنبأنا السكن بن سعيد حدثنا محمد بن عباد حدثنا بن الكلبي قال زار النابغة زهيرا فنحر له وأكرمه وجاء بشراب فجلسا فعرض لهما شعره فقال النابغة البيت الأول وقال بعده
نزلت بمستقر العز منها
ثم وقف فقال لزهير أجز فهمهم ولم يحضره شيء وكان حينئذ يلعب بالتراب مع الصبيان فأقبل فرأى كلا منهما ذقنه على صدره ففكر فقال يا ابت ما لي أراك قد اعتممت فقال تنح لا أم لك فدعاه النابغة على فخذه وانشده فقال ما يمنعك ان تقول
فتمنع جانبيها ان تميلا
فضمه أبوه اليه وقال ابني ورب الكعبة وقال أبو أحمد العسكري وكان موت زهير قبل المبعث وقال بن إسحاق كان قدوم كعب بن زهير بعد الطائف وقال خلف الأحمر لولا قصائد لزهير ما فضلته على ابنه كعب وكان زهير وولداه بجير وكعب وولدا كعب عقبة والعوام شعراء وقال الحطيئة لكعب بن زهير أنتم أهل بيت ينظر اليكم في الشعر فاذكرني في شعرك ففعل وقال أبو عمر من جيد شعر كعب
لو كنت أعجب من شيء لاعجبني
سعي الفتى وهو مخبوء له القدر
يسعى الفتى لامور ليس يدركها
فالنفس واحدة والهم منتشر
والمرء ما عاش ممدود له أمل
لا تنتهي العين حتى ينتهى الأثر
records.english:
ibn Abī Salamah—the first letter of Sulma has a dammah—whose name was Rabi‘ah ibn Riyah, with kasrah then ya, ibn Qurt ibn al-Harith ibn Mazin ibn Khilawah ibn Tha‘labah ibn Thawr ibn Latim ibn Uthman ibn Muzaynah al-Muzani, the celebrated poet and well-known Companion. Ibn Abi Asim said in al-Ahad wa-l-Mathani: Yahya ibn Amr ibn Jurayj related to us; Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us; al-Hajjaj ibn Dhi al-Ruqaybah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: Ka‘b and Bujayr set out until they reached Abraq. Bujayr told Ka‘b, “Stay here with our sheep while I go to this man and hear what he says.” Bujayr went to the Messenger of Allah ﵌ and embraced Islam. When Ka‘b learned of it, he said:

Convey from me to Bujayr a message:
alas, what has someone else led you to?
To a creed upon which you found neither mother nor father,
nor ever found a brother of yours?
Abu Bakr gave you a well-filled cup to drink;
the one commanded made you drain it, and gave it again.

His verses reached the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم, who said, “Whoever encounters Ka‘b, let him kill him,” and declared his blood unprotected. Bujayr wrote this to him, telling him to save himself. He later wrote that no one came to the Prophet as a Muslim without being accepted and having his prior acts set aside. Ka‘b embraced Islam and came, making his camel kneel at the mosque door. He said: I recognized the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم by his description, stepped across the people until I sat before him, embraced Islam, and then said, “Safety, Messenger of Allah! I am Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr.” He said, “Are you the one who says …?” He turned to Abu Bakr and asked, “How does it go?” Abu Bakr recited the three verses. When he said, “The one commanded made you drain it,” I said, “Messenger of Allah, that is not how I said it. I said, ‘the trusted one.’” He replied, “Trusted, by Allah.” Ka‘b recited to him the ode that begins Banat Su‘ad, and the account gives the poem. We received it through a short chain in the large collection of Ibrahim ibn Dizil. Ibn Qani‘ transmitted through al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar, from one of the people of Medina, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When news of Ibn Khatal's killing reached Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr—and he had learned that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم had threatened him as he had threatened Ibn Khatal—Ka‘b was told, “Unless you take steps to save yourself, you will be killed.” He came to Medina and asked which of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم was gentlest. He was directed to Abu Bakr and told him his story. Abu Bakr walked with Ka‘b behind him; Ka‘b had veiled his face. When they stood before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, Abu Bakr said, “A man wishes to pledge allegiance to you.” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم extended his hand, and Ka‘b extended his and pledged allegiance. He then uncovered his face and recited his ode, which contains:

I was told that the Messenger of Allah had threatened me,
yet pardon from the Messenger of Allah is hoped for.

It also contains:

Indeed, the Messenger is a light by which illumination is sought,
an Indian blade, drawn from among the swords of Allah.

The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم clothed him in a mantle of his. Mu‘awiyah later bought it from Ka‘b's descendants, and it is the mantle the caliphs wear on feast days. Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Ahmad ibn al-Miqdam related to us; Umar ibn Ali related to us; Zakariyya—that is, Ibn Abi Za’idah—related to us from al-Sha‘bi, who said: Al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani recited to al-Nu‘man ibn al-Mundhir:

When you die, the earth will see you as light,
though while you live upon it, you are heavy.

Al-Nu‘man told him, “Unless you follow this verse with another that clarifies its meaning, it is closer to satire.” Composition proved difficult for al-Nabighah. Al-Nu‘man said, “I have given you three days. If you produce it, you shall have one hundred ‘sparrow’ camels; otherwise, the sword will strike as far as it strikes.” Al-Nabighah left in fear and met Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, to whom he recounted the matter. Zuhayr said, “Come out with us into the open country.” Ka‘b followed them. Zuhayr sent him back, but al-Nabighah said, “Let my nephew come with us,” and seated him behind himself. Nothing came to either man. Ka‘b said to al-Nabighah, “Uncle, what keeps you from saying:

That is because you dulled the eyes of calamity against her,
and kept her two flanks from inclining?”

Al-Nabighah admired it and went to al-Nu‘man the next morning to recite it. He gave him the hundred camels, which al-Nabighah offered to Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr, but Ka‘b refused to accept them. Ibn Durayd related the story differently in his Amali. He said: Al-Sakan ibn Sa‘id informed us; Muhammad ibn Abbad related to us; Ibn al-Kalbi related to us, saying: Al-Nabighah visited Zuhayr, who slaughtered an animal for him and honored him. Drink was brought, and they sat. Poetry was proposed to them, and al-Nabighah recited the first verse, followed by:

You alighted at her abode of might …

Then he stopped and asked Zuhayr to complete it, but nothing occurred to either of them. Ka‘b was then playing in the dirt with the boys. He came over and saw each man with his chin on his chest, thinking. He asked, “Father, why do I see you turbaned?” His father said, “Move away, may you lose your mother.” Al-Nabighah called him onto his thigh and recited the verse. Ka‘b said, “What keeps you from saying:

And kept her two flanks from inclining?”

His father embraced him and said, “My son, by the Lord of the Ka‘bah!” Abu Ahmad al-Askari said that Zuhayr died before the prophetic mission. Ibn Ishaq said that Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr came after al-Ta’if. Khalaf al-Ahmar said, “Were it not for certain odes by Zuhayr, I would not rank him above his son Ka‘b.” Zuhayr, his sons Bujayr and Ka‘b, and Ka‘b's sons Uqbah and al-Awwam were all poets. Al-Hutay’ah said to Ka‘b ibn Zuhayr, “You are a household to whom people look in poetry, so mention me in your poetry,” and he did. Abu Umar counted among Ka‘b's fine poetry:

Were I to marvel at anything, I would marvel
at a young man's striving while fate lies hidden for him.
The young man strives for things he cannot attain;
the soul is one, while its concerns are scattered.
As long as a man lives, hope is stretched out before him;
the eye does not cease until the track itself ends.

records.english: ibn Mālik ibn Kaʿb ibn Harithah ibn Dinar ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari. Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ibn Shihab, included him among those who witnessed Badr. Ibn Ishaq did likewise and said that he was martyred at the Trench. Ibn Ishaq said that a stray arrow struck and killed him, while al-Waqidi said that Dirar ibn al-Khattab killed him. Abu Nu‘aym mistakenly included the story of the Ghifari woman in his biography; that concerns another man called Zayd ibn Ka‘b, or, according to another view, Ka‘b ibn Zayd.

records.english: ibn Asad, also called Ka‘b ibn Hayyan al-Qurazi, Muhammad's father. He was among the captives of Qurayzah whose lineage was not known, and no narration by him is known. Ibn Abd al-Barr said this. Ibn Hibban included him among the trustworthy Successors and said: He related from Ali, and his son related from him. Ibn Mandah cited a hadith in his biography but erred in doing so; it has been mentioned in the biography of Abd al-Rahman al-Khatmi.

records.arabic: الأشعري قال المزني الصحيح انه غير أبي مالك الأشعري الذي يروي عنه عبد الرحمن بن غنم فان ذلك معروف بكنيته وهذا معروف باسمه لا بكنيته انتهى وكل من صنف في الكنى كنى هذا أيضا أبا مالك منهم النسائي والدولابي وأبو أحمد الحاكم وأطال أبو أحمد القول فيه وقال إعتمدت في كنيته على حديث إسماعيل بن عبد الله بن خالد عن أبيه عن جده قال سمعت أبا مالك الأشعري كعب بن عاصم يقول فذكر حديثا قال البخاري له صحبة قال إسماعيل بن أويس كنيته أبو مالك وقال البغوي سكن كعب بن عاصم مصر روت عنه أم الدرداء وحديثه عند أحمد والنسائي وابن ماجة وغيرهم ليس من البر الصيام في السفر ووقع عند أحمد بالميم بدل لام التعريف في الثلاثة في البر وفي الصوم وفي السفر وجاء عنه حديث آخر من رواية جابر بن عبد الله عنه انه رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يخطب عند الجمرة أوسط أيام النحر أخرجه البغوي وقال غريب وأخرجه بن السكن
records.english: al-Ashʿarī. al-Muzanī said: The correct view is that he is someone other than Abu Malik al-Ash‘ari, from whom Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm relates, for the latter is known by his kunyah while this man is known by his name, not by a kunyah. End quote. Yet everyone who wrote on kunyahs also gave this man the kunyah Abu Malik, including al-Nasa’i, al-Dulabi, and Abu Ahmad al-Hakim. Abu Ahmad discussed the matter at length and said, “For his kunyah I relied on the hadith of Isma‘il ibn Abd Allah ibn Khalid, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: I heard Abu Malik al-Ash‘ari, Ka‘b ibn Asim, say …” and he mentioned a hadith. Al-Bukhari said that he had companionship. Isma‘il ibn Uways said that his kunyah was Abu Malik. Al-Baghawi said: Ka‘b ibn Asim lived in Egypt, and Umm al-Darda’ related from him. His hadith, found in Ahmad, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and others, says: “Fasting while traveling is not an act of righteousness.” Ahmad's version substitutes mim for the definite article's lam in all three words: “in righteousness,” “fasting,” and “while traveling.” Another hadith is related from him by Jabir ibn Abd Allah: he saw the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم delivering a sermon at the middle stoning place during the days of sacrifice. Al-Baghawi transmitted it and called it uncommon; Ibn al-Sakan also transmitted it.

records.english: al-Saʿdī. He was a Companion, according to Ja‘far al-Mustaghfiri. Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the Companions but called him al-Sa‘idi. Al-Bawardi likewise transmitted, through Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Rafi‘ in his naming of the Companions who witnessed Siffin with Ali: “Ka‘b ibn Amir, of Banu Sa‘idah, a veteran of Badr.” That is what he said, but his chain is exceedingly weak.

records.arabic: بن أمية بن عدي بن عبيد بن خالد بن عمرو بن عوف بن غنم بن سواد بن مري بن أراشة البلوي ويقال بن خالد عن عمرو بن زيد بن ليث بن سواد بن أسلم القضاعي حليف الأنصار وزعم الواقدي انه أنصاري من أنفسهم ورده كاتبه محمد بن سعد بان قال طلبت نسبه في الأنصار فلم أجده وكذا أطلق انه أنصاري البخاري وقال مدني له صحبة يكنى أبا محمد ذكره بن سعد بإسناده وقيل كنيته أبو إسحاق بابنه إسحاق وقيل أبو عبد الله روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحاديث وعن عمر وشهد عمرة الحديبية ونزلت فيه قصة الفدية وقد أخرج ذلك في الصحيحين من طرق منها رواية بن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن كعب بن هجرة ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم مر به وهو محرم يوقد تحت قدر والقمل يتهافت على وجهه فقال له احلق رأسك واطعم فرقا بين ستة مساكين الحديث في بعض طرقه ما كنت اظن ان الوجع بلغ ما نرى وفيها قال كعب فكانت لي خاصة وهي لكم عامة ومن مستغرب طرق قصته ما أخرجه بن المقري في فوائده من طريق عبد الله بن سليمان الطويل عن نافع ان رجلا من الأنصار أخبره ان كعب بن عجرة من بني سالم كان أصابه في رأسه أذى فحلقه فقال للنبي صلى الله علي وآله وسلم فماذا انسك فامره ان يهدي بقرة يقلدها ثم يسوقها ثم يقفها بعرفة ثم يدفع بها مع الناس وكذلك يفعل بالهدى ويعارضه ما أخرجه البغوي من طريق أبان بن صالح عن الحسن قال قال رجل لكعب بن عجرة يا أبا محمد ما كانت فديتك قال شاة واخرج الطبراني في الأوسط من طريق ضمام بن إسماعيل عن موسى بن وردان عن كعب بن عجرة قال أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوما فرأيته متغيرا فذهبت فإذا يهودي يسقى ابلا له فسقيت له على كل دلو بتمرة فجمعت تمرا فاتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الحديث واخرج بن سعد بسند جيد عن ثابت بن عبيد ان يد كعب قطعت في بعض المغازي ثم سكن الكوفة روى عنه بن عمر وجابر وابن عباس وطارق بن شهاب وزيد بن وهب وآخرون وروى عنه أيضا أولاده إسحاق ومحمد وعبد الملك والربيع قيل مات بالمدينة سنة إحدى وقيل ثنتين وقيل ثلاث وخمسين وله خمس وقيل سبع وسبعون سنة
records.english: ibn Umayyah ibn ʿAdī ibn Ubayd ibn Khalid ibn Amr ibn Awf ibn Ghanm ibn Sawad ibn Murri ibn Urashah al-Balawi. It is also said: ibn Khalid, from Amr ibn Zayd ibn Layth ibn Sawad ibn Aslam al-Quda‘i, an ally of the Ansar. Al-Waqidi claimed that he was himself an Ansari, but his scribe Muhammad ibn Sa‘d rejected this, saying, “I searched for his lineage among the Ansar and did not find it.” Al-Bukhari likewise simply called him an Ansari and said that he was a Medinan Companion whose kunyah was Abu Muhammad. Ibn Sa‘d mentioned this with his chain. It is also said that his kunyah was Abu Ishaq, after his son Ishaq, or Abu Abd Allah. He related hadiths from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and from Umar. He witnessed the Lesser Pilgrimage of al-Hudaybiyah, and the account of the expiation was revealed concerning him. It is transmitted in the two Sahih collections through several routes, including the report of Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ka‘b ibn Ujrah: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم passed him while Ka‘b, in a state of consecration, was kindling a fire beneath a pot and lice were falling over his face. He told him, “Shave your head and feed a faraq measure among six poor people,” continuing the hadith. One route says, “I did not think the affliction had reached the extent we see.” It also says that Ka‘b said, “It applied specifically to me, but it applies generally to you.” Among the unusual routes for his account is one transmitted by Ibn al-Muqri’ in his Fawa’id through Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Tawil, from Nafi‘, that a man of the Ansar informed him that Ka‘b ibn Ujrah of Banu Salim suffered an ailment in his head and shaved it. He asked the Prophet ﵌, “What sacrificial rite should I now perform?” He ordered him to offer a cow, place a garland around it, drive it, have it stand at Arafah, then move on with it when the people moved on, doing the same with the sacrificial animal. This is contradicted by al-Baghawi's report through Aban ibn Salih, from al-Hasan, who said: A man asked Ka‘b ibn Ujrah, “Abu Muhammad, what was your expiation?” He replied, “A sheep.” Al-Tabarani transmitted in al-Awsat through Dimam ibn Isma‘il, from Musa ibn Wardan, from Ka‘b ibn Ujrah, who said: I came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم one day and saw that his appearance had changed. I went away and found a Jew watering camels. I drew water for him, receiving one date for each bucket, collected the dates, and brought them to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم—and he continued the hadith. Ibn Sa‘d transmitted with a good chain from Thabit ibn Ubayd that Ka‘b's hand was severed on one of the military expeditions. He later settled in Kufa. Ibn Umar, Jabir, Ibn Abbas, Tariq ibn Shihab, Zayd ibn Wahb, and others related from him. His sons Ishaq, Muhammad, Abd al-Malik, and al-Rabi‘ also related from him. It is said that he died in Medina in the year fifty-one, fifty-two, or fifty-three, at the age of seventy-five or seventy-seven.

records.arabic: التنوخي مخرج حديثه عن أهل مصر روى عنه ناعم بن اجيل حديثا حسنا هكذا اختصره بن عبد البر ونسبه بن منده عن بن يونس فقال بن عدي بن عمرو بن ثعلبة بن عدي بن ملكان بن عذرة بن زيد اللات هو الذي يقال له التنوخي لان ملكان بن عوف حلفاء تنوخ وهم العباد بكسر المهملة وتخفيف الموحدة بالحيرة وهكذا قال بن يونس في تاريخ مصر قال بن السكن يقال ان له صحبة وقال البغوي وابن قانع عنه حدثنا أبو الأحوص محمد بن الهيثم أبنأنا سعيد بن جبير بن عفير حدثني عبد الحميد بن كعب بن علقمة بن كعب بن عدي التنوخي عن عمرو بن الحارث عن ناعم بن اجيل بالجيم مصغرا عن كعب بن عدي قال أقبلت في وفد من أهل الحيرة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فعرض علينا الإسلام فأسلمنا ثم انصرفنا إلى الحيرة فلم نلبث ان جاءتنا وفاة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فارتاب أصحابي وقالوا لو كان نبيا لم يمت فقلت فقد مات الأنبياء قبله فثبت على الإسلام ثم خرجت أريد المدينة فمررت براهب كنا لا نقطع أمرا دونه فعجت اليه فقلت أخبرني عن أمر اردته لقح في صدري منه شيء قال ائت باسمك من الأشياء فأتيته بكعب قال القه في هذا الشعر لشعر أخرجه فألقيت الكعب فيه فإذا بصفة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما رأيته وإذا موته في الحين الذي مات فيه فاشتدت بصيرتي في ايماني فقدمت على أبي بكر فاعلمته واقمت عنده ووجهني إلى المقوقس ورجعت ثم وجهني عمر أيضا فقدمت عليه بكتباه بعد وقعة اليرموك ولم اعلم بها فقال لي علمت ان الروم قتلت العرب وهزمتهم قلت لا قالا ولم قلت لان الله وعد نبيه ليظهره على الدين كله وليس يخلف الميعاد قال فان العرب قتلت الروم والله قتلة عاد وان نبيكم قد صدق ثم سألني عن وجوه الصحابة فاهدي لهم وقلت له ان العباس عمه حي فتصله قال كعب وكنت شريكا لعمر بن الخطاب فلما فرض الديوان فرض لي في بني عدي بن كعب وقال البغوي لا اعلم لكعب بن عدي غيره وهكذا أخرجه بن قانع عن البغوي ولكنه اقتصر منه إلى قوله مات الأنبياء قبله وابن شاهين عن أبيه عن أبي الأحوص بطوله وأبو نعيم عن أبي العباس الصرصري عن البغوي بطوله وأخرجه بن السكن بطوله عن شيخ آخر عن أبي الأحوص ومن رواية عبد الله بن سعيد بن عفير عن أبيه بطوله وزاد فيه فالقيت الكعب فيه فصحف فيه وقال فيها وكنت شريكا لعمر في البز قال بن السكن رواه غيره سعد فادخل بين عمرو بن حريث وناعم يزيد بن أبي حبيب قلت أخرجها بن يونس في تاريخ مصر من طريق إبراهيم بن أبي داود البرلسي انه قرأ في كتاب عمرو بن الحارث بخطه حدثني يزيد بن أبي حبيب أن ناعما حدثه عن كعب بن عدي قال كان أبي اسقف الحيرة فلما بعث محمد قال هل لكم ان يذهب نفر منكم إلى هذا الرجل فتسمعوا من قوله لا يموت غدا فتقولوا لو انا سمعنا من قوله وقد كان علي حق فاختاروا أربعة فبعثوهم فقلت لأبي انا انطلق معهم قال ما تصنع قلت انظر فقدمنا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكنا نجلس اليه إذا صلى الصبح فنسمع كلامه والقرآن ولا ينكرنا أحد فلم نلبث الا يسيرا حتى مات فقال لاربعة لو كان امره حقا لم يمت انطلقوا فقلت كما أنتم حتى تعلموا من يقوم مكانه فينقطع هذا الأمر أم يتم فذهبوا ومكثت انا لا مسلما ولا نصرانيا فلما بعث أبو بكر جيشا إلى اليمامة ذهبت معهم فلما فرغوا مررت براهب فذكر قصة معه وقال فيها فوقع في قلبي الإيمان فآمنت حينئذ فمررت على الحيرة فعيروني فقدمت على عمر وقد مات أبو بكر فبعثني إلى المقوقس فذكر نحوه ثم اخرج بن يونس رواية سعيد بن عفير وقال الصواب ما في الكتاب لم يسمعه عمرو بن ناعم قلت اعتمد بن يونس على ما في هذه الرواية فقال في أول الترجمة كان أحد وفد أهل الحيرة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يسلم واسلم زمن أبي بكر وكان شريك عمر في الجاهلية في تجارة البز وقدم الإسكندرية سنة خمس عشرة رسولا من عمر إلى المقوقس وشهد فتح مصر واختط بها وكان ولده بمصر يأخذون العطاء في بني عدي بن كعب حتى نقلهم أمير مصر في زمن يزيد بن عبد الملك إلى ديوان قضاعة وولده بمصر من عبد الحميد بن كعب بن علقمة بن كعب بن عدي وله بمصر حديث فذكره وتبع بن يونس أبو عبد الله بن منده وأخرج الحديث عن بن يونس من طريق يزيد بن أبي حبيب المذكورة وقال قال بن يونس هكذا وجدته في الدرج والرق القديم الذي حدثني به محمد بن موسى عن بن أبي داود عن كتاب عمرو بن الحارث قال بن منده غريب لا نعرفه الا من هذا الوجه وكان سياق سند سعيد بن عفير بعلو من روايته عن أحمد القاري عن عبيد الله بن سعيد عن أبيه ولم يسق المتن بلى قرنه برواية يزيد بن أبي حبيب وبينهما من المخالفة ان في رواية سعيد بن عفير انه اسلم عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي رواية يزيد بن أبي حبيب انه لم يسلم إلى في عهد أبي بكر ويمكن الجمع بين الروايتين بأنه ليس في رواية يزيد بن أبي حبيب انه لم يسلم بل سكت عن ذلك وذكر انه بعد موت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أقام لا مسلما ولا نصرانيا وفي رواية سعيد التصريح بإسلامه عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذكر بعد ذلك انه ازداد يقينا في ايمانه فيحمل على انه بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقع له تردد فصار في حكم من رجع عن الإسلام فلما شاهد نصرة المسلمين مرة بعد مرة رجح عنده الإسلام وعاوده اليقين فعلى هذا يعد في الصحابة لأنه لو تخللت له ردة صريحة ثم عاد استمر له اسم الصحبة كالأشعث بن قيس وغيره ممن ارتد وعاد وقد كنت اعتمدت على قول بن يونس وكتبته في المخضرمين ثم رجح عندي ما في رواية بن عفير فحولته إلى هذا القسم الأول وبالله التوفيق وأورد بن منده في ترجمته قصة له تتضمن رواية أبي ثور الفهمي عنه أخرجها من طريق بن وهب أخبرني عبد الرحمن بن شريح عن يزيد بن عمرو عن أبي ثور الفهمي قال كعب العبادي عقيدا لعمر بن الخطاب في الجاهلية فقدم الإسكندرية فوافق لهم عيدا يكون على رأس مائة سنة فهم مجتمعون فحضر معهم حتى إذا فرغوا قام فيهم من يناديهم أيها الناس أيكم أدرك عيدنا الماضي فيخبرنا أيهما أفضل فلم يجبه أحد حتى ردد فيهم فقال اعلموا أنه ليس أحد يدرك عيدنا المقبل مما لم يدرك هذا العيد من شهد العيد الماضي قال بن يونس وكان هذا العيد عندهم معروفا بالإسكندرية إلى بعد الثلاثمائة ووقع لصاحب أسد الغابة في ترجمته وكان أحد وفد الحيرة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زمن أبي بكر وكان شريك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الجاهلية وقدم الإسكندرية سنة خمس عشرة رسولا لعمر إلى المقوقس وشهد فتح مصر وهذا نقله من كلام بن منده ولكن ليس عند بن منده الا ما عند غيره ممن ترجم له وهو انه كان شريكا لعمر بن الخطاب وقد وقع ذلك في رواية أبي ثور الفهمي أيضا
records.english: al-Tanūkhī. The source of his report is through the people of Egypt. Na‘im ibn Ajil related a fair hadith from him. Ibn Abd al-Barr abridged his notice in these words. Ibn Mandah, citing Ibn Yunus, gave his lineage as Ibn Adi ibn Amr ibn Tha‘labah ibn Adi ibn Malkan ibn Udhrah ibn Zayd al-Lat. He is called al-Tanukhi because Malkan ibn Awf were allies of Tanukh; they were the Ibad—with kasrah on the unpointed letter and a single ba—of al-Hirah. Ibn Yunus said the same in Tarikh Misr. Ibn al-Sakan said that it was reported that he had companionship. Al-Baghawi and Ibn Qani‘ related from him: Abu al-Ahwas Muhammad ibn al-Haytham related to us; Sa‘id ibn Jubayr ibn Ufair informed us; Abd al-Hamid ibn Ka‘b ibn Alqamah ibn Ka‘b ibn Adi al-Tanukhi related to me, from Amr ibn al-Harith, from Na‘im ibn Ajil—the latter name with jim, in the diminutive—from Ka‘b ibn Adi, who said: I came in a delegation from the people of al-Hirah to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. He presented Islam to us, and we embraced it. We then returned to al-Hirah. It was not long before news of the death of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم reached us. My companions fell into doubt and said, “Had he been a prophet, he would not have died.” I said, “Prophets before him have died,” and remained firm in Islam. I then set out for Medina. I passed a monk without whose counsel we used to decide nothing, so I turned aside to him and said, “Tell me about a matter I have intended, concerning which something has arisen in my breast.” He said, “Bring me an object that bears your name.” I brought him a ka‘b, or die. He said, “Cast it among this hair,” producing some hair. I cast the die into it and there found the description of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم exactly as I had seen him, as well as his death at the very time he died. My insight and certainty in my faith grew strong. I came to Abu Bakr, informed him, and stayed with him. He sent me to al-Muqawqis, and I returned. Umar later sent me as well. I brought al-Muqawqis Umar's letter after the Battle of Yarmuk, though I had not learned of it. He said to me, “Did you know that the Byzantines killed and defeated the Arabs?” I said, “No.” He asked, “Why not?” I replied, “Because Allah promised His Prophet that He would make him prevail over all religion, and He does not break His promise.” He said, “Rather, the Arabs have killed the Byzantines—by Allah, killing them like Ad—and your Prophet has spoken the truth.” He then asked me about the leading Companions so that he might send gifts to them. I told him that al-Abbas, the Prophet's uncle, was alive, so he sent him a gift. Ka‘b said: I had been Umar ibn al-Khattab's business partner. When he established the military registers, he assigned me a stipend among Banu Adi ibn Ka‘b. Al-Baghawi said, “I know no other hadith of Ka‘b ibn Adi.” Ibn Qani‘ likewise transmitted it from al-Baghawi, but only as far as the words, “Prophets before him have died.” Ibn Shahin transmitted it in full from his father, from Abu al-Ahwas; Abu Nu‘aym transmitted it in full from Abu al-Abbas al-Sarsari, from al-Baghawi; and Ibn al-Sakan transmitted it in full from another shaykh, from Abu al-Ahwas, and also through Abd Allah ibn Sa‘id ibn Ufair, from his father. The latter adds, “I cast the die into it,” but the word “into it” is a scribal corruption. It also says, “I was Umar's partner in the cloth trade.” Ibn al-Sakan said: Another narrator, Sa‘d, related it and inserted Yazid ibn Abi Habib between Amr ibn al-Harith and Na‘im. I say: Ibn Yunus transmitted it in Tarikh Misr through Ibrahim ibn Abi Dawud al-Burullusi, who read in a book written in Amr ibn al-Harith's own hand: Yazid ibn Abi Habib related to me that Na‘im related to him from Ka‘b ibn Adi, who said: My father was the bishop of al-Hirah. When Muhammad was sent, he said, “Would some of you go to this man and listen to what he says, lest he die tomorrow and you say, ‘If only we had heard his teaching’?” I was under an obligation to him. They chose four and sent them. I told my father, “I will go with them.” He asked, “What will you do?” I said, “I will see.” We came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم. We would sit with him after he prayed the dawn prayer, listening to his speech and the Qur’an, and no one objected to our presence. It was only a short time before he died. The four said, “Had his cause been true, he would not have died. Let us depart.” I said, “Stay where you are until you learn whether someone will take his place and this affair will end, or whether it will continue.” They left, while I remained, neither a Muslim nor a Christian. When Abu Bakr sent an army to al-Yamamah, I went with them. After they finished, I passed a monk—and he related his story with the monk. He said, “Faith entered my heart and I believed at that time.” I passed through al-Hirah, where they reproached me. I came to Umar, Abu Bakr having died, and Umar sent me to al-Muqawqis. He then related something similar. Ibn Yunus next cited Sa‘id ibn Ufair's version and said that the correct account is the one in the book: Amr did not hear it from Na‘im. I say: Ibn Yunus relied on this version and began the biography by saying: He was one of the delegation from al-Hirah to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم, but he did not embrace Islam; he embraced Islam in Abu Bakr's time. He had been Umar's partner in the cloth trade in the pre-Islamic period. He came to Alexandria in the year fifteen as Umar's envoy to al-Muqawqis, witnessed the conquest of Egypt, and marked out a residence there. His descendants in Egypt received their stipends among Banu Adi ibn Ka‘b until Egypt's governor, in the time of Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik, transferred them to Quda‘ah's military register. His descendants in Egypt were through Abd al-Hamid ibn Ka‘b ibn Alqamah ibn Ka‘b ibn Adi. He has a hadith in Egypt. Ibn Yunus then cited it. Abu Abd Allah ibn Mandah followed Ibn Yunus and transmitted the hadith from him by the aforementioned route through Yazid ibn Abi Habib. He said: Ibn Yunus said, “This is how I found it on the roll and the old parchment that Muhammad ibn Musa related to me, from Ibn Abi Dawud, from the book of Amr ibn al-Harith.” Ibn Mandah said: “It is uncommon; we know it only by this route.” He had given the chain of Sa‘id ibn Ufair in abbreviated form in his report from Ahmad al-Qari, from Ubayd Allah ibn Sa‘id, from his father, without setting out the text; rather, he joined it to the version of Yazid ibn Abi Habib. The two versions differ: Sa‘id ibn Ufair's version says that he embraced Islam in the presence of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, while Yazid ibn Abi Habib's version says that he did not embrace Islam until Abu Bakr's reign. The two can be reconciled, because Yazid ibn Abi Habib's report does not actually say that he had not embraced Islam; it is silent on that point and says only that, after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم died, he remained neither a Muslim nor a Christian. Sa‘id's version explicitly states that he embraced Islam before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and later grew in certainty in his faith. This may be understood to mean that doubt befell him after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم died, placing him under the ruling of one who had left Islam; then, after repeatedly witnessing the Muslims' victory, Islam became preponderant for him and certainty returned. On this understanding he is counted among the Companions, for even if an explicit apostasy intervened and he then returned, the designation of companionship continued to apply to him, as with al-Ash‘ath ibn Qays and others who apostatized and returned. I had relied on Ibn Yunus's statement and listed him among the mukhadramun, but Sa‘id ibn Ufair's version later appeared stronger to me, so I moved him to this first section. وبالله التوفيق. Ibn Mandah also included in his biography an account related by Abu Thawr al-Fahmi from him. He transmitted it through Ibn Wahb: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh informed me, from Yazid ibn Amr, from Abu Thawr al-Fahmi, who said: Ka‘b al-Ibadi, Umar ibn al-Khattab's contract partner in the pre-Islamic period, came to Alexandria. He arrived when they were holding a festival that occurred once every hundred years. They were assembled, and he remained with them until they finished. Someone then stood and called out, “People, which of you was present at our previous festival, so that he may tell us which of the two was better?” No one answered, even after he repeated the question among them. He said, “Know that no one present at our next festival will be among those who did not witness this festival, or among those who witnessed the last festival.” Ibn Yunus said that this festival remained known among them in Alexandria until after the year three hundred. The author of Usd al-Ghabah wrote in his biography: “He was one of the delegation from al-Hirah to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم in the time of Abu Bakr, was the Prophet's صلى الله عليه وسلم business partner in the pre-Islamic period, and came to Alexandria in the year fifteen as Umar's envoy to al-Muqawqis and witnessed the conquest of Egypt.” He copied this from Ibn Mandah's words, but Ibn Mandah has only what the others who wrote his biography have: namely, that he was Umar ibn al-Khattab's partner. The same is also stated in Abu Thawr al-Fahmi's version.

records.arabic: الأنصاري روى حديثه عبد الله بن وهب عن مسلمة بن علي عن سعيد بن عبد العزيز عن رجل من قريش ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما حاصر خيبر جاع بعض الناس فافتتحوا حصنا من حصونها فأخذ بعض المسلمين جراب شحم فبصر به صاحب المغانم وهو كعب بن عمرو بن زيد الأنصاري فأخذه منه فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خل بينه وبين جرابه فذهب به إلى اصحابه وفي سنده مع انقطاعه ضعف وقد وقع في الصحيح عن عبد الله بن مغفل قصة له في جراب شحم أخذه يوم خيبر فكأنه المراد بقوله في هذه الرواية بعض المسلمين وذكر أبو عمر في العبادلة عبد الله بن كعب بن عمرو بن عوف كان على المغانم ببدر والذي يظهر انه غير هذا
records.english: al-Anṣārī. His report was transmitted by Abd Allah ibn Wahb from Maslamah ibn Ali, from Sa‘id ibn Abd al-Aziz, from a man of Quraysh: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم besieged Khaybar, some of the people grew hungry. They opened one of its forts, and one of the Muslims took a leather bag of fat. The official in charge of the spoils, Ka‘b ibn Amr ibn Zayd al-Ansari, saw him and took it away. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم said, “Leave him with his bag,” and he took it to his companions. In addition to the break in its chain, the report is weak. The Sahih contains an account about Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal and a bag of fat he took on the day of Khaybar. He appears to be the person meant by “one of the Muslims” in this version. Abu Umar mentioned among the men named Abd Allah: Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Amr ibn Awf, who was in charge of the spoils at Badr. It appears that he is someone else.

records.english: ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb ibn Mu‘awiyah ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar al-Ansari. He witnessed Uhud and the campaigns that followed and was martyred at al-Yamamah. Al-Adawi mentioned him, and Ibn Fathun and Ibn al-Athir added him.

names.arabic: كعب بن عمرو بن عبيد بن الحارث بن كعب بن معاوية بن مالك بن النجار الأنصاري

records.arabic: اليامي بتحتانية باثنتين جد بن مصرف وقيل هو عمرو بن كعب بن مصرف حديثه عند أبي داود ويأتي المبهمات
records.english: al-Yāmī, with an initial yāʾ bearing two dots beneath—the grandfather of Ibn Masraf. It is also said that he was Amr ibn Ka‘b ibn Masraf. His hadith is found in Abu Dawud. He will appear among the anonymous reports.

names.arabic: كعب بن عمرو بن مصرف اليامي
names.english: Ka‘b ibn Amr ibn Masraf al-Yami

records.arabic: الخزاعي قيل هو اسم خويلد بن عمرو وخويلد أشهر يأتي في الكنى
records.english: al-Khuzāʿī. It is said this was the name of Khuwaylid ibn ʿAmr, but Khuwaylid is better known. He will appear in the section on kunyahs.

records.arabic: الشاعر يأتي في الكنى واختلف في اسمه فقيل كعب وقيل عبد الله وقيل عامر بن كعب وقيل كعب بن عامر وذكر فيمن شهد صفين مع على والسند بذلك ضعيف
records.english: the poet; he appears among the kunyās. There is disagreement over his name: it is said to have been Ka‘b, Abd Allah, Amir ibn Ka‘b, or Ka‘b ibn Amir. He is mentioned among those who witnessed Siffin with Ali, but the chain for this is weak.

records.arabic: الغفاري قال أبو عمر من كبار الصحابة أمره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على سرية فقتل ذكره موسى بن عقبة عن بن شهاب وأبو الأسود عن عروة قالا بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كعب بن عمير الغفاري نحو ذات أطلاح من البلقاء فاصيب كعب ومن معه وذكره بن سعد في الطبقة الثالثة وان قصته كانت في ربيع الأول سنة ثمان وفيه فقتل أصحابه جميعا وتحامل هو حتى بلغ المدينة كذا قال وقد ساق شيخه الواقدي القصة ولكن فيها فتحامل رجل جريج في القتلى لما برد الليل فنحا وهكذا ذكره بن إسحاق عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر وان كعب بن عمير قتل يومئذ
records.english: al-Ghifārī. Abū ʿUmar said that he was one of the senior Companions. The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم placed him in command of an expedition, and he was killed. Musa ibn Uqbah, from Ibn Shihab, and Abu al-Aswad, from Urwah, both mentioned him. They said: The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم sent Ka‘b ibn Umayr al-Ghifari toward Dhat Atlah in al-Balqa’, and Ka‘b and those with him were struck down. Ibn Sa‘d placed him in the third class and said that his account occurred in Rabi al-Awwal of the year eight. His account says that all his companions were killed and that he forced himself onward until he reached Medina. That is what he said, although his shaykh al-Waqidi related the account with the wording, “A wounded man lay among the dead, and when the night grew cool, he slipped away.” Ibn Ishaq likewise mentioned, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, that Ka‘b ibn Umayr was killed that day.

records.arabic: الأشعري ذكره البخاري وقال له صحبة عداده في أهل الشام وقال بن السكن له صحبة وقال مسلم تفرد عنه جبير بن نفير بالرواية وتبعه بن السكن والازدي وأفاد بن عبد البر أن جابر بن عبد الله روى عنه وقال البغوي ماله غير حديث واحد وهو الذي أخرجه له الترمذي والنسائي في قنية المال وقد أخرج له بن قانع وابن السكن آخر وهو حديث القصاص ثلاثة من رواية جبير بن نفير أيضا عنه وأخرج له الدارمي ثالثا وهو لو كان لابن آدم واديان من مال وكأنها من رواية عبد الرحمن بن جبير بن نفير عن أبيه عنه وأخرج له الدارقطني رابعا من رواية خالد بن معد ان عنه وهو منقطع وأخرجه بن أبي داود وابن شاهين من طريق معاوية بن صالح أيضا لكن عن أبي الزاهرية عن جبير بن نفير عنه وصرح في رواية البخاري عن أبي صالح أيضا لكن عن معاوية أبي صالح بسماعه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال أبو عمر حديثه في قنية المال صحيح وقد روى عنه جابر وقيل أن أم الدرداء روت عنه انتهى وفي قوله جابر نظر وانما روى جابر عن كعب بن عاصم وكذا رواية أم الدرداء إنما هي عن كعب بن عاصم
records.english: al-Ashʿarī. al-Bukhārī mentioned him and said that he had companionship and was counted among the people of Syria. Ibn al-Sakan also said that he had companionship. Muslim said that Jubayr ibn Nufayr alone related from him; Ibn al-Sakan and al-Azdi followed him in this. Ibn Abd al-Barr added that Jabir ibn Abd Allah related from him. Al-Baghawi said, “He has only one hadith,” namely the one al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i transmitted concerning the temptation of wealth. Ibn Qani‘ and Ibn al-Sakan transmitted another, the hadith that retaliation is threefold, also related from him by Jubayr ibn Nufayr. Al-Darimi transmitted a third, “If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth,” apparently from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from his father, from Ka‘b. Al-Daraqutni transmitted a fourth from Khalid ibn Ma‘dan, from him, but its chain is disconnected. Ibn Abi Dawud and Ibn Shahin transmitted it through Mu‘awiyah ibn Salih as well, but from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from him. In al-Bukhari's version, through Abu Salih as well—but from Mu‘awiyah Abu Salih—he explicitly says that he heard it from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Abu Umar said: “His hadith concerning the temptation of wealth is sound. Jabir related from him, and it is said that Umm al-Darda’ related from him.” End quote. His statement concerning Jabir is questionable; Jabir related from Ka‘b ibn Asim. Likewise, Umm al-Darda’ related only from Ka‘b ibn Asim.

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن جبير بن نفير
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr

records.arabic: بن عائشة التميمي تقدم ذكر أبيه في العين قال الحاكم في تاريخه كعب بن عيينة صحابي ذكر سلمويه بن صالح انه ورد خراسان مع عبد الله بن عامر وله عقب بمرو واستدركه يحيى بن عبد الوهاب بن عبد الله على كتاب جده في الصحابة
records.english: ibn ʿĀʾishah al-Tamīmī. His father has been mentioned above under the letter ayn. Al-Hakim said in his Tarikh: “Ka‘b ibn Uyaynah was a Companion. Salmuwayh ibn Salih mentioned that he entered Khurasan with Abd Allah ibn Amir. He had descendants in Marw.” Yahya ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd Allah added him to his grandfather's book on the Companions.

names.arabic: كعب بن عيينة بن عائشة التميمي
names.english: Ka‘b ibn Uyaynah ibn A’ishah al-Tamimi

names.arabic: يحيى بن عبد الوهاب بن عبد الله
names.english: Yahya ibn Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd Allah

records.arabic: القرشي ذكر وثيمة انه كان رسول أبي بكر الصديق إلى خالد بن الوليد بعد فتح اليمامة انتهى وقد تقدم انه لم يبق قرشي في ذلك العصر الا اسلم وشهد حجة الوداع
records.english: al-Qurashī. Wathīmah mentioned that he was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq's messenger to Khalid ibn al-Walid after the conquest of al-Yamamah. End quote. It has already been stated that no Qurashi remained in that period without embracing Islam and witnessing the Farewell Pilgrimage.

records.arabic: ذكره الطبراني في المعجم الكبير ولم يذكر له شيئا وقال أبو أحمد العسكري احسب خبره مرسلا قلت كأنه وقع له بالعنعنة لكن وقع عند غيره بالتصريح وقال بن منده له ذكر في حديث أبي رزين العقيلي كذا قال بن الأمين ووهم فان كلام بن منده هذا إنما قاله في كعب بن الخدارية كما مضى وأورد الطبراني في الأوسط في ترجمة أحمد بن زهير التستري بسنده إلى علي بن ربيعة عن كعب بن قطبة سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ان كذبا على ليس ككذب على أحد الحديث وسنده صحيح الا انه اختلف في صحابيه فرواه إسحاق الأزرق عن سعيد بن عبيد عن علي بن ربيعة هكذا وخالفه أبو نعيم فقال عن سعيد عن علي بن ربيعة عن المغيرة بن شعبة أخرجه البخاري في الأدب عن أبي نعيم والطبراني في ترجمة المغيرة بن شعبة عن علي بن عبد العزيز عن أبي نعيم وفيه قصة النوح على قرظة بن كعب وكذا أخرجه مسلم والترمذي من طرق عن سعيد بن عبيد وأخرجه بن قانع من طريق إسحاق الأزرق عن شيخ الطبراني فقال كعب بن علقمة وهو وهم ولعل سبب الوهم ذكر قرظة بن كعب فلعله صحف وقلب والله اعلم
records.english: al-Ṭabarānī mentioned him in al-Mu‘jam al-Kabir but related nothing for him. Abu Ahmad al-Askari said, “I consider his report to be mursal.” I say: It appears that the report reached him with an ambiguous “from,” but elsewhere the hearing is stated explicitly. Ibn Mandah said that he is mentioned in the hadith of Abu Razin al-Uqayli. Ibn al-Amin said this, but it is an error, for Ibn Mandah said those words only about Ka‘b ibn al-Khadariyyah, as noted above. In al-Awsat, under the entry for Ahmad ibn Zuhayr al-Tustari, al-Tabarani cited with his chain from Ali ibn Rabi‘ah, from Ka‘b ibn Qutbah: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “A lie against me is not like a lie against anyone else,” continuing the hadith. Its chain is sound, except that there is disagreement about which Companion related it. Ishaq al-Azraq related it from Sa‘id ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Rabi‘ah, in this form. Abu Nu‘aym differed, relating it from Sa‘id, from Ali ibn Rabi‘ah, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah. Al-Bukhari transmitted it in al-Adab from Abu Nu‘aym, and al-Tabarani included it in the biography of al-Mughirah ibn Shu‘bah from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Abu Nu‘aym. It contains the account of lamentation over Qarazah ibn Ka‘b. Muslim and al-Tirmidhi likewise transmitted it through several routes from Sa‘id ibn Ubayd. Ibn Qani‘ transmitted it by way of Ishaq al-Azraq, from al-Tabarani's shaykh, but gave the name as Ka‘b ibn Alqamah, which is an error. Perhaps the error arose from the mention of Qarazah ibn Ka‘b, and the name may have been misread and transposed. والله أعلم.

records.arabic: بن مالك بن عمرو بن عون بن عامر بن ذيبان بن الدئل بن صباح بضم المهملة وتخفيف الموحدة العبدي الصباحي ذكر الرشاطي عن أبي عمرو الشيباني انه كان من فرسان عبد القيس واشرافهم ووفد مع أشج عبد القيس على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم واستدركه بن الأمين
records.english: ibn Mālik ibn ʿAmr ibn Awn ibn Amir ibn Dhibyan ibn al-Du’il ibn Sabah—the last name with a dammah on the unpointed letter and a single ba—al-Abdi al-Sabahi. Al-Rushati related from Abu Amr al-Shaybani that he was one of the horsemen and nobles of Abd al-Qays and came with al-Ashajj Abd al-Qays as a delegate to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Ibn al-Amin added him.

names.arabic: كعب الأعور بن مالك بن عمرو بن عون بن عامر بن ذيبان بن الدئل بن صباح
names.english: Ka‘b al-A‘war ibn Malik ibn Amr ibn Awn ibn Amir ibn Dhibyan ibn al-Du’il ibn Sabah

records.arabic:
بن أبي كعب بن القين بن كعب بن سواد بن غنم بن كعب بن سلمة بكسر اللام بن سعد بن علي بن أسد بن ساردة أبو عبد الله الأنصاري السلمي بفتحتين ويقال أبو بشير ويقال أبو عبد الرحمن قال البغوي حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد حدثني أبي حدثنا هارون عن إسماعيل من ولد كعب بن مالك قال كانت كنية كعب بن مالك في الجاهلية أبا بشير فكناه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبا عبد الله ولم يكن لمالك ولد غير كعب الشاعر المشهور وشهد العقبة وبايع بها وتخلف عن بدر وشهد أحدا وما بعدها وتخلف في تبوك وهو أحد الثلاثة الذين تيب عليهم وقد ساق قصة في ذلك سياقا حسنا وهو في الصحيحين وروى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعن اسيد بن حضير روى عنه أولاده عبد الله وعبد الرحمن وعبيد الله ومعبد ومحمد وابن ابنه عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله وروى عنه أيضا بن عباس وجابر وأبو امامة الباهلي وعمر بن الحكم وعمر بن كثير بن افلح وغيرهم وقال بن سيرين قال كعب بن مالك بيتين كان سبب إسلام دوس وهما
قضينا من تهامة كل وتر
وخيبر ثم اغمدنا السيوفا
تخبرنا ولو نطقت لقالت
قواطعهن دوسا أو ثقيفا فلما بلغ ذلك دوسا قالوا خذوا لانفسكم لا ينزل بكم ما نزل بثقيف قال بن حبان مات أيام قتل علي بن أبي طالب وقال بن أبي حاتم عن أبيه ذهب بصره في خلافة معاوية واقتصر البخاري في ذكر وفاته على انه رثى عثمان ولم نجد له في حرب علي ومعاوية خبرا وقال البغوي بلغني انه مات بالشام في خلافة معاوية وقد اخرج أبو الفرج الأصبهاني في كتاب الاغاني بسند شامي فيه ضعف وانقطاع ان حسان بن ثابت وكعب بن مالك والنعمان بن بشير دخلوا على علي فناظروه في شأن عثمان وانشده كعب شعرا في رثاء عثمان ثم خرجوا من عنده فتوجهوا إلى معاوية فأكرمهم
records.english:
ibn Abī Kaʿb ibn al-Qayn ibn Ka‘b ibn Sawad ibn Ghanm ibn Ka‘b ibn Salimah—with kasrah on the lam—ibn Sa‘d ibn Ali ibn Asad ibn Saridah, Abu Abd Allah al-Ansari al-Sulami—with two open vowels. He is also called Abu Bashir or Abu Abd al-Rahman. Al-Baghawi said: Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us; my father related to me; Harun related to us, from Isma‘il, a descendant of Ka‘b ibn Malik, who said: Ka‘b ibn Malik's kunyah in the pre-Islamic period was Abu Bashir, but the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم gave him the kunyah Abu Abd Allah. Malik had no child other than Ka‘b, the celebrated poet. He witnessed al-Aqabah and pledged allegiance there. He did not take part at Badr, but witnessed Uhud and the campaigns that followed. He stayed behind from Tabuk and was one of the three whose repentance was accepted. He related the account of this in a fine narrative found in both Sahih collections. He related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and from Usayd ibn Hudayr. His sons Abd Allah, Abd al-Rahman, Ubayd Allah, Ma‘bad, and Muhammad related from him, as did his grandson Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah. Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Abu Umamah al-Bahili, Umar ibn al-Hakam, Umar ibn Kathir ibn Aflah, and others also related from him. Ibn Sirin said that Ka‘b ibn Malik composed two verses that caused Daws to embrace Islam:

We settled every blood debt in Tihamah,
and Khaybar too; then we sheathed the swords.
They would tell you, if they could speak,
that their cutting edges promise Daws or Thaqif.

When this reached Daws, they said, “Take measures for yourselves, lest what befell Thaqif befall you.” Ibn Hibban said that he died around the time Ali ibn Abi Talib was killed. Ibn Abi Hatim related from his father that Ka‘b lost his sight during Mu‘awiyah's caliphate. Al-Bukhari, in mentioning his death, said only that he elegized Uthman; we find no report of his participation in the war between Ali and Mu‘awiyah. Al-Baghawi said, “I learned that he died in Syria during Mu‘awiyah's caliphate.” Abu al-Faraj al-Isbahani transmitted in Kitab al-Aghani, with a Syrian chain containing weakness and a break, that Hassan ibn Thabit, Ka‘b ibn Malik, and al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir entered upon Ali and debated with him concerning Uthman. Ka‘b recited poetry elegizing Uthman, then they left him and went to Mu‘awiyah, who honored them.

names.arabic: سعد بن علي بن أسد بن ساردة
names.english: Sa‘d ibn Ali ibn Asad ibn Saridah

records.arabic: البهزي ويقال مرة بن كعب البهزي السلمي بضم المهملة سكن البصرة ثم الأردن وقال بن السكن الأكثر يقولون كعب بن مرة وكذا قال أبو عمر قال البغوي روى أحاديث ثم اخرج من طريق سالم بن أبي الجعد عن شرحبيل بن السمط قال قلت لكعب بن مرة حدثنا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يا كعب قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاء رجل فقال يا رسول الله استسق الله لمضر قال فرفع يديه وقال اللهم اسقنا غيثا مغيثا الحديث وفيه فاتوه فشكوا اليه المطر فقالوا انهدمت البيوت الحديث ويقال هما اثنان الذي سكن البصرة وروى عنه أهلها والذي سكن الشام روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم روى عنه أبو الأشعث الصنعاني وشرحبيل بن السمط ويقال عن سالم بن أبي الجعد ان شرحبيل قال يا كعب بن مرة حدثنا واحذر قال سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول من شاب شيبة في الإسلام كانت له نورا يوم القيامة أخرجه الترمذي بهذا وأورده بن ماجة مطولا وفي بعض طرقه النسائي وفي بعضها كعب بن مرة ولم يشك وكذا عند بن قانع على ثلاثة أوجه لكنه عدده بحسبها
records.english: al-Bahzī, also called Murrah ibn Kaʿb al-Bahzi al-Sulami—with a dammah on the unpointed letter. He lived first in Basra and then in the Jordan district. Ibn al-Sakan said that most authorities call him Ka‘b ibn Murrah; Abu Umar said the same. Al-Baghawi said that he related several hadiths, then transmitted through Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d, from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, who said: I asked Ka‘b ibn Murrah, “Ka‘b, relate to us from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم.” He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم when a man came and said, “Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to send rain to Mudar.” He raised his hands and said, “O Allah, give us rescuing rain,” continuing the hadith. It says that they later came to him and complained of the rain, saying that the houses had collapsed, and so on. It is also said that they were two men: the one who lived in Basra and was related from by its people, and the one who lived in Syria and related from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. Abu al-Ash‘ath al-San‘ani and Shurahbil ibn al-Simt related from the latter. It is related from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja‘d that Shurahbil said, “Ka‘b ibn Murrah, relate to us, and be cautious.” He said: I heard the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “Whoever grows one gray hair in Islam will have it as a light on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Tirmidhi transmitted it with this wording. Ibn Majah gave it at greater length. Some routes in al-Nasa’i have the name Ka‘b ibn Murrah without uncertainty. Ibn Qani‘ likewise transmitted it in three forms, but counted the man separately under each.

records.arabic: بن ضنة بمعجمة ونون ثقيلة بن ربيعة بن قزعة بن عبد الله بن مخزوم بن غالب بن قطيعة بن عبس العبسي بن بنت خالد بن سنان العبسي الذي يقال انه كان نبيا وانما نسب لجده قال بن يونس هو صحابي شهد فتح مصر واختط بها ويقال انه ولى القضاء بها واخرج من طريق الضحاك بن شرحبيل ان عمار بن سعد التجيبي أخبرهم ان عمر بن الخطاب كتب إلى عمرو بن العاص ان يجعل كعب بن ضنة على القضاء فأرسل اليه عمرو فقال كعب لا والله لا ينجيه الله من الجاهلية ثم يعود فيها ابدا بعد إذ نجاه الله منها فتركه عمرو وروى أبو عمر الكندي في قضاة مصر من طريق عبد الرحمن بن السائب بن عيينة بن السائب بن كعب بن ضنة قال قضى جدي بمصر شهرين ثم ورد كتاب عمر بصرفه ومن طريق بن لهيعة عن الحارث بن يزيد ان كعبا ولى القضاء يسيرا حتى اعفاه عمر بن الخطاب
records.english: ibn Ḍannah, with a dotted letter and a doubled nun—ibn Rabi‘ah ibn Qaza‘ah ibn Abd Allah ibn Makhzum ibn Ghalib ibn Qati‘ah ibn Abs al-Absi, the daughter's son of Khalid ibn Sinan al-Absi, who is said to have been a prophet. He was ascribed to his grandfather. Ibn Yunus said: He was a Companion who witnessed the conquest of Egypt and marked out a residence there. It is also said that he was appointed its judge. Ibn Yunus transmitted through al-Dahhak ibn Shurahbil that Ammar ibn Sa‘d al-Tujibi informed them that Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Amr ibn al-As instructing him to appoint Ka‘b ibn Dinnah as judge. Amr sent for him, but Ka‘b said, “No, by Allah. Allah would not deliver him from the pre-Islamic state only for him ever to return to it after Allah had saved him from it.” Amr therefore left him alone. Abu Umar al-Kindi related in Qudat Misr through Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sa’ib ibn Uyaynah ibn al-Sa’ib ibn Ka‘b ibn Dinnah, who said, “My grandfather served as judge in Egypt for two months, after which Umar's letter dismissing him arrived.” He also related through Ibn Lahi‘ah, from al-Harith ibn Yazid, that Ka‘b held the judgeship briefly until Umar ibn al-Khattab excused him.

names.arabic: ربيعة بن قزعة بن عبد الله بن مخزوم بن غالب بن قطيعة بن عبس العبسي
names.english: Rabi‘ah ibn Qaza‘ah ibn Abd Allah ibn Makhzum ibn Ghalib ibn Qati‘ah ibn Abs al-Absi

names.arabic: عبد الرحمن بن السائب بن عيينة بن السائب بن كعب بن ضنة
names.english: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Sa’ib ibn Uyaynah ibn al-Sa’ib ibn Ka‘b ibn Dinnah

records.arabic: رجل من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قطعت يده يوم اليمامة ذكره بن يونس واخرج من طريق عمرو بن الحارث عن بكر بن سوادة ان زياد بن نافع حدثه عن كعب وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قطعت يده يوم اليمامة ان صلاة الخوف بكل طائفة ركعة وسجدتان اظن في إسناده انقطاعا فقد علقه البخاري من طريق زياد بن نافع عن أبي موسى الغافقي عن جابر بن عبد الله وقال البخاري في التاريخ كعب قطعت يده يوم غزوة اليمامة له صحبة روى عنه زياد بن نافع
records.english: A man among the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم whose hand was severed on the day of al-Yamamah. Ibn Yunus mentioned him and transmitted through Amr ibn al-Harith, from Bakr ibn Sawadah, that Ziyad ibn Nafi‘ related to him from Ka‘b—who was one of the Companions of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and whose hand was severed on the day of al-Yamamah—that the fear prayer consists of one bowing cycle and two prostrations for each group. I think there is a break in its chain. Al-Bukhari cited it without a full chain by way of Ziyad ibn Nafi‘, from Abu Musa al-Ghafiqi, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah. Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: “Ka‘b, whose hand was severed on the expedition of al-Yamamah, had companionship. Ziyad ibn Nafi‘ related from him.”

records.arabic: ذكر بن منده من طريق عبد ربه بن عطاء عن بن القري قال كنت جالس عند علقمة بن نضلة فقال أخبرني كعب ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ما من أمير عشرة الا يؤتى به يوم القيامة مغلولا حتى يكون الله يرحمه أو يقضي فيه غير ذلك
records.english: Ibn Mandah mentioned him through ʿAbd Rabbih ibn ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn al-Qari, who said: I was sitting with Alqamah ibn Nadlah when he said, “Ka‘b informed me that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم said: No commander over ten people will fail to be brought on the Day of Resurrection in shackles, until either Allah's mercy releases him or He passes some other judgment concerning him.”

records.arabic:
بن الاسكر الجندعي تقدم ذكره في ترجمة والده ونقل أبو موسى عن عبد الله انه سمى جده الأشكر بمعجمة وقيل بمهملة وزيادة نون ذاك تصحيف واضح ونقل المستغفري عن البردعي عن البخاري انه سمع من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ويكنى أبا هارون وقال أبو حاتم السجستاني في كتاب المعمرين نزل البصرة واليه تنسب مربعة كلاب واخرج بن قانع من طريق خليد بن دعلج عن سعيد بن عبد الرحمن عن كلاب بن أمية سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول ان الله يغفر لمن استغفر الا لبغى بفرجها والعشار وفي هذا السند ضعف وقد أخرجه بن عساكر من الوجه الذي أخرجه منه بن قانع فقال فيه فقال له عثمان بن أبي العاص ما جاء بك قال استعملت على العشور بالأبلة فقال اني سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد تقدم في ترجمة أمية بن الاسكر أيضا ان كلاب بن أمية روى هذا الحديث عن عثمان بن أبي العاص وكذا ذكر الحاكم أبو أحمد ان كلابا روى عن عثمان واخرج أيضا من طريق علي بن زيد بن جدعان عن الحسن قال بعث زياد كلاب بن أمية الليثي على الأبلة فمر به عثمان بن أبي العاص فقال يا أبا هارون فذكر الحديث ولم يسقه أبو أحمد وهو عند أحمد وأبي يعلى من هذا الوجه وتمامه ما يجلسك ها هنا فذكر له فقال المكس من بين عمله فقال الا أحدثك حديثا سمعته من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ان داود كان يوقظ أهله في ساعة من الليل يقول يا آل داود قوموا فصلوا فان هذه الساعة يستجاب فيها الا لساحر أو عشار قال فدعا أمية بسفينة فركبها ثم رجع إلى زياد فقال ابعث على عملك من شئت وذكر صاحب التاريخ المظفري ان كلاب بن أمية هاجر إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال أبوه شعرا يتشوق اليه فامره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ببر أبيه ويقال ان عمر لما سمع أبيات أمية التي أولها
لمن شيخان قد شدوا كلابا
رق لامية وأورد كلابا فنهشته افعى فمات وقد تقدم في ترجمة أبيه ان كلابا كان في زمن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجلا وقيل ان كلابا لما أبطأ على أبيه اهتر أبوه أي خرف فاقدمه عمر فقدم قبل ان يعرف به أمية فامره عمر بحلب ناقة وان يسقيها أمية فلما شرب قال اني لاشم رائحة يدي كلاب فبكى عمر فقال هذا كلاب فضمه إليك
records.english:
Ibn al-Askar al-Jundaʿī. He has been mentioned in his father's biography. Abu Musa transmitted from Abd Allah that he called his grandfather al-Ashkar, with a pointed letter. The reading with an unpointed letter and an added nun is an obvious scribal error. Al-Mustaghfiri transmitted from al-Barda‘i, from al-Bukhari, that Kilab heard from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and had the kunyah Abu Harun. Abu Hatim al-Sijistani said in Kitab al-Mu‘ammarin that he settled in Basra and that Kilab Square was named after him. Ibn Qani‘ transmitted through Khulayd ibn Da‘laj, from Sa‘id ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Kilab ibn Umayyah: I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم say, “Allah forgives whoever seeks forgiveness, except an unchaste woman plying her sex and a tithe collector.” This chain is weak. Ibn Asakir transmitted it through the same route used by Ibn Qani‘ but included: Uthman ibn Abi al-As asked him, “What brought you here?” He replied, “I was appointed over the levies at al-Ubullah.” Uthman then said, “I heard the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم …” It has already appeared in the biography of Umayyah ibn al-Askar that Kilab ibn Umayyah related this hadith from Uthman ibn Abi al-As. Abu Ahmad al-Hakim likewise stated that Kilab related from Uthman. He also transmitted through Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud‘an, from al-Hasan, who said: Ziyad appointed Kilab ibn Umayyah al-Laythi over al-Ubullah. Uthman ibn Abi al-As passed him and said, “Abu Harun …” then mentioned the hadith, though Abu Ahmad did not give its full text. Ahmad and Abu Ya‘la have it through this route. Its continuation is: “What keeps you sitting here?” Kilab told him. Uthman said, “The illicit levy is among the worst of occupations. Shall I not relate to you a hadith I heard from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم? David used to wake his household at an hour of the night and say, ‘House of David, rise and pray, for at this hour prayers are answered—except the prayer of a sorcerer or a tithe collector.’” The report then has a damaged clause naming Umayyah in connection with calling for a boat and boarding it; it does not securely identify the actor. The traveler then returned to Ziyad and said, “Send whomever you wish to perform your work.” The author of al-Tarikh al-Muzaffari mentioned that Kilab ibn Umayyah emigrated to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. His father composed poetry longing for him, so the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم instructed him to honor his father. It is related that when Umar heard Umayyah's verses beginning:

For whom are two old people who have held Kilab fast …

he felt compassion for Umayyah and summoned Kilab. A snake then bit Kilab and he died. It has already appeared in his father's biography that Kilab was a grown man in the time of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم. It is also related that, when Kilab remained away too long, his father became senile. Umar had him brought back. He arrived before Umayyah knew of his presence. Umar instructed Kilab to milk a she-camel and give the milk to Umayyah. When Umayyah drank, he said, “I can smell the scent of Kilab's hand.” Umar wept and said, “This is Kilab; embrace him.”

names.arabic: كلاب بن أمية بن الاسكر الجندعي
names.english: Kilab ibn Umayyah ibn al-Askar al-Junda‘i

records.arabic: يأتي في كليب
records.english: He appears under Kulayb.

records.arabic: مولى العباس بن عبد المطلب ذكر بن سعد واخرج بسند فيه الواقدي عن أبي هريرة قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم الجمعة يخطب إلى جذع في المسجد قائما فقال ان القيام قد شق على فقال له تميم الداري الا اعمل لك منبرا كما رأيت يصنع بالشام فشاور النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المسلمين في ذلك فرأوا ان يتخذه فقال العباس بن عبد المطلب ان لي غلاما يقال له كلاب اعمل الناس فقال مره أن يعمله فأرسله إلى أثلة بالغابة فقطعها وعمل منها درجتين مقعدا ثم جاء فوضعه في موضعه اليوم فقام عليه وقال منبري على ترعة من ترع الجنة
records.english: A client of al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib. Ibn Sa‘d mentioned him and transmitted with a chain containing al-Waqidi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: On Fridays the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم used to deliver the sermon standing beside a palm trunk in the mosque. He said, “Standing has become burdensome for me.” Tamim al-Dari asked him, “Shall I make you a pulpit like those I have seen made in Syria?” The Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم consulted the Muslims, and they approved making it. Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib said, “I have a slave named Kilab, the most skilled of people.” He said, “Tell him to make it.” Al-Abbas sent him to a tamarisk tree at al-Ghabah. He cut it down and made from it two steps and a seat. He then brought it and placed it where it stands today. He stood upon it and said, “My pulpit stands over one of the channels of Paradise.”

records.arabic: هو ذئيب بن شعثم كان يسمى بذلك فغيره النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد تقدم في ذؤيب
records.english: He is Dhuʾayb ibn Shaʿtham and used to be called by this name, but the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم changed it. He has appeared above under Dhu’ayb.

records.english: Abū Rahm al-Ghifārī. He is famous by his kunyah and will appear in the section on kunyahs. Al-Bukhari said that he had companionship.

records.arabic: بن خالد بن وهب بن ثعلبة بن واثلة بن عمرو بن شيبان بن محارب بن فهر القرشي الفهري أخو الضحاك بن قيس وهو الأكبر ذكره الزبير بن بكار وقال ولى ولده سويد إمرة دمشق
records.english: Ibn Khālid ibn Wahb ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Wathilah ibn Amr ibn Shayban ibn Muharib ibn Fihr al-Qurashi al-Fihri, brother of al-Dahhak ibn Qays and the elder of the two. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned him and said that his son Suwayd governed Damascus.

names.arabic: كلثوم بن قيس بن خالد بن وهب بن ثعلبة بن واثلة بن عمرو بن شيبان بن محارب بن فهر القرشي الفهري
names.english: Kulthum ibn Qays ibn Khalid ibn Wahb ibn Tha‘labah ibn Wathilah ibn Amr ibn Shayban ibn Muharib ibn Fihr al-Qurashi al-Fihri

records.arabic: بكسر الهاء وسكون الدال بن امرئ القيس بن الحارث بن زيد بن عبيد بن زيد بن مالك بن عوف بن مالك بن الأوس الأنصاري الأوسي ذكر موسى بن عقبة وغيره من أهل المغازي ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نزل عليه بقباء أول ما قدم المدينة وقال بعضهم نزل على سعد بن خيثمة وقال الواقدي كان نزوله على كلثوم وكان يتحدث في بيت سعد بن خيثمة لان منزله كان منزل العرب وذكر الطبري وابن قتيبة أنه أول من مات من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة ثم مات بعده اسعد بن زرارة وله ذكر في ترجمة غلامه نجيح
records.english: With kasrah on the hāʾ and sukūn on the dāl—ibn Imri’ al-Qays ibn al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Ubayd ibn Zayd ibn Malik ibn Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws al-Ansari al-Awsi. Musa ibn Uqbah and other authorities on the campaigns mentioned that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم stayed with him in Quba’ when he first arrived in Medina. Some said that he stayed with Sa‘d ibn Khaythamah. Al-Waqidi said that he lodged with Kulthum but would converse with people in Sa‘d ibn Khaythamah's house, because Sa‘d's home was where the Arabs gathered. Al-Tabari and Ibn Qutaybah stated that he was the first of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم to die in Medina. As‘ad ibn Zurarah died after him. He is mentioned in the biography of his servant Najih.

names.arabic: القيس بن الحارث بن زيد بن عبيد بن زيد بن مالك بن عوف بن مالك بن الأوس الأنصاري الأوسي
names.english: al-Qays ibn al-Harith ibn Zayd ibn Ubayd ibn Zayd ibn Malik ibn Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws al-Ansari al-Awsi

records.arabic: ذكره مطين في الوحدان وروى هو وابن ماجة من طريق جامع بن شداد عن كلثوم الخزاعي قال اتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل فقال يا رسول الله كيف لي إذا أحسنت ان اعلم اني أحسنت الحديث وكذا هو في مسند أبي بكر بن أبي شيبة ولم يسم أبوه عند واحد منهم وقال المزي في الأطراف كلثوم بن المصطلق مختلف في صحبته فذكر حديث بن ماجة وقال قبل ذلك في مسند بن مسعود كلثوم بن المصطلق وله صحبة عن بن مسعود فذكر حديثا من رواية الزبير بن عدي عنه عن بن مسعود ويقال انه نسب إلى جده الأعلى وانه كلثوم بن علقمة بن ناجية بن الحارث بن المصطلق وعلى هذا فهو تابعي وقيل هو كلثوم بن عامر بن الحارث بن أبي ضرار بن المصطلق بن أخي جويرية أم المؤمنين وله رواية عن جويرية وهو تابعي أيضا ذكره البخاري وابن أبي حاتم وابن حبان في التابعين ومقتضى صنيع بن أبي شيبة ومطين انه كلثوم آخر وكذا فرق بينهما البخاري
records.english: Muṭayyan mentioned him in al-Wuḥdān. He and Ibn Majah related through Jami‘ ibn Shaddad, from Kulthum al-Khuza‘i, who said: A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم and asked, “Messenger of Allah, when I do good, how can I know that I have done good?” and continued the hadith. The same appears in the Musnad of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah. None of them named his father. Al-Mizzi said in al-Atraf: “Kulthum ibn al-Mustaliq—there is disagreement as to whether he had companionship.” He then cited Ibn Majah's hadith. Before that, under the Musnad of Ibn Mas‘ud, he said: “Kulthum ibn al-Mustaliq, who had companionship, from Ibn Mas‘ud,” and cited a hadith related by al-Zubayr ibn Adi, from him, from Ibn Mas‘ud. It is said that he was ascribed to a remote ancestor and was Kulthum ibn Alqamah ibn Najiyah ibn al-Harith ibn al-Mustaliq. On this view he was a Successor. It is also said that he was Kulthum ibn Amir ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar ibn al-Mustaliq, a nephew of Juwayriyyah, Mother of the Believers. He related from Juwayriyyah and was also a Successor. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the Successors. The arrangement of Ibn Abi Shaybah and Mutayyan requires this Kulthum to be another man, and al-Bukhari likewise distinguished between the two.

names.arabic: كلثوم بن علقمة بن ناجية بن الحارث بن المصطلق
names.english: Kulthum ibn Alqamah ibn Najiyah ibn al-Harith ibn al-Mustaliq

names.arabic: كلثوم بن عامر بن الحارث بن أبي ضرار بن المصطلق
names.english: Kulthum ibn Amir ibn al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar ibn al-Mustaliq

records.arabic: ويقال بن عبد الله بن الحنبل وعند بن قانع كلدة بن قيس بن حنبل الأسلمي ويقال الغساني حليف بني جمح وهو أخو صفوان بن أمية لامه ويقال بن أخيه وقال بن الكلبي كان هو وأخوه عبد الرحمن بن حنبل ممن سقط من اليمن إلى مكة وقال بن إسحاق هو الذي قال يوم حنين لما شهدها مع أخيه صفوان ووقعت هزيمة المسلمين بطل السحر فزجره صفوان في قصة مشهورة ثم اسلم كلدة بعد ذلك واقام بمكة صفوان قال البخاري وله صحبة وقال بن الكلبي كان مولى لعمر بن حبيب الجمحي ثم انتسب في بني جمح فقيل بن حنبل بن مالك ويقال مليك بن عاتقة بن محمد بن كلدة انتهى وقد اخرج أصحاب السنن الثلاثة من طريق بن جريج أخبرني عمرو بن أبي سفيان ان عمرو بن عبد الله بن صفوان أخبره عن كلدة بن الحنبل ان صفوان بن أمية بعثه إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بلبن وجداية وضغابيس والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأعلى مكة قال فدخلت فلم اسلم قال ارجع فقل السلام عليكم وذلك بعدما اسلم صفوان قال عمرو فأخبرني صفوان بهذا عن كلدة بن الحنبل ولم يقل سمعته منه لفظ أبي داود في رواية يحيى بن حبيب عنده أمية بن صفوان وفيه ان كلدة بن الحنبل أخبره وقال الترمذي حسن غريب لا نعرفه الا من حديث بن جريج
records.english: He is also said to be ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥanbal, while Ibn Qani‘ gives Kaldah ibn Qays ibn Hanbal al-Aslami. He is also called al-Ghassani, an ally of Banu Jumah. He was Safwan ibn Umayyah's maternal brother, though he is also said to have been his brother's son. Ibn al-Kalbi said that he and his brother Abd al-Rahman ibn Hanbal were among those who came down from Yemen to Mecca. Ibn Ishaq said that, on the day of Hunayn, which he witnessed with his brother Safwan, he said when the Muslims were routed, “The sorcery has failed.” Safwan rebuked him in a well-known account. Kaldah later embraced Islam and remained with Safwan in Mecca. Al-Bukhari said that he had companionship. Ibn al-Kalbi said: He had been a client of Umar ibn Habib al-Jumahi, then affiliated himself with Banu Jumah and was called Ibn Hanbal ibn Malik. It is also said: Mulayk ibn Atikah ibn Muhammad ibn Kaldah. End quote. The compilers of the three Sunan transmitted through Ibn Jurayj: Amr ibn Abi Sufyan informed me that Amr ibn Abd Allah ibn Safwan informed him, from Kaldah ibn al-Hanbal, that Safwan ibn Umayyah sent him to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وسلم with milk, a young gazelle, and tender shoots, while the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم was in upper Mecca. Kaldah said: I entered without offering the greeting of peace. He told me, “Go back and say, ‘Peace be upon you.’” This occurred after Safwan had embraced Islam. Amr said, “Safwan related this to me from Kaldah ibn al-Hanbal,” without saying that he had heard it directly from him. In Yahya ibn Habib's version in Abu Dawud, the name is Umayyah ibn Safwan, and it states that Kaldah ibn al-Hanbal informed him. Al-Tirmidhi said: “It is fair but uncommon; we know it only through Ibn Jurayj.”

records.english: Al-Aṣbaḥī. Ibn Ḥibbān said that he is reported to have had companionship. This is how I read it in the handwriting of al-Sadr al-Bakri. It is possible that he was Abrahah's brother. The man commonly known is Kurayb, as noted above.

records.english: Ibn Shāhīn said: I heard Ibn Abi Dawud say, “He witnessed Uhud and was Khalid's brother.”

records.arabic: بن عمرو بن خديج بن عامر بن جشم بن الحارث بن الخزرج قال العدوي وابن سعد والطبري شهد أحدا وهو أخو حبيب بن إساف ويقال فيه وفي الذي قبله بن يساف بتحتانية بدل الهمزة
records.english: Ibn ʿAmr ibn Khudayj ibn Amir ibn Jusham ibn al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj. Al-Adawi, Ibn Sa‘d, and al-Tabari said that he witnessed Uhud. He was the brother of Habib ibn Isaf. His name and that of the preceding man are also given as Ibn Yasaf, with ya instead of the hamzah.

names.arabic: كليب بن إساف بن عبيد بن عمرو بن خديج بن عامر بن جشم بن الحارث بن الخزرج
names.english: Kulayb ibn Isaf ibn Ubayd ibn Amr ibn Khadij ibn Amir ibn Jusham ibn al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj
